## Entry J-579 — Address book §4–§7 locked: F1∪F2 fill, V2 freshness, E1+E2+E3 erasure, own file — and D-088 corrected §6 mid-session

**Date:** 2026-07-24 · **Seats:** Joe (locked all four; the ordering; the reserved appearance/architecture surfaces) · Chat (Leg A measurement, D-088 grounding, records). **ZERO code. ZERO `skin.css`.**

**WHAT SHIPPED.** `tasks/M_RP_ADDRESS_BOOK.md` **v1.2** — the four Phase-0 locks written in. `DECISIONS.md` **D-126** (humane pubkey label, adopted, non-protocol, no runbook). Milestone still ACTIVE (build not begun); Phase-0 decisions closed.

**LEG A — MEASURED at `7ab743e`, ANSWER: NO node→client revocation-push path exists.** Positive control: 254 source `.rs`, 792 `pub fn` (`target/` + `.claude/worktrees/` excluded). A live push channel *does* exist — the home-Node WS `Inbound::Event` fan-out — but **it cannot carry identity**: the whole DAG event space is `message.*` / `state.*` / `space.join_request`, with **no `identity.*` event type**; identity is control-layer only. Revocation *is* modelled (`IdentityRecord.revoked`/`revoked_at`) and propagates **node↔node** via `identity.replicate` (spec 3.13.4) — **replicas are pushed, clients are not**. Client identity access is pull-only (`identity.get`→`identity.record`). `xgen-client` has one revocation grep hit and it is an unrelated AI-delegation CLI arg. ⇒ **V3 is a protocol addition, unavailable this arc**; §5 chooses V1 vs V2 only.

**THE FOUR LOCKS (Joe, 2026-07-24):**
- **§4 FILL — F1 ∪ F2, F3 refused.** Author-on-sight ∪ Space-membership sweep. F3 (registry pull) refused on **spec** grounds — Ch2 §Cross-Space Discoverability forbids a global membership index — not weighed on cost.
- **§5 FRESHNESS — V2 refresh-on-encounter.** Take the higher `update_version`. Firmed by Leg A (V3 unavailable) and by D-088 (re-encounter is the only path back to a fresh record). V1's revoked-renders-as-valid trust defect bought off for one integer compare.
- **§6 ERASURE — E1 + E2 + E3.** All three. E3 (eviction of records unseen for *N*) is the client-side arm of the spec's own **TTL-expiry** cache-erasure mechanism (Appendix D §3.3), not a nice-to-have. ⚠️ **N is the one open parameter, Joe's**, needed before Leg C exercises eviction.
- **§7 STORAGE — its own file.** Delete-the-file = clean verifiable E1; keeps other people's identity PII out of the client's own state.

⚠️ **N-164 CAUGHT LIVE, AND OWNED.** §6's first recommendation ("E1+E2, E3 deferred") was written **without D-088**, a standing decision from 2026-06-04. Joe's informational question about erasure ("some data stay… for owner of occasional events") sent Chat to the docs; the read surfaced D-088; the recommendation was **corrected to include E3** — the change came from documentation, not from any instruction to alter it. *Recommending before grounding fully against the spec is exactly the trap; the pointer paid a third time.*

📌 **D-088 restated for the record.** XGen identity erasure = **orphaning the pubkey↔person binding**: PII removed, pubkey persists as an anonymous token, every signature keeps verifying, **no Event touched** (`Event.sender` is inside the signed payload, `xgen-common/src/wire.rs:482`). The address book is that binding **one hop past the spec** — a client cache of it — so a cache-forever book would be a client PII store surviving upstream Art.17 erasure indefinitely. E1+E2+E3 bound the local exposure; the **upstream-propagation collision** (does the local book ever *learn* of an upstream erasure? only via `identity.not_found` on V2's re-fetch — no push) stays **handed over unresolved per D-121**, not traded away.

📌 **D-126 — humane pubkey label (side thread, adopted).** A pure deterministic render of an XGID for convenience listings (e.g. statistics) where full 65-char XGIDs are heavy and precision is not needed — *"not profound but sufficient distinguishing."* Two families: tail-truncation (N=8, cheapest, already the `app.rs` pattern) and word-rendering (SHA-256 → 11-bit chunks → 2048-word list → `amber-falcon`). ⚠️ **Label, never identifier** — not typeable/searchable/trust-bearing, full XGID always reachable (PGP short-key-ID lesson). Canonical-vs-cosmetic and wordlist language left open, Joe's. No code, no protocol surface.

**NEXT.** Leg C — Chat specifies the seed corpus from the locked policy and writes the `--batch` set (blocked only on Joe supplying **N**), then Leg D — Clair builds from a runbook. **M-RP-MEMBERS** unblocks at the members-widget step of the agreed order, after populate + book build.

Ch2 ASSIGNS S a home** — the *Space membership record*. ⇒ **S is SPECIFIED-BUT-UNBUILT, not unimagined.** *The measurement was right; the word libelled an architecture that had already answered.* ⇒ **`M-RP-INBOUND-NAME` is materially larger than filed** — the four-layer chain with the address book as the Private Identity record **plus the resolver that walks it**, not a flat XGID→name lookup.

## Entry J-576 — The self widget design walk: "customisable" was three features, one of them a protocol operation — and the row defect was filed against the wrong widget

**Date:** 2026-07-23 · **Seats:** Joe (taxonomy, scope rulings, naming, the deferral) · Chat (grounding, measurement, records). **ZERO code. ZERO `skin.css`. The diff is `.md` only.**

**WHY THE MILESTONE WAS REDIRECTED BEFORE IT OPENED.** `M-RP-SELF-SURFACE` was scoped as *"land the Self name + styling"*. Joe opened the session with the reason: *"it is special widget that can be the gate to the whole user identity's setting."* ⇒ **that scope was too small** — if the self region is the entry point to identity settings, then **what it IS** decides what it shows and what it opens, and the name and styling are **consequences, not the subject**.

**🔑 THE GROUNDING FINDING THAT MADE IT A PROTOCOL QUESTION.** Lock #5's fix carries *"customisable later"*, which had been read as a UI affordance. It is not. `identity.update` is a **real, signed, versioned wire message** — `xgen-core/src/identity/registration.rs`: `update_version`, `changes`, signature-verified, `is_ai` immutable (3041), `display_name` validated (≤128, non-empty, no control chars) and **replicating**. ⚠️ **And the client cannot emit it:** `xgen-client/src/ops.rs` L392/404 set `display_name` at **registration only**, and `xgen-client` holds **zero** references to `sign_update` — every "rename" hit in the client is a **room** rename. *A phrase in a lock was carrying a protocol operation nobody had costed.*

**🔒 D-124 — ONE WORD WAS CARRYING THREE FEATURES.** Joe fixed the vocabulary: **L** local override (you rename someone else; only you see it — **zero lines exist**) · **S** per-space name (⚠️ **impossible today** — `SpaceMember` is `identity_id · role · joined_at · invited_by`, **no name field at all**) · **G** global name (= `identity.update`). 🔑 **The axis is SCOPE — nobody · one space · everywhere — not "local vs replicated".** L is not a cheap G: **it points at a DIFFERENT PERSON.** And **erasure difficulty scales with scope**, which is the GDPR gradient. *The D-122 shape at the identity layer.*

**🔒 AND "SELF" TURNED OUT NOT TO BE A LABEL.** Joe: *"self will be optional … merge names in display to Self or stay various by the wish."* ⇒ it is a **TOGGLE** — ON (default) merges all your **own** names to *"Self"* **in your own view**; OFF shows your actual name. 🔒 **ONE GLOBAL PREFERENCE, not per-space** — *"globally is correct. if for all spaces, one could loose his mind."* 🔑 **The joke is the rationale:** the toggle exists to REDUCE the load of tracking your own names, so a per-space version would reinvent the problem it solves. ⇒ **it is L pointed at yourself: a VIEW PREFERENCE, ZERO wire, no migration gate.** **Therefore lock #5 lands WITHOUT resolving how G is edited** — that fork is later. Preference home: **per-device**, on `uiStateStore`, which already persists `session.layout`.

**🔑 JOE'S CORRECTION, AND IT WAS RIGHT.** Chat filed the 65-char-XGID row defect as *"one thing that should NOT be deferred"* — **under the self widget**. Joe: *"how this relates to the self widget? it relates to the messages widget, doesnt it?"* **It does.** ⚠️ **And the correction went further than the challenge.** Measured: `stream/derive.ts:80` (**inbound**) and `stream-panel.svelte:115` (**own echo**) both carry the declared marker *"NO name (C-8)"* ⇒ **no row of ANY kind can render a name — the stream has no name-resolution layer at all.** 🔑 **And that is precisely why the self panel is fine:** it never reads the message plane; it reads `selfState.identity.display_name` off a **Tauri `get_self_state` invoke**. ⇒ §6's *"same identity, two surfaces, two answers"* now has its mechanical cause: **TWO SOURCES, NOT TWO BUGS.** *A finding filed against the wrong subject reads as true and routes the work to the wrong milestone.*

**⇒ THE MILESTONE SPLIT IN TWO, AND NEITHER HALF IS THE SELF WIDGET.** `M-RP-OWN-ROW-NAME` (own rows resolve the self display name + the toggle; **codeable now**, closes lock #5, zero `self-panel.svelte` edits) and `M-RP-INBOUND-NAME` (XGID→name for **other people** — ⚠️ **blocked**, because that resolution exists nowhere in the client; **it is the address book showing through its own absence**). 🔑 *It also explains J-575's recorded limit from a second direction: "there were NO inbound names on screen" was not only a fixture accident — inbound names cannot render at all yet.*

**THE REFERENCE, AND THE FOUR THINGS IN IT.** Joe supplied a Discord self-panel shot, explicitly *"i dont mean to copy it"*. ⚠️ It holds **four different kinds of thing at four different stages**: avatar+name **shipped** (with `entity-avatar`'s `image?` **reserved and never fed**) · the **status line = Track A**, whose own Phase-0 doc `docs/xgen-status-gap-phase0.md` v1.0 cites *"per the Discord reference shot"* — **the SAME reference, from 2026-07-05** — protocol closed at PROTO-STATUS.2 (J-461) with **no client read path** · settings **cheapest door** · address book **parts built, destination absent** · mic/headphones **not identity at all**. 🔑 *The reference had already been used once in this repo and nobody connected the two.*

**🔒 D-125 — "ALL AS JUST BUTTONS?" IS NO, AND ALL FOUR KINDS ARE ALREADY SHIPPED.** `button`(64) · `toggle`(36) · `status-indicator`(73)/`led`(58) · `menu`(283), every one `use:envelope`-registered. ⚠️ **The reason the distinction is not cosmetic is user-visible (D-121 ①):** a toggle authored as a button loses its on/off affordance, and an indicator authored as a button **invites a click that does nothing** — on the one surface that represents the person to themselves. **Nothing new enters `core`;** the row is a widget-tier composition. Joe named it: *"utilities -> utility buttons for button forms"*.

**⚠️ THE THIRD VOCABULARY COLLISION — AND THE FIRST ONE CAUGHT BEFORE IT LANDED.** Chat wrote *"panel-card collapse"*. Joe: *"what really means 'collapse' in this case? hope is not to close or diminish the self widget."* **He was not misreading — his was the more literal reading:** `collapsed` is a **persisted layout schema field on leaves including `widgetId:'self'`**, migrated twice (`layout-default.ts:91`, v1/v2 boolean → v3 FoldAxis via `migrateLayout`; `foldLeaf`/`handleFold`). 🔑 `window` (D-122) and `self` were both caught **after** entering records; **this one was caught before.** Fixed term: **`merge`** — Joe's own word from his own ruling.

**🔒 THE DEFERRAL, AND THE LINE DRAWN THROUGH IT.** Joe: *"we can define its more final face now, record it and that is all. the implementation we defer till more mechanics will be in the place."* **Agreed — with one carve-out that is not a hedge.** ⚠️ **A "final face" recorded today would be a `[👁️ PERCEPTION]` verdict taken with nothing on screen**, and D-122 says those cannot be made from records at all — *you cannot look at a document*, with J-570 as the receipt. ⇒ `tasks/M_RP_SELF_GATE.md` records **structure, taxonomy and reasoning as settled**, and carries a **mandatory RE-OPEN-ON-BUILD clause** for layout, geometry, display form and arrangement. 🔑 **The reasoning is inherited; the conclusions are re-judged in front of the real screen.** Joe set the lock point himself: *"locked will be on the round-0 before implementation"* ⇒ recorded as **Phase-0**, D-071's canonical term, so it greps.

**🔒 AND THE GATE COSTS NOTHING TO DEFER, BECAUSE IT TOUCHES NOTHING.** Joe: *"self widget stays as is in the same format, just region we be created again for new"* and *"we dont need to make edits on its regard"* ⇒ **the utilities strip is a NEW region; `self-panel.svelte` is untouched.** Two open questions close by consequence: the **connection light stays** and the **selection-bus writer is preserved** (`self-panel.svelte:78`, D5's FIRST WRITER) — **by construction, not by decision.**

**⚠️ TWO PROBES FAILED SILENTLY IN ONE SESSION, BOTH N-156 SHAPED — see N-163.** A line-ending audit returned **`CRLF=0 LF=0` for five files** (PowerShell's `cd` does not move .NET's working directory, so `ReadAllBytes` on a relative path threw into a suppressed error and the counter loop simply never ran). An encoding probe then wrote a **zero-byte file** rather than erroring, because `[char]0x1F512` cannot hold an astral code point in PS 5.1 and `WriteAllText` received `$null`. 🔑 **Both produced a plausible-looking result rather than a failure.** The write path was only trusted after a **differential** check: literal `—⇒🔒🟡⚠️ž ý` written, read back as bytes, and compared **against a `ConvertFromUtf32`-constructed reference** — N-161's general form applied to encoding instead of type.

**⚠️ `Filesystem:*` MCP FAILED EVERY CALL FOR A THIRD SESSION**, including `get_file_info`. `Windows-MCP:PowerShell` was the fallback throughout — **flagged, not silently substituted.**

**📌 FILED, NOT FIXED.** ① ⚠️ **`DECISIONS.md` carries a SHORT header** (Status · Last updated · Author · Credits) — **no Version, Date, Language or License**, against the standing header rule. `Last updated` was bumped; **the missing fields were NOT added** — editing a file's header convention without a ruling is not Chat's call. ⇒ candidate for a header pass. ② The region model for the gate — **dock tile or chrome** — is unresolved and structural (`self` is currently one leaf among eight in `layout-default.ts`). ③ Whether the utilities row is **fixed or plugin-extensible** is **FILED INTENT**, locking at Phase-0; extensible makes it a **plugin surface under D-112/D-113**.

**New `D`:** **D-124**, **D-125**. **New `N`:** **N-163**. **No new `core` component.** Records: this entry · `DECISIONS.md` · `tasks/M_RP_SELF_GATE.md` v0.1 PENDING · `docs/ROADMAP.md` · `CLAUDE.md` PLAY · `ui/docs/xgen-ui-notes.md` N-163. **NEXT — Joe's call:** `M-RP-OWN-ROW-NAME` is the only codeable item and closes lock #5; everything else waits on the address book.

## Entry J-575 — M-RP-SELF-VARIANTS: the perception test re-run against real faces, and the verdict that repaired a legibility floor nobody was measuring

**Date:** 2026-07-23 · **Seats:** Joe (scope rulings, the verdict) · Chat (controls, drive, records). **Zero code. Zero `skin.css` edit.** Every styling change applied at **runtime via CDP** and dies on reload.

**WHY IT WAS RE-RUN.** J-570 found that the three *"Self"* typeface variants Joe had judged were **all fallback fonts** — no mono face was declared, and the italic was a **skewed Regular**. ***A [👁️ PERCEPTION] verdict is only as good as whether the thing looked at WAS THE SUBJECT.*** 🔑 **A distinction the original filing missed: variant 1 was never corrupted** — *"system mono"* **is** `ui-monospace`, so it rendered exactly what it claimed. What was invalid was **the comparison**, not each reading: choosing among three when two are impostors is not a choice anyone made.

**🔒 JOE'S SCOPE RULINGS, WHICH REDIRECTED THE MILESTONE BEFORE IT RAN.** Typeface is **not** the only axis — the first test is **CSS styling only** (bold / italic / letter-spacing), with a mono family change held in reserve. **Name only**, not the row. And the distinction applies **everywhere, not only where avatars gather**: in the thread it is merely *the only* change, because the avatar's side already carries the rest. ⚠️ Chat had proposed judging in the message row as a **compromise** surface; Joe's reasoning made it a **legitimate** one, which is a better answer than either option offered.

**🔑 AND A RULING ABOUT HOW QUESTIONS ARE PUT.** Joe: *"as for a human, i cannot imagine font weight from number."* ⇒ **weights are presented in words; numbers live only in records.** ⚠️ `semibold` is **not** a CSS keyword — only `normal` and `bold` are absolute — so the in-between weight can only be written as a number, and that is a records problem, not a judging one. ***A question whose answer he cannot perceive is not a perception question.***

**THE CONTROL WAS THE MILESTONE'S REAL CONTENT.** ⚠️ `getComputedStyle().fontFamily` returns **the declared stack, not the resolved face** — the most likely route by which variant 2 passed as JetBrains Mono last time (**N-156**: a probe returning the wrong thing confidently is a hole shaped like a result). ⚠️ And a browser **fakes italic by skewing the Regular**, so a skew and a true italic both render plausibly. ⇒ **`font-synthesis: none` + advance-width measurement + a deliberately bogus family as the negative reference**, all after a forced `document.fonts.load()`. **Results:** real family **133.04** vs bogus **118.80** ⇒ resolves · italic **133.68 ≠ 133.04** ⇒ **a TRUE italic, not last session's skew** · italic-700 **138.19 ≠ 137.40** ⇒ true bold italic · **600 → 135.95 with NO static file on disk** ⇒ **the variable weight axis is real, not assumed.**

**FIXTURE, STATED SO IT IS NOT MISTAKEN FOR THE FIX.** No node (`RECONNECTING`) and both seeded rooms empty (`emptyState: "no-messages"`), so the own row came from **an actual send** — a real local echo, `isOwn: true`, rendering lock #5's defect live at **`nameLen: 65`**. Its text was set to `"Self"` at runtime; V1–V3 were **DOM clones** of that real row, removed afterwards.

**🔒 VERDICT — JOE, 2026-07-23, verbatim: *"v3 + 90% grey colour (90% white in grey)"*, confirmed as applied.** Chosen values for `M-RP-SELF-SURFACE`: **`font-weight: 600` · `font-style: italic` · `letter-spacing: 0.05em` · `color: #E5E5E5`**, and ⚠️ **`font-synthesis: none` is REQUIRED or a skew silently satisfies the italic.**

**🔑 THE FINDING THAT REFRAMES THE VERDICT: the author name was ALREADY `font-weight: 600` at 10px.** So V3's weight **is** the baseline's — **the distinction is carried entirely by italic + tracking + brightness, not by weight at all.** *"Bold" was only ever one step (600→700); 800 and 900 remain if more force is wanted.*

**⚠️ AND IT REPAIRED A DEFECT NOBODY WAS LOOKING FOR.** The self name rendered at `rgb(88,92,100)` on `rgb(22,24,28)` = **2.65 : 1 at 10px — below WCAG AA (4.5:1)**. The chosen colour takes it to **14.1 : 1**. *The question asked was "which reads as Self"; the answer incidentally fixed a measurable failure that no automated test covers — **the J-568 shape again: appearance has no verifier, so appearance defects survive.*** Surfaced and accepted: at `#E5E5E5` the name sits **within 3% of the body text**, so it reads at body strength rather than as a subordinate label.

**⚠️ THE LIMIT ON THE VERDICT, RECORDED IN THE SAME SECTION AS THE VERDICT.** **There were NO inbound names on screen.** The self name was judged **in isolation**. 🔑 This establishes that the styling **reads as deliberate and legible**; it does **NOT** establish that it **DISTINGUISHES**, because nothing was present to distinguish it from — and by Joe's own ruling the distinction is *from other people's names*. **Closing this as "distinction achieved" would be the J-560 defect in a new place.** Needs **M-RP6.4 backfill or a second identity**, both already owed.

**📌 FILED, NOT FIXED.** ① **The self panel already solves #5 and the message row does not** — `self-panel.svelte:43` resolves `display_name` ⇒ **"Joe"**, while `entity-item.svelte:65` / `message.svelte:69` use `name ?? id` with `name` null (`stream-panel.svelte:115`, *"NO name (C-8)"*) ⇒ the **65-char XGID**. Same identity, two surfaces, two answers. ② **`region-tile#region-members` exists as a stub with no panel plugin** — the gathered-avatar surface is **not built**. ③ **A registry ladder deviation:** documented 149 → **156** space → 158 latched; **measured 149 → 158 on space selection alone.** Either an eighth axis or an auto-latch — **N-155 says a baseline has seven; this says otherwise.** Unexplained, filed.

**⚠️ A RECORDS ERROR CAUGHT IN THE WRITING.** The session crossed midnight — `e4d9625` was committed **2026-07-22 22:05**, the drive and verdict happened **2026-07-23**. The task doc was first written dated 07-22 throughout and **corrected before commit**. *A verdict carrying the wrong date is a verdict that cannot be checked against the thing that produced it.*

**No new `D`. No new `core` component.** Records: this entry · CLAUDE.md PLAY · `docs/ROADMAP.md` · `tasks/M_RP_SELF_VARIANTS.md` v1.0 **COMPLETED** · `tasks/M_RP_FONTS.md` `Owes:` discharged · `ui/docs/xgen-ui-notes.md` N-161. **NEXT:** `M-RP-SELF-SURFACE` carries these values; ⚠️ **`M-RP-SELF-NAME`'s persisted `widgetId:"self"` stored-data migration is the harder gate.**

## Entry J-572 — The vocabulary crystallised: "window" becomes a loose umbrella, and display form is decided in situ

**Date:** 2026-07-22 · **Seats:** Joe (proposed the loose umbrella, named both fixed terms, reserved the right to change any display form, ruled that form is chosen in the moment) · Chat (grounding, the origin dig, records). **RECORDS + VOCABULARY. Zero code.**

**🔑 THE CONTRADICTION HAD A CAUSE, AND IT WAS NOT CARELESSNESS.** Four locked docs defined `window` as *"its own OS window"* while Joe's D-A (2026-07-16) said *standalone modal area*. Digging to the origin — **Ch6 §6.8.3, Session 2, April 2026** — found: *"A full separate desktop window … it can be opened, minimised, and closed without affecting the main application window."* **That is unambiguous; a modal area cannot be minimised. The text was never vague.**

**🔑 WHAT EXPLAINS IT IS THE MENTAL MODEL, NOT THE WORDING.** Joe recalled meaning a Delphi modal subwindow *with Owner set*. **A Delphi owned modal form IS a real OS window** — a Win32 window, owned by the main form, modal to it. ***In that vocabulary "modal subwindow" and "OS window" were THE SAME OBJECT, and the distinction we now draw — in-DOM overlay vs separate webview — was not expressible.*** ⇒ **"Modal" names a BEHAVIOUR, "window" names a MECHANISM, and this project inherited a model where they were inseparable** (N-160). *When one word carries two properties that were fused in an older model, it splits silently the moment the newer model separates them — and every document written in between looks correct. Ch6 was right, D-A was right, and they contradicted each other.*

**🔒 JOE'S RESOLUTION, AND IT IS SMALLER THAN CHAT'S.** Chat proposed splitting the word into two precise terms across five locked documents. **Joe proposed instead: take `window` and `modal` LIGHTLY — a loose umbrella for "a new area with information not displayed before it opened" — and decide the mechanism per surface, when that surface is designed.** Then he named the two fixed terms: **`separate window`** (*"for distinction from the loose term window"*) and **`modal area`** (*"we can establish as fix term which we know and use already"*).

**🔑 AND BOTH FIXED TERMS TURNED OUT TO BE ALREADY IN THE RECORDS.** *"standalone modal area"* is Joe's own D-A wording; *"a full separate desktop window"* is Ch6 §6.8.3's own April sentence. ***Adopting `separate window` does not correct Ch6 — it makes Ch6 correct as written, and its April text becomes the term's first use rather than a contradiction.*** **Nothing migrated except the vocabulary table.** *The concepts were always right; only the shared word was overloaded.*

**🔒 THE CLAUSE THAT MATTERS MOST — DISPLAY FORM IS DECIDED IN SITU, NEVER INHERITED.** Joe: *"I put an accent on the moment when we will choose any display type — in the moment, not from the old records. Minimum re-discuss it."* So when the Auth plugin is built, **Ch6's "separate window" is HISTORY, NOT INSTRUCTION.** 🔑 **This is forced, not preferred: a display-form decision is a [👁️ PERCEPTION] call, and those cannot be made from records at all** — proven twice the same day, when lock #5 was unfalsifiable until someone looked at a real screen and three typeface variants were void because the thing on screen was not the subject (J-570). ***You cannot look at a document.***

**⚠️ TWO GUARDS PUT ON THAT CLAUSE.** ① **The REASONING is inherited even when the CONCLUSION is not** — Ch6 says *why* (a UI too substantial for a widget, wanting its own lifecycle), and that input survives a flipped answer; otherwise every re-discussion restarts from zero, expensive in the other direction. ② **SCOPE: display form ONLY.** For the wire, identity, the no-anonymity core, GDPR and anything irreversible, **records remain BINDING**. *"Decide in situ, not from old records" is a sentence that would be dangerous if it escaped its category.*

**⚠️ AND THE VOCABULARY IS EXPLICITLY NOT A COMMITMENT.** D-122 now states that it **names mechanisms without assigning them** — Settings being a modal area is a fact about Settings, not a property of the word — and records **Joe's standing reservation to change the display form of any information at any time**, because the UI environment is still crystallising and these shapes were not visible two months ago. ***Stable words, mutable referents — the opposite of what happened to "window".***

**⚠️ CHAT'S OWN HYGIENE DEFECT, SELF-CAUGHT.** Line-ending checks before the Ch6 edit revealed **Chat had been injecting CRLF into predominantly-LF files** across this whole session — 46 lines in `JOURNAL.md`, 46 in `DECISIONS.md`, 23 in `ui-notes`, 7 in each `vite.config.js` (the last already shipped in `9f427a0`). **The repo is per-file, not uniform** — `CLAUDE.md`, `ROADMAP.md` and `skin.css` are natively CRLF, while `Ch6`, the surfaces/tier/dock docs and the configs are pure LF. *The rule is to match the file, not to impose a convention.* All injected CRLF normalised back to LF; Ch6 and N-160 written LF from the start. **Found only because an anchor guard failed and the diagnosis went one level past "retry".**

**WRITTEN:** **D-122 rewritten in place** (it had not yet been committed — so a same-day amendment became a clean single decision instead) · **five vocabulary lines** in `ui/docs/xgen-region-dock-model.md`, `ui/docs/xgen-widget-tier.md` (W-12) and `docs/xgen-widget-surfaces-phase0.md` (×3, incl. the locked §6 block) · **Ch6 §6.8.3 banner** · **N-160** · J-571 corrected where D-122's rewrite made it false · ROADMAP · this entry.

**🔑 THE BOUNDARY IS THE PART THAT WOULD HAVE BITTEN SILENTLY: LOCKS #8 AND #11 CONTRADICT EACH OTHER AT OS-WINDOW SCOPE, AND NOBODY HAD PUT THEM SIDE BY SIDE.** Each Tauri webview is its own JS context, so module-level `$state` is **per-window**, and **#8 makes the echo session-mortal and never persisted** ⇒ two OS windows would hold **two independent echo stores by construction**. *Without that written down, the likeliest future outcome is a user opening a second view and watching a message they just sent simply not be there.* Sharing it requires promoting the store **out of the webview** — a protocol/Rust arc, not a UI one.

**🔑🔑 THEN THE REAL QUESTION: "IF I WANT TO WATCH TWO ROOMS SIDE BY SIDE, WHAT DO I DO?" — AND IT IS NOT A WINDOWING PROBLEM.** Joe's instinct was real OS windows. The dock already supplies the geometry for free. ***A second OS window gives the identical result plus an unshared context — the viewport was never the blocker. The binding is.***

**⚠️ AND THE GATE IS NOT CODE, IT IS W-12:** *"a widget MAY declare exactly one of: `region` … at most one."* **Two stream regions violate the locked model**, so this cannot start as an implementation task — it starts as a taxonomy decision affecting **every** widget, not just the stream.

## Entry J-570 — M-RP-FONTS: the fonts were never loading, and the fix had already been written down once

**Date:** 2026-07-22 · **Seats:** Joe (pushed back on the static-set recommendation, pointed at `fonts/`, locked the plan) · Chat (grounding, build, verification, records). **CODE + ASSETS. No Rust — cargo identical, which proves it.**

**🔑 IT WAS SCOPED AS A TYPOGRAPHY CHORE AND IT FOUND A DEFECT OLDER THAN THE MILESTONE.** `skin.css` asked for weights 500/600/700 at fourteen sites and italic at two while declaring **one** face — Inter-Regular 400 — so every bold and italic in the app was a renderer-synthesised smear. Fixing that meant declaring the rest. Then the verification leg asked a question nobody had asked: *do the fonts actually load?* **They did not. None of them. Not the new ones, and not the Inter-Regular that had been declared all along.**

**⚠️ ROOT CAUSE:** `ui/assets/` sits **outside** each app's Vite root, so `skin.css`'s `url()` references resolve to `/@fs/` paths and the dev server answers **403 Forbidden**. The stylesheet itself loads fine — it arrives through the `$assets` alias as a **module**, not as a served file — so ***the CSS was correct, the files existed, and nothing ever fetched them successfully.*** The dev client had been rendering **`system-ui` / Segoe UI** for the project's entire life.

**🔑 AND IT IS WORSE THAN BEING BROKEN, BECAUSE `vite build` EMITS THE FONTS CORRECTLY** (verified: four fingerprinted assets in `client-dist`). ***So dev and the built app rendered in DIFFERENT TYPEFACES — and every appearance judgement in this project is made in dev.*** A uniform failure would have been noticed years ago; a failure that only affects the surface people look at is invisible by construction.

**🔑🔑 THE FIX WAS ALREADY IN THE REPO, WRITTEN OUT, WITH THE REASONING.** `ui/sampler/vitest.config.js` carries it verbatim from **J-491**: *"The suites live in ../common (outside this package's root), so widen Vite's fs allow-list to the repo root or Vite refuses to load them."* **Same constraint, same directory layout, same solution — applied to the test harness and never generalised to the three dev servers.** *A lesson learned once and filed against one consumer is not a lesson the project has learned.* → `server.fs.allow` added to **client, node and sampler**; fixing one would have left two shells drawing a typeface they do not ship.

**🔒 THE DESIGN CALL, AND JOE OVERTURNED CHAT'S FIRST ANSWER.** Chat recommended declaring **all 34 statics** (~4 MB) and flagged variable fonts as *"worth ten minutes before committing."* Joe pointed at the upstream distributions already sitting in `fonts/` — **both families ship variable builds.** → **4 files, ~1.35 MB**: `InterVariable` + `-Italic` (weight **100–900**) and `JetBrainsMono` + `-Italic` (**100–800**). *The ten minutes Chat flagged and did not spend were the ten minutes that mattered.*

**🔑 AND THE DECIDING ARGUMENT WAS NOT SIZE — IT WAS THE TRAP.** A static subset means the next `font-weight` nobody declared falls back to a synthesised smear **silently, with no error and no failing test**. A continuous axis makes every weight real, including stops no static file can provide. ***The person a silent type fallback catches is whoever is tuning appearance*** — and `skin.css` is Joe's file, tuned live over HMR. *The same shape as the appearance-has-no-automated-verifier finding at J-568: type had no verifier either, and that is exactly why it stayed broken.*

**⚠️ THE DIRECT COST TO WORK ALREADY DONE:** Joe had judged three *"Self"* typeface variants on screen — *"1 system mono"*, *"2 JetBrains Mono"*, *"3 Inter italic + tracking"*. **All three were fallback fonts.** No JetBrains Mono face was ever declared, so variant 2 could not have been it; variant 3's italic was a skewed Regular. ***A [👁️ PERCEPTION] verdict is only as good as whether the thing looked at was the subject*** — the test is filed to be re-run, not salvaged. *(N-157 at the type layer: it was named, it rendered, and it was plausibly not the subject.)*

**VERIFIED — and the control mattered more than usual.** ⚠️ `document.fonts.check()` returns **false for an unloaded face**, so *"never requested"* and *"broken"* return the same string; every check was preceded by a forced `document.fonts.load()`. Results: fetch **403 → 200** · all four faces reach **`loaded`** · `check('600 …')` **true** and `check('italic 700 … Mono')` **true** — **combinations with no static file on disk, so the variable axis is proven, not assumed** · the head-marker notice now computes italic against a **loaded** italic face where it had been a skew. Registry **149** at open, **149 → 156 → 158** on latch.

**FLOORS:** cargo **1553/0/62 across 56 terminator lines — IDENTICAL** (summed programmatically; *proves* no Rust landed) · vite **202 / 170** · npm **154** · svelte-check **0/34/15** · sampler catalogue **419**. **Scope:** 34 statics + 2 orphan copies removed, 4 faces + 3 licence files added, `skin.css` + 3 `vite.config.js` modified. ⚠️ **The `ui/templates` Inter copy was deliberately KEPT** — it is referenced by that template's own `app.css`, which makes it the last surviving instance of the old pattern. *Chat's earlier "three stale copies" claim was two out of three, corrected by grounding before anything was deleted.*

**⚠️ TWO OF CHAT'S OWN MISTAKES, BOTH CAUGHT BY GUARDS RATHER THAN BY LUCK.** ① **`Copy-Item` copied nothing and reported success** — `JetBrainsMono[wght].ttf` contains `[wght]`, a PowerShell **wildcard character class**, so the pattern matched no file; `-LiteralPath` fixes it. *N-156's shape in the shell: an operation that does nothing and returns cleanly.* ② **A `Regex.Replace` with an escaped replacement corrupted `skin.css` into a single escaped line** — caught by **reading the file back** instead of trusting the `@font-face` count, reverted with `git checkout` after confirming the only dirty tracked file was that one, then redone with a plain string replace. A third guard fired correctly and wrote nothing when a here-string's LF met a CRLF file. ***Every one of these was caught by a read-back or an anchor assertion, which is the only reason none of them shipped.***

**OWED:** **M-RP-FONTS-WOFF2** (mono TTF→woff2, ~400 KB, size not correctness) · **M-RP-SELF-VARIANTS** (re-run the perception test against real fonts). Records: `tasks/M_RP_FONTS.md` **v1.0** · ROADMAP · this entry. **No new D.** ⚠️ **M-RP-LOCK-RECHECK remains ACTIVE** — #11's wording and Leg C are still owed and none of this touched them.
## Entry J-569 — The lock re-check, Leg A: ten locks re-driven with controls, and a SECOND lock that cannot fail

**Date:** 2026-07-21 · **Seats:** Joe (locked the #5 split; app free for the drive) · Chat (grounding, drive, controls, records). **VERIFICATION + RECORDS. ZERO code. No fix landed.**

**🔑 THE MILESTONE FOUND ITS OWN DEFECT A SECOND TIME, AND THAT IS THE ENTRY.** M-RP-LOCK-RECHECK was filed because J-560 closed Leg D2 claiming *"ONE LOCK UNMET"* when two were, and because lock **#5** appeared nowhere in that close — *not met, not unmet, not deferred.* The stated lesson was that **a lock with no verification leg is unfalsifiable: it cannot fail, so it cannot be trusted.** Leg A re-drove the ten machine locks at HEAD `b477bae` — and found **lock #11 in exactly the same condition, unnoticed for the whole arc.** *One instance is an oversight; the second one, found by the pass filed to investigate the first, is a mechanism.*

**⚠️ FINDING ① — #5 WAS NEVER EYE-ONLY, AND THE PROBE TOOK FIVE LINES.** The runbook's §2 classified it *"EYE — Joe. No mechanism to drive."* **§2 also warns, in its own text, that it is a PREDICTION and that §7's cargo row was a confident prediction that was false two days earlier.** Grounded against the code: `stream/derive.ts::projectEvent` and `stream-panel.svelte:115` both apply C-8's **inbound** rule to own rows — `isOwn` is computed and **never used to suppress the identifier**. So the lock's negative half — *does a person see their own hash tail?* — is a **DOM read with a control**, and it **fails**: the rendered author name is **byte-identical to the self `identity_id`** (65 chars, tail `wpKHGc` present), avatar `name:null` / `initials:"GC"`, agreed by **three independent sources** (painted `textContent`, the registry getter, the self store). 🔑 **The unmet half was the machine-checkable half all along.** What belongs there INSTEAD stays Joe's. ⇒ **#5 splits exactly as #6 already does** — Joe locked the split.

**⚠️⚠️ FINDING ② — #11 IS A SECOND UNFALSIFIABLE LOCK, AND ITS OWN WORDING IS THE AMBIGUITY.** *"N windows, one device."* Measured, not remembered: `xgen-client/tauri.conf.json` declares **ONE** window, and there is **ZERO** runtime window-creation code (`WebviewWindowBuilder` / `WindowBuilder` / `create_window` — none). **At OS-window scope the lock cannot be driven, cannot fail, and cannot be trusted** — #5's shape precisely. At **tile** scope — which is what the store's own comment argues — it is drivable and **MET**: the whole grid was unmounted (composer *and* stream) and **all four echoes survived**, with `composerMounted` 1→0 as the control proving the unmount really happened. **Same words, opposite verdicts.** ***Rewording a lock is a records decision about Joe's own design, so it was NOT taken*** — filed, named, and left on his desk. *(And a quiet second lesson: module-level `$state` is per-webview, so if #11 ever DID mean OS windows, it would not merely be unverified — it would be false.)*

**⚠️ FINDING ③ — LOCK #7's TEXT IS STALE AGAINST WHAT SHIPPED.** §9.11.3 reads *"timed_out → retry only behind an explicit warning."* Shipped is **no retry affordance at all**, narrowed deliberately at D2 §3.1 and enforced in **both** the store's refusal and the widget's button (one predicate, N-126). The behaviour is right and the reasoning is sound — a retry on `timed_out` can place a permanent identity-attributed duplicate on the federated network. **The table simply never received the amendment.** *The J-566 shape again: a decision applied in code and not in the record.*

**🔑 THE STRONGEST LEG WAS #7, BECAUSE IT PROVED A REFUSAL RATHER THAN AN ABSENCE.** *"The bad thing is absent"* and *"nothing happened"* are the same string. So the bypass was driven at the **store** layer, beneath the button: `retry()` on `rejected` and on `timed_out` resolved to **`null`** and left both rows byte-unchanged — **and the SAME call on the `failed` row MUTATED it** (`failed`→`accepted`, eventId ABSENT→`RETRYPROOF0001`). *A refusal indistinguishable from a stuck bridge is not proven* — the M-RP7.6 V1 pattern, applied without being asked for.

**MEASURED — every lock with its own control (full table in `tasks/M_RP_LOCK_RECHECK.md` §10):** #1 ✅ (echo 0→1 read in the SAME eval as the click — on screen before the network) · #2 ✅ (grep proven live by 8 other `$state` hits) · #3 ✅ (ABSENT pre-state measured, so the stitch is a transition) · #4 ✅ (`sentAt` invariant across an outcome that changed OTHER fields on that row) · **#5 ❌ UNMET** · #6 ✅ machine half (getter tone === painted `data-tone` ×4, labels distinct) · #7 ✅ · #8 ✅ (no persistence path; live 4→0 on reload) · #9 ✅ · **#10 ❌ UNMET, re-confirmed not re-tested into a pass** (row landed 15→16, max 639→705, `scrollTop` stayed **0**; the probe proven to see scroll at 639.2→0) · #11 ⚠️ split · #12 ✅ both directions (typing yes / sending no; latching flipped ONLY the button and the 18-char draft survived).

**🔑 #9's "MISSING" 13th ROW WAS EXPLAINED BY ARITHMETIC, NOT BY A STORY.** `groupedCount` read **12** where 14 echoes after a `system` head should give 13 continuations. Rather than reason about it, the per-row flags were measured: **two group heads**, 425,026 ms ≈ **7.1 minutes** apart — past the 5-minute window. The rule was working. *A number that disagrees with the expectation is a hypothesis; measure before you explain.*

## Entry J-568 — The ACTIVE-header sweep: a status field that could not answer "is anything open?", and a retired seat that left ten orphans

**Date:** 2026-07-21 · **Seats:** Joe (locked the `Owes:` convention, the `HANDS OFF` convention, the folder split, and the B-split on the orphans) · Chat (sweep, grep, filings, records). **RECORDS + ONE FILE MOVE. ZERO code, zero floors touched, none re-measured** (N-108 — nothing was built).

**🔑 IT STARTED AS A ONE-LINE QUESTION FROM JOE — *"do we have some milestone still open?"* — AND THE HONEST ANSWER REQUIRED A GREP.** Five task files read `Status: ACTIVE` while the ROADMAP recorded their milestones closed. ***A DoD signal that needs a human to interpret it has stopped being a signal.*** Two were genuinely stale (`M_RP6_1I_SHELF` → closed J-508, `M_RP6_1J_SHELF_MOUNT` → closed J-509, both now **COMPLETED**); two are real parents with real open work; one was not a milestone at all.

**🔒 Q1 — THE `Owes:` LINE (Joe-locked, "very strict and unexpanded").** Parent docs gain **one header line**: IDs with short titles, separated by `·`, **nothing else** — no reasons, no dates, no parentheticals. **One physical line**, and *if it does not fit, the doc owns too much and should be split — the line's length is the signal.* An item leaves when it closes; **when the line is empty, `Status` flips to `ARCHIVED`**, so *`Owes:` empty plus `ACTIVE` is a contradiction anyone can spot.* Leg runbooks never get one. Applied to `M_RP6_3_COMPOSER` (v2.1) and `M_RP6_6_RESIDENT` (v1.3). **Not applied retroactively** — only to files a sweep touches.

**🔒 Q2 — THE `INTERACTIVE — HANDS OFF` CONVENTION (Joe-locked).** Any leg whose reading depends on UI state posts a clear chat warning **before** driving — app, what is being read, what not to touch, expected duration — and **always** an `✅ ALL CLEAR` after, *including when the run dies*. 🔑 **The all-clear is half the protocol, not politeness:** a hands-off with no stated end leaves Joe frozen or guessing when it expired, *and a guess is exactly the click that lands mid-probe.* Fires for registry counts, computed style, geometry, scroll/focus and keystroke legs; **does NOT fire for cargo, npm, svelte-check, git or files on disk** — ***warning on those would train him to ignore the warning, which is worse than missing one.*** ⚠️ **And the standing default outranks the convention: the app is Joe's.** If he is in it, the driver waits. *His walking through the app is the highest-yield verification this project has — three defects in one day that no automated leg caught.* ⚠️ Harness limit stated rather than worked around: the dev ports are fixed, so **two clients cannot run at once**; node and sampler are separate.

**🔒 THE FOLDER SPLIT (Joe-locked, option B).** `CDP_DEBUG_HARNESS.md` is a **living reference, not a milestone** — it will never be COMPLETED, ARCHIVED or DEPRECATED, and **none of the five statuses fits it.** Moved `tasks/` → `docs/` (`git mv`, history preserved), header gains a `Kind:` line. ***This fixes the category error rather than the label***, and it makes *"everything in `tasks/` is a milestone"* true — which is what gives the `Owes:` rule and the next sweep any meaning. **Live pointers updated** (`cdp-debug.ps1` ×2, `run-sampler.ps1`); **historical references in JOURNAL and the UI notes left untouched** — *a pointer someone will follow gets fixed; a record of what was true then does not.*

**⚠️⚠️ AND THE SWEEP FOUND WHAT THE MORNING'S CORRECTION ONLY GUESSED AT.** J-567 recorded that D2's lock #5 is the only one of the twelve with a split owner — *"Wording/appearance = Ms Design"* — and that the seat was retired at **J-555**, five entries before D2 shipped. **That was written down explicitly as INFERENCE, not proven cause.** The sweep then found `M_RP6_6_RESIDENT.md` **§7, a handoff stub addressed to the same retired seat**, also unmoved. 🔑 **Two identically-shaped orphans from one retirement stopped being a coincidence**, so a grep followed: **eight comments in SHIPPED CODE name the retired seat**, four of them marking copy **the user is reading right now** as PROVISIONAL — `derive.ts:39` (the C-6 head-marker notice) · `stream-panel.svelte:45` (empty-stream copy) · `resident.rs:840` (connection copy) · plus five appearance assignments. **Ten known, and the document-side sort is not done.**

**🔑 THE FINDING IS WORTH MORE THAN THE LIST, AND IT EXPLAINS SOMETHING THIS PROJECT HAS COMPLAINED ABOUT THREE TIMES.** ***Every single orphan is an appearance or wording item. Not one is code, a test, or a protocol decision.*** That is not chance: **appearance is the only category here with no automated verifier** — cargo, svelte-check, npm, the catalogue and the registry all say nothing about whether a sentence is the right sentence. So an appearance item parked against a seat **produces no failing signal when the seat disappears.** It simply waits. ⇒ ***M-RP-SKIN is not six cosmetic chores Joe has not got to; it is the sink for the one category the project cannot verify, and it has been fed by a retirement nobody swept after.*** Chat has written *"a discharger that only accumulates has stopped being a plan"* three times — **this is the first time the cause is on the table rather than the symptom.**

**🔒 AND JOE SPLIT IT RATHER THAN LETTING IT RIDE (option B).** The orphans arrived mid-scoping of the lock re-check and would have roughly doubled it. **Two filings, not one:** `M-RP-LOCK-RECHECK` asks *"were the locks true?"*; `M-RP-SEAT-ORPHANS` asks *"who owns appearance now that the seat is gone?"* — *different questions, and B is the only option where the second gets asked out loud instead of absorbed into a queue.*

**FILED:** **`M-RP-LOCK-RECHECK` — re-verify the twelve D2 locks and mark each with its verifier.** ZERO code; **no fix lands there** — *a verification pass that also fixes things cannot tell you whether it verified or created.* Ten locks machine-driven with controls, **two eye-judged by Joe and by nobody else** (#5, known unmet; #6, whether four distinct outcomes *read as three states*), verdicts **quoted, not paraphrased** — *a paraphrased appearance verdict is Chat deciding what Joe meant.* Its floors are a **control, not a gate**: the milestone writes no code, so **a moved floor means something was touched that should not have been.** ⚠️ Its §2 classification table is a **prediction**, and *§7's cargo row was a confident prediction that was false yesterday* — a lock resisting its predicted verifier is a finding. **`M-RP-SEAT-ORPHANS` — re-home the retired seat's unowned appearance items**, whose real output is a **routing decision per item** and a **standing rule**: candidate — *no item may be assigned to a SEAT; items belong to a MILESTONE, and seats are staffing.* ⚠️ *A seat can be retired. A milestone must be closed, deferred or cancelled — all three leave a trace.*

**No new N, no new D** — the two conventions are Joe-locked here and will graduate to DECISIONS when a milestone exercises them. **🟢 NEXT = M-RP-LOCK-RECHECK, then M-RP-SELF-NAME.**

## Entry J-566 — M-RP-PROCESSOR-SEED design-locked: the fix was already decided on 4 July, and the code never received it

**Date:** 2026-07-21 · **Seats:** Joe (locked all four decisions; supplied the finding that turned the seed into a requirement) · Chat (grounding, options, runbook, records). **DESIGN + RECORDS ONLY, NO CODE. No floor moved, none re-measured** (N-108 — nothing was built). → `tasks/M_RP_PROCESSOR_SEED.md` v1.0 ACTIVE · **D-100 SECOND AMENDMENT** (no new D-number, Joe's call).

**⚠️⚠️ THE FINDING THAT REFRAMES THE MILESTONE, AND IT WAS THE FIRST THING THE GREP RETURNED. `DECISIONS.md` D-100's FIRST AMENDMENT, DATED 2026-07-04, ALREADY LOCKS THIS EXACT FIX — INCLUDING THE BYTE-IDENTICAL SEED STRING** `-> → | <- ← | :) 🙂 | <3 ❤️ | :( 🙁 | -- ‒` — **and already states the general rule** (*a shorter `find` shadows a longer one during live keystroke-rescan*) as a sibling to the convergence lint. It names **THREE sites**: client `app.rs`, sampler host `main.rs`, and the sampler placeholder. **`git log -S` proves exactly ONE was done** — commit `7872a77` changed the placeholder to `type -> <- :) <3 :( -- to morph`; **neither Rust const has moved since `7ea70fa`.** ⇒ *For seventeen days the decision said one thing, both binaries did another, and the sampler's own placeholder instructed users to type tokens the shipped seed does not contain.* **Then on 2026-07-20 Joe found the defect by typing, Chat proposed dropping `--`, Joe re-derived the shortened arrows, and J-563 recorded it as a novel improvement over Chat's proposal.** 🔑 ***A decision that is not applied is indistinguishable from one that was never taken, and the record then credits the rediscovery.*** **THE J-561 CLASS INVERTED, AND WORSE:** J-561 was a *remembered* gate asserted as current; this is a **written, locked, on-disk decision that nobody read** — and unlike J-561, which cost a choice, this one cost **a live defect reaching the user and staying there for two and a half weeks.** → **J-563 corrected in place by pointer, D-100 opened with the admission. Nothing rewritten.**

**🔑 JOE'S CLARIFICATION TURNED A CONVENIENCE INTO A REQUIREMENT, AND IT ARRIVED AS A CHALLENGE TO THE DESIGN.** He raised that he had wanted **no hardcoded pairs** — rules should come only from the config file. **Checked by grep, not answered from the decision text: he is right and it already holds.** `configs.ts` (the retired `arrowMorph`/`emojiMorph` presets) is **not on disk**; there are **ZERO** hardcoded rule arrays in live UI code; every path into the store is `setRules(<string>)` sourced from a config file or the user's own typing (`app_client.svelte:537` · `app_sampler.svelte:90` · the editor's `setRules(draft)`). **The processor cannot see a pair that did not come from a config file or from the user.** The one remaining hardcoded pair *text* is the seed const, used exactly once — in `write_fresh_config`, at config **birth**. **Then Joe closed the loop himself:** the generator must write *something*, and the pairs must be there from the first run *"also because they are examples how to define the next ones."* ⇒ **THE SEED HAS A SECOND JOB THAT WAS NEVER WRITTEN DOWN: it is the ONLY worked example of the D-100 grammar anywhere in the UI.** That makes it **unemptyable** and constrains its **content** — the set must demonstrate the grammar's range, not merely be useful. The locked set does (multi-char `find`, emoji `replace`, symbol `replace`), *which was luck rather than design and is now a stated property.* **Recorded because a hardcoded literal whose second job is undocumented looks exactly like dead data to whoever reads it next.** *A design question raised as a doubt turned into the requirement that protects the thing from a future tidy-up.*

**🔒 FOUR DECISIONS, BOTH D-121 LENSES PER OPTION.** **D-a — the migration list is S2 ONLY.** **🔑 S1 IS NOT DEFECTIVE:** it carries no `--` rule, so nothing is a proper prefix of `-->` and typing `-->` under S1 correctly yields `→`; **the defect arrived with S2**, when `--` was added beside a rule it shadows. Migrating an S1 install would make `--` a rule and turn its working `-->` into `‒>` — ***the exact defect this milestone removes, newly installed, silently, in a file the user never touched.*** **⚠️ CHAT RECOMMENDED S1+S2 AND THEN REVERSED IT** — the first answer reasoned correctly about cost (one const, one test) and was **answering the wrong question**; *the bound's principle is that untouched defaults get migrated, but its PURPOSE is to repair a defect we shipped, and consistency is not a reason to change behaviour under someone.* **D-b — the absent-section repair is IN, as a named FOURTH leg**, not folded into the migration. **D-c — D-100 second amendment, no new D-number.** **D-d — the reachability check is a NON-THROWING diagnostic and must never join `assertSafeRules`.**

**🔑 D-d IS THE FINDING THAT DECIDES LEG D, AND IT INVERTS THE OBVIOUS IMPLEMENTATION.** `assertSafeRules` **throws**, and `store.svelte.ts:setRules` **fails safe to empty** on rejection. Folding reachability into the validator would take a user with **five working rules and one broken one** and leave them with **ZERO substitutions**, explained only by a `console.warn` stripped from release builds. ***A check that blanks the whole rule set to report one unreachable pair is strictly worse than the bug it diagnoses.*** ⇒ computed separately, **never gates Apply**, surfaced beside the offending rule — the V-C3b shape: *make it visible and let the user fix their own data.*

**⚠️ AND A LIVE DEFECT THE GROUNDING TURNED UP, IN SCOPE BY JOE'S CALL (D-b).** `SubstitutionsSection` derives `Default` and `rules` carries `#[serde(default)]`, so a config with **no `[substitutions]` section at all** parses to `Some("")` — **indistinguishable from *the user cleared their pairs***. `clean_slate_config` re-injects that empty string over the freshly seeded pack, so ***a pre-M-RP4.2 config launching on a current build is blanked permanently and never receives the starter pack — including the grammar example it now exists to provide.*** **Real, not hypothetical:** `instances\lp-cli\xgen-client_config.toml` on this machine has no section. *J-562's §3.1 conflation one level up — two states that are the same value at the point of decision, and only the presence of the section can tell them apart.*

**SCOPE CORRECTED BEFORE THE RUNBOOK, BY GREP:** the kickoff called Leg A *"one `const`, Rust"*. It is **TWO consts in TWO crates** (`app.rs:155` + `xgen-sampler/main.rs:30`), **both cargo floors move**, and **the sampler placeholder is already correct and must not be touched.** *The J-556 / J-560 §1.4 shape — a count asserted from the file someone happened to have open — caught this time before it reached a runbook rather than by the implementer reading one.*

**GROUNDED POPULATION CHECK, so D-a was not argued in the abstract:** every config on this machine reads **S2** — Joe's live config, `instances\bob`, and the stale seeded copy under `C:\cargo-targets\XGenProtocol\debug\`. **Zero S1 configs exist here.** Combined with the fact that **no config could carry a stale seed until Leg C shipped on 2026-07-20**, the migration's real-world population today is **one machine**. *The bound still matters as precedent; the urgency is lower than the kickoff implied, and saying so is cheaper than discovering it mid-build.*

**THE BOUND, WRITTEN BEFORE THE CODE (D-100 ②):** byte-identity only — **never** a substring match, prefix/suffix test, normalisation, trim, parse-and-compare or similarity heuristic · an explicit list of **named constants**, the old seed kept **because the constant IS the evidence** · **a curated list is NEVER migrated** · the list never grows silently. **And the mechanism is smaller than the ceremony:** the migration is a **SKIP**, not a rewrite — `write_fresh_config` has already written the new seed, so migrating means *not overwriting it back*.

**⚠️ §5's V-A2 IS THE LEG THIS MILESTONE EXISTS FOR AND THE RUNBOOK NAMES IT BY NAME:** every seed pair typed **one character at a time**, with a **positive control** (a non-rule token comes through unmorphed) and a **negative control** (`-->` must now yield `‒>`, proving the shadowing relation is gone rather than hidden). *A wholesale value-set verifies the transform function, not the feature — and that is exactly how this shipped broken* (N-154).

**Apps and dev servers stopped, verified BY PORT** (5173 · 5174 · 5175 · 8080 · 9222 · 9322 · 9422 all 0 listeners, zero `XGenProtocol` processes) — the static gates need them down and the next seat should not inherit them (N-117 / N-140).

**No new N** — nothing was measured that a note would outlive; the findings live in D-100 where they bind. **🟢 NEXT = M-RP-PROCESSOR-SEED implementation from runbook v1.0 (Clair), Legs A+B together** — ⚠️ they are ONE user-visible outcome and must not be split.

## Entry J-565 — M-RP-MSG-NEWLINE closed: one CSS declaration, and the question it was filed to answer turned out not to be a question

**Date:** 2026-07-21 · **Seats:** Joe (locked both decisions; made the `skin.css` edit with his own hands) · Chat (grounding, the two option sets, live CDP verification, records). **Scope: ONE file, ONE hunk, +13/−0 — `ui/assets/skin.css`.** Zero `.rs`, zero `.ts`, zero `.svelte`. → `tasks/M_RP_MSG_NEWLINE.md` v1.0 `COMPLETED`.

**WHAT SHIPPED.** `white-space: pre-wrap` on `.message .message-paragraph`, with a twelve-line comment marking it NOT COSMETIC and naming its own measurement. Shift+Enter now reaches the rendered message. **First of the five sequenced at J-564, and it goes first not for its size** — *solving line breaks in CSS takes `<br>` off kind-4's allowlist, and every element removed from a sanitiser's allowlist is one less thing that has to be right forever.*

**🔑 DECISION ① DISSOLVED UNDER GROUNDING — THE TOMBSTONE AND `(edited)` WERE NEVER DESCENDANTS.** The milestone was filed asking whether they *inherit* `pre-wrap`. Reading `message.svelte` answered it structurally: `.msg-content` holds **three SIBLINGS** — the `<p class="message-paragraph">`, `<span class="msg-deleted">` and `<span class="message-edited">`. A rule on the body **cannot reach** the other two; they would inherit only if the declaration were hoisted to `.message` / `.msg-content`. ***The question was real, and its answer was that it was the wrong question*** — cheap to find by reading, expensive to find by arguing.

**THREE OPTIONS, BOTH D-121 LENSES PER OPTION, JOE LOCKED A.** **A** on `.message-paragraph` — ① breaks render, tombstone and marker untouched; ② one line, **no floor moves** (CSS moves no module graph, J-550) · **B** hoisted — ① identical today, ***a trap later***: any skin copy string with indentation or a run of spaces starts rendering it literally; ② same line plus a latent constraint on all future copy · **A2** a new `<style>` block in `message.svelte` — ① identical, protects the declaration from a skin sweep **structurally** rather than by comment; ② **moves two vite floors** (N-141: a Svelte `<style>` block is exactly one module — client 202→203, sampler 170→171). *A2's protection is real; it costs two floor moves on a one-declaration fix, and a comment is cheaper than a module.*

**🔑 NAMED, NOT TRADED — THE PROPERTY THAT MAKES THE SCOPE CORRECT RATHER THAN CONVENIENT:** `pre-wrap` also preserves **runs of spaces and leading indentation**. On the body that is **user content**, so preserving it is right. On skin-owned copy it would be wrong. ***The same declaration is correct in one place and a defect three lines away, which is precisely why the scope is a decision and not a detail.*** **DELIBERATELY NOT FOLDED IN:** `overflow-wrap: anywhere` — `pre-wrap` still soft-wraps at spaces, so long tokens behave exactly as today; *an unmeasured change riding a measured one is how a clean verification stops meaning anything.* **STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER:** `.message[data-kind="system"] .message-paragraph` also matches, so system notices gain it too — app-authored strings, **no user-visible change today**, and correct if one ever holds a newline.

**🔒 DECISION ② — THE WIRE LEG IS SEPARATE, AND NOT ASSUMED.** The echo store proves the **client's own record** holds `\n`; whether it survives out to a node and back is **untested**. Shipping the CSS fixes the case Joe reported; no wire outcome changes the declaration; if `\n` dies on the round trip that is a **protocol/serialisation defect with its own fix**, and finding it after the CSS is in is strictly easier **because the renderer is no longer a confound**. → filed `M-RP-MSG-NEWLINE-WIRE`. ⚠️ *Do not assume the protocol preserves it.*

**⚠️ WHOSE HANDS, RECORDED SO IT DOES NOT WIDEN SILENTLY.** `ui/assets/skin.css` is Joe's cosmetics file. Chat brought **the line and the reasoning**; **Joe pasted it himself**. For a single declaration a runbook and a handoff cost more than the change — he approved that deviation from *"Chat does not implement"* explicitly, and it is written down **as a deviation**, not absorbed as a new norm. The in-block comment is what stops a future M-RP-SKIN sweep from deleting a correctness fix that happens to live in the skin.

**VERIFIED LIVE AT 9222 (Chat drove; client only, no concurrent cargo — N-117; ports polled by number, not by name).** **V1** computed `whiteSpace` = `pre-wrap`; nothing shadows it, since the pre-fix probe measured `normal`, i.e. **no author rule reached the element at all** · **V2 AND ITS POSITIVE CONTROL** — `controlline` (11 chars, no newline) **18px** vs `alpha\nbravo` (11 chars, one newline) **36px**: ***the identical character count is the whole point*** — same font, same element, same width, so wrapping cannot explain the difference · **V3** injected `.msg-deleted` and `.message-edited` into a real `.msg-content` → both **`normal`**, parent `.msg-content` **`normal`**, **control** the real `.message-paragraph` in the *same subtree* **`pre-wrap`**, probes reverted to 0. ***Without that control, "normal everywhere" is indistinguishable from a probe reading nothing*** — the N-139/N-142 family, guarded against rather than re-learned · **V4** registry **164**, `count === unique === domCount`, 0 duplicates, **decomposed not adjusted**: 158 − 2 (the *"No messages in this room yet."* row leaves) + 5 (first echo) + 3 (second echo, grouped) = **164 exact**.

**🔑 AN UNPLANNED RESULT THAT LANDS ON THE STRONGEST AVAILABLE ROW:** the newline message arrived as a **grouped continuation** — same author within the window, avatar and name suppressed, **3 registered ids instead of 5**, D-106 behaving. *So `pre-wrap` is proven on the row type that strips the most chrome, not merely on a fresh-header row — the case nobody thought to specify.*

**⚠️ N-155 — A REGISTRY BASELINE HAS A SEVENTH AXIS: WHETHER A ROOM IS LATCHED.** Measured on one fresh launch: **149** at rest (three spaces in the store, nothing selected) → **156** with a space selected → **158** with a room latched. The kickoff carried **158** as *the* client baseline **without naming the condition that produces it**. ***A baseline quoted without its condition is not wrong, it is unreadable*** — and this one would have read as a `+9` defect to anyone who launched the app and counted. Extends N-148/N-152: quiescence · store · selection · saved-state count · echo count · settings drill-in · **room latch**. **⚠️ AND ONE DELTA IS LEFT UNEXPLAINED ON PURPOSE:** space-select moved 149 → 156, of which rooms account for **+3**; **+4 has no account and none was invented.** Outside this milestone, no bearing on the fix. *An honest gap in a record is worth more than a plausible story.*

**FLOORS NOT RE-MEASURED, WITH THE REASON STATED INSTEAD OF THE NUMBERS QUOTED:** the diff is one CSS block — zero `.rs`, zero `.ts`, zero `.svelte`. cargo 1549/0/62 × 56 · svelte-check 0/34/15 · npm 142 · vite 202 client / 170 sampler · catalogue 419 stand **by scope** (N-108 — *arithmetic is not measurement, and quoting numbers nobody took is worse than naming which ones were not taken*).

## Entry J-564 — The next five milestones sequenced, and two new ones filed: line breaks, and the render-side engine that has never existed

**Date:** 2026-07-20 · **Seats:** Joe (asked the question that found it; locked the sequence) · Chat (grounding, filing). **Records-only, NO CODE, no floor moved.** ⚠️ **`ui/assets/skin.css` is modified in the working tree and the apps are running — JOE'S WORK IN FLIGHT (`.subs-note` margin `--sp-1` → `--sp-0`), appearance being his domain. Deliberately EXCLUDED from this commit rather than folded in.**

**🔑 JOE ASKED WHETHER ALL PROCESSOR MODES HAD BEEN TESTED, ESPECIALLY RICH TEXT / `.md` RENDERING. THE ANSWER IS NO, AND THE REASON IS THAT HALF THE ARCHITECTURE HAS NEVER BEEN BUILT.** Grounded against D-099 (*two engines × four rule-kinds*) rather than answered from the runbook's own fence line: **edit-side engine BUILT** (`processor.ts`) · **kind 1 transformer BUILT and now wired at exactly one call site** · **kind 2 converter and kind 3 filter/guard built in `$common` but with ZERO CLIENT CALL SITES — sampler only** · **render-side engine (`use:render`) DOES NOT EXIST** · **kind 4 renderer `string → safeHTML` DOES NOT EXIST.** D-099 says it outright: *the markup/sanitiser sink is not built this arc* — deferred under D-065, no empty machinery. ***So there was nothing to test: markdown rendering has never been built.***

**AND A SECOND REPORT OF JOE'S, GROUNDED: SHIFT+ENTER WORKS IN THE COMPOSER BUT THE LINE BREAK NEVER REACHES THE MESSAGE.** ⚠️ **The newline is NOT lost — it is COLLAPSED AT PAINT.** `composer-panel.svelte:67` is `draft.trim()`, which strips leading/trailing whitespace only and **does not touch interior newlines**, so the `\n` is in the sent text; `message.svelte` renders `body` as a **plain text node**, and a `white-space` sweep of `skin.css` returns only `nowrap` rules, **none on the message body** — so HTML's default collapses the newline to a space. ***The data is fine; the renderer throws it away. What the user sent is not what the user is shown — the D6 / D-065 class, quiet rather than loud.*** **⚠️ Confidence stated rather than buried: that is TWO GREPS, NOT A LIVE PROBE.** Leg 1 must read `\n` out of the echo store's `text`; if it is absent there the diagnosis flips to a data bug and the fix moves. *N-153's lesson, one day old — a wrong cause that reproduces looks exactly like a fixed one.* **Separate and NOT assumed: whether `\n` survives a real WIRE round-trip is untested and needs a node** — named as an open leg rather than presumed.

**🔑 THE TWO REPORTS ARE THE SAME DESIGN QUESTION, AND THE CODE ALREADY KNEW IT.** `paragraph.svelte:13–19` describes the planned kind 4 in detail — WordStar/markdown-lineage `_x_`/`*x*`, a whitelist of `<strong>`/`<em>`/**`<br>`**, an escape character, and links named as *"the one risky add"*, landing as a `$common` `use:render` action, *"built separately, later."* **So `<br>` is already in the planned allowlist.** **⚠️ BUT THE TWO ROUTES TO A LINE BREAK ARE NOT EQUIVALENT:** `white-space: pre-wrap` is **CSS only — the body stays a TEXT NODE, no `{@html}`, no sanitiser, NO XSS SURFACE AT ALL**; kind-4 `<br>` requires **opening `{@html}` and trusting a sanitiser on every message body, including ones that arrived over the wire from another identity.** ⇒ ***For typed line breaks the CSS route is strictly better, and it keeps `{@html}` closed — which is exactly what N-032's anti-`{@html}` lean and `message.svelte:40`'s "never `{@html}`" were protecting.*** **Kind 4 is then needed only for AUTHORED MARKUP, not for paragraph breaks. 🔒 This is written down BEFORE kind 4 is built, because otherwise someone implements `<br>` as the newline answer and opens the sanitiser surface for something CSS already solved.**

**🔒 SEQUENCE LOCKED BY JOE. The ordering argument is about WHAT MAKES LATER WORK SMALLER, not about size.**
1. **`M-RP-MSG-NEWLINE`** — preserve typed line breaks. *Goes first not because it is small but because* ***solving line breaks in CSS TAKES `<br>` OFF KIND-4'S ALLOWLIST*** *— and every element removed from a sanitiser's allowlist is one less thing that has to be right forever.*
2. **`M-RP-PROCESSOR-SEED`** — the arrow, the migration, the lint. Joe is waiting on it and it affects every install. ⚠️ carries the **first config rewrite on upgrade the project has ever done**, with a bound Joe must approve — *that is the part that deserves the time, not the `const`.*
3. **`core`'s prop-less `Record<string, Component>`** — six sites. 🔑 **Two of them are `message.svelte` and `message-stream.svelte`, the exact files milestone 5 will open** — fix the types first and the message family is touched **once with correct types instead of twice.**
4. **`M-RP-COMPOSER-SCROLL`** — *you scroll up to re-read, reply, press Enter, and your message drops to a bottom you cannot see, with its send-status.* **Same family as the newline defect: the app quietly not showing you what you did.**
5. **`M-RP-PROCESSOR-RENDER`** — the render-side engine and kind-4 markup. **LAST, DELIBERATELY:** by then `<br>` is handled, the message family is correctly typed and the scroll is right, **so it can be ONLY about the sanitiser.** ⚠️ ***THE FIRST THING IN THE PROJECT THAT RENDERS ANOTHER IDENTITY'S TEXT AS MARKUP, ON A NETWORK WITH NO ANONYMITY. That is a SECURITY LOCK, JOE'S, and the one milestone here that must not be scoped in a single sitting — placing it fifth buys that time honestly rather than by stalling.***

*Chat deferred to Joe on 1-vs-2 as genuinely interchangeable (independent, both small); **the only ordering carrying a real argument is newline-before-RENDER and typing-before-RENDER**. Joe took the recommendation as given.*

**⚠️ M-RP-SKIN FLAGGED: A DISCHARGER THAT ONLY ACCUMULATES STOPS BEING A PLAN.** It now owes D2/D3's three tones · the editor note wording · M-RP6.6 ConnStats row-swap · M-RP-FOCUS · **Send-as-icon — itself blocked on a verified glyph, since `icons.ts` holds 17 and none is a send glyph and D-108 forbids fabricating a Material `d` path.** Either take it soon or split out the parts that are ready.

→ CLAUDE.md PLAY · `docs/ROADMAP.md` v5.30. **No new D** — the kind-4 sanitiser will want one, and it is **Joe's to mint** when M-RP-PROCESSOR-RENDER locks.

**WHAT THE MILESTONE DID.** The client already **loaded** the user's substitution rules (`app_client.svelte:537`) and had **no screen to edit them and no input that applied them** — a subsystem complete at both ends and connected in the middle to nothing. **🔑 THE FINDING THAT MATTERS MOST IN THIS ENTRY, AND IT IS NOT OURS.** Joe opened the app, typed, and reported *"`->` doesn't work."* Grounded keystroke-by-keystroke against the shipped build:

| typed | result | |
|---|---|---|
| `-->` | **`‒>`** | ❌ **BROKEN** |
| `<--` | `←` | ✅ |
| `:)` `<3` `:(` `--` | 🙂 ❤️ 🙁 `‒` | ✅ |
| `->` | `->` | not a rule — correct |

**`-->` IS UNREACHABLE BY TYPING.** The seed holds **both** `--` → `‒` and `-->` → `→`; typing `-` `-` completes the **shorter** rule immediately, so the `>` lands after a figure dash and the longer rule can never fire. `<--` survives for the mirror reason — `<-` is **not** a rule, so nothing fires early. ⇒ **GENERAL PRINCIPLE, now named: A RULE WHOSE PROPER PREFIX IS ALSO A RULE IS UNREACHABLE BY SEQUENTIAL TYPING.** `transform.ts:60` lints **convergence** (the `a aa` case) and lints **nothing** for prefix-reachability — which is why validation passes `-->` happily: it is not *invalid*, it is *unreachable*.

**⚠️ AND THE REASON NOBODY CAUGHT IT IS A METHOD DEFECT, NOT AN ATTENTION DEFECT. EVERY AUTOMATED PROBE ACROSS ALL THREE LEGS SET THE TEXTAREA VALUE WHOLESALE** — one `value` assignment plus one dispatched `input` — so `-->` always arrived **as a complete string** and always matched. *A live edit-side transformer is a function of the INPUT SEQUENCE, not of the final string, and a probe that skips the sequence cannot see a class of defect that only exists in the sequence.* Both seats did this, with positive controls, on V-B1 and on the Chat re-drive. **🔑 THREE LEGS OF DISCIPLINED VERIFICATION, AND THE DEFECT NEEDED A HUMAN TYPING FOR TWO MINUTES.** → **N-154.** *This is the sharpest vindication of §7's "judged by Joe live" the arc has produced, and it arrived in the one milestone where §7 had been left undischarged through all three legs.*

**🔒 THE SEED FIX IS JOE'S, AND HIS VERSION IS BETTER THAN CHAT'S.** Chat proposed dropping `--` → `‒` along with the long arrows. **Joe corrected it: shorten the arrows instead** — `-->` → `->`, `<--` → `<-` — *"we said that we change `-->` to `->` because of `--`; the same with `<--`."* Final set: **`-> → | <- ← | :) 🙂 | <3 ❤️ | :( 🙁 | -- ‒`.** **Six rules, same count, nothing lost.** ***Chat's version over-corrected: the defect was never `--` itself, it was that `--` is a PROPER PREFIX of `-->`. Shorten the arrow and the prefix relation vanishes, because `-` alone is not a rule.*** Verified across the whole set — no rule is a proper prefix of any other — and corroborated by measurement rather than reasoning alone: all four existing 2-character rules fire correctly today, and `<--` reached `←` **precisely because** `<-` was not a rule to fire early, which is the same shape `<-` will now occupy.
