## Entry J-561 — M-RP-PROCESSOR-WIRE design lock: a remembered gate that was never a gate, and the config file that deletes the settings screen's data at every launch

**Date:** 2026-07-20 · **Seats:** Chat (grounding, design walk, runbook, records) · Joe (locks: B-narrow, the title, the leg order). **Design/records-only — NO CODE.** Runbook `tasks/M_RP_PROCESSOR_WIRE.md` v1.0 ACTIVE. Registry unchanged; no floor moved.

**🔑 THE FINDING THAT SETS THE MILESTONE'S SCOPE, AND NEITHER THE KICKOFF NOR J-560 KNEW IT: D-101 IS LIVE IN THE SHIPPING CLIENT.** `desktop.rs:677` calls `app::clean_slate_config()` at launch; `app.rs:414` removes `xgen-client_config.toml` and regenerates from seed. So the substitutions **write path works and the file is deleted at the next launch** — the editor's own note already says *"Changes apply this session; config resets on restart."* ***A settings screen for user-authored data, in front of a config file that is deleted at every launch, is the sharpest available instance of what D6 and D-065 exist to prevent — and it would have shipped looking finished.*** J-560 filed the write-path question as OPEN (*"the difference between one milestone and two"*); grounding answered it in the harder direction — the write path **exists and is tested** (`desktop.rs:421` → `app.rs:271`, round-trip / error / clearing tests), and the problem was never the write, it was the wipe.

**⚠️ THE SEVENTH SELF-CONTRADICTION ON THIS ARC, ALL SEVEN CHAT'S — AND THE FIRST TO CHANGE WHAT JOE DECIDED TO DO NEXT.** The J-560 kickoff asserted *"M-RP-SETTINGS is gated on J-513, and the processor unblocks it rather than following it"*, and recommended Joe reorder his round on that basis. **It is false.** `ROADMAP.md` L931: Leg A ✅ J-535 · Leg B ✅ J-537 · **Leg C CLOSED J-540 → the SETTINGS arc is CLOSED**, with D-B → **D-120 minted** (`DECISIONS.md:4452`). J-513 was decided at J-534 and minted at J-540; it was **never** waiting on a second `settingsComponent`. **The prior seat did not misread the ROADMAP — it never read it**, carrying the gate from an older memory of the arc and writing it into J-560, the CLAUDE.md PLAY block, `ROADMAP.md` L804 and the kickoff. ***The previous six were documents disagreeing with themselves or with the code: expensive, but they cost rework. This one cost a decision.*** **The lesson is NOT "check the ROADMAP" — it is that a remembered gate is not a gate, and that a recommendation about SEQUENCING is the highest-leverage place an ungrounded premise can sit, because it is acted on before anything downstream can catch it.** The "one instance is a special case, two is a pattern" argument is **dead**; the `Text Processing` row is a **second tenant of a closed mechanism**, corroboration for D-120 at best, and D-120 does not need it. Corrected in all three places.

**GROUNDED, NOT INHERITED (J-560's processor findings re-verified by grep, with a positive control on the file list first).** All held: `composer-panel.svelte` has **zero** `processor`/`substitution` mentions · `textarea.svelte` is processor-READY (`:24`/`:28`, `...rest` `:52`, `{...rest}` `:73`) · `app_client.svelte:537` already loads the rules · the editor is sampler-only (`plugins/registry.ts:100` says so in writing). ⇒ ***The client loads your substitution rules, has no screen to edit them, and no input that applies them.***

**🔑 THE CRASH PATH I WENT LOOKING FOR DOES NOT EXIST, AND THE REASON IS THE MITIGATION.** `processor.ts:38` calls `assertSafeRules` at **render time** and **throws** on an invalid untrusted set — which reads like a crash surface for a persisted-and-gone-bad rules file. It is not: `store.svelte.ts:setRules` validates as Tier-2 and **fails safe to empty** while still stashing the raw text in `_source`, so `substitutions.rules` is always a validated set. **⚠️ But the failure it DOES have is the one persistence creates:** a bad rules file **silently disables every substitution**, explained only by a `console.warn` stripped from release builds. Under D-101 this was near-impossible (seed-fresh every launch); under persistence a stale or hand-edited file survives into every launch and quietly does nothing. **The surface for it already exists and is free** — `_source` is set on reject as well as success and the editor seeds from it with live inline validation, so the user opens Settings ▸ Text Processing and sees their own text **with the reason it was refused**. It has simply never been reachable in the client. → **verification leg V-C3, not an assertion.**

**🔒 JOE LOCKED B-NARROW, WITH E ON THE TABLE.** Four options were put with both D-121 lenses stated per option: **A** live-only labelled · **B-narrow** stop wiping user-owned content · **C** persist and keep wiping (*full editor, real write, edits die at reload* — no reason to pick it) · **E** move `[substitutions]` to its own store beside `xgen-client_uistate.json`. **E's user-visible outcome is IDENTICAL to B-narrow** — no difference a person could perceive — at meaningfully higher cost (new file, new load/write path, both Tauri commands repointed, one-time migration); it was named explicitly **so Joe chose B-narrow rather than defaulting into it**, and it remains available later as the tidier home without reversing anything.

**🔑 THE FRAMING IS THE DECISION'S REAL CONTENT: NOT AN EXEMPTION FROM D-101, A CORRECTION OF A MIS-FILING.** Chat's first draft called the carve-out *"a partial retirement of a Joe-locked discipline"*; grounded, the project had **already drawn this exact line in writing** — `app.rs:290–291`: *"NOT config: the UI-state store is the project's first deliberately persistent user-facing state, so it is NOT touched by D-101 clean-slate-on-start."* **The discriminator there was never "this section is special" — it was persistent user-facing state vs. config.** `ClientConfig` holds five sections; four are machine and deployment config, and **`substitutions` is the only one whose content a human authors** (`app.rs:69` — *"user-owned text-substitution pairs"*). ⇒ **The sentence is "user-owned content was mis-filed into the config file, and D-101 wipes config files."** *Load-bearing, because it keeps D-101 crisp — config wiped whole and undiminished — and stops this becoming a precedent for arbitrary per-section exemptions later. Whether Joe is punching a hole in a discipline or correcting a mis-filing are different questions and deserve different answers.*

**🔑 AND THE CODE SHAPE B-NARROW NEEDS IS ALREADY THE CODE SHAPE THAT IS THERE.** `clean_slate_config` is **already gated on `config_path.exists()`** so a genuine first run is left untouched (`clean_slate_leaves_first_run_untouched`, `app.rs:6555`) — **and that gate is exactly the J-438 discriminator**: no config → first run seeds the starter pack; config with an **empty** rules string → preserved empty → **cleared pairs stay cleared**. Leg C adds a capture and a re-inject inside an existing gate; it does not add a gate.

**🔒 J-438 SEED-ONCE RESUMES FOR THE PRESERVED SECTION — RECORDED AS CHOSEN, NOT DISCOVERED.** With Leg C, cleared pairs stop reappearing. Correct behaviour — a user who deletes a rule expects it to stay deleted — **but a behavioural change, written down as intended with its own verification leg (V-C2) so it cannot surface later as a surprise.** D-101 is otherwise unretired; the other four sections stay ephemeral by design.

**DECISIONS TAKEN UNDER THE GRANT, BOTH WITH "NO USER-FACING IMPACT" STATED PLAINLY (D-121: a legal and expected answer).** ① **The composer writes `processor(substitutions.rules)` with NO options object** — the `trusted` default is already `false` (`processor.ts:33`) and the store has already validated as Tier-2, so behaviour is identical either way; the cost argument decides it, and ***an explicit `trusted: false` is a worse artifact than an absent one: it advertises a knob that must never be turned.*** (The kickoff's premise was half right — the sampler **does** pass `trusted: true`, `app_sampler.svelte:586`.) ② **The persist seam lives on the `$common` store**, filled once by the shell beside the existing read at `app_client.svelte:537` — because `settings-dialog.svelte:193–195` mounts `<C />` **prop-less and generic by design** and `substitutions-editor` takes a host-injected `onApply` it cannot supply itself under W-3, so **mounted as-is it type-checks, renders, and silently never persists.** Widening the mount would change D-120's contract for one tenant; a shell wrapper is structurally impossible from `$common`. **`onApply` is NOT removed** — it is the sampler's live-only channel (D-097/W-8).

**🔒 TITLE LOCKED BY JOE: `M-RP-PROCESSOR-WIRE — the Text Processing row, composer wiring, and rule persistence`.** The fuller title was taken deliberately: with B-narrow, Leg C is a **Rust persistence change**, and "WIRE" alone would hide that from whoever reads the ROADMAP in three months. *The naming rule exists precisely so Joe can object before it ships.* **Leg order C → A → B, Joe's delegation on a question left open:** Leg C is the only leg with a Rust floor and the only one whose absence makes the other two **ship a promise we break** — building it last would mean A+B exist for a window in exactly the state this entry opens by rejecting.

**⚠️ FOUR KICKOFF CLAIMS CHECKED BECAUSE THE PRIOR SEAT FLAGGED THEM AS ITS OWN AND UNVERIFIED. All four hold; ONE IS MATERIALLY WIDER THAN STATED.** Svelte three-version split confirmed **from the lockfiles** (client **5.55.5** · node **5.55.5** · sampler **5.56.4** — `package.json` reads `^5` in all three, the **J-497 range trap**, avoided) · N-144's four latent files still latent (`color-picker`, `shelf-face`, `shelf`, `region-tile` — each 1 comment-`<style>`, 0 real style blocks) · M-RP-SKIN's D2/D3 debt real (`send-status.svelte:47`, `composer-panel.svelte:47`, `skin.css:2994`) · **`core`'s prop-less `Record<string, Component>`: SIX live declaration sites, not the two named** — `message.svelte:56` · `message-stream.svelte:62` · `mounts.ts:52` · `region-node.svelte:44` · `region-shell.svelte:49` · `:60`, with `send-status.svelte:36` already documenting it in a comment. ***The scope had been asserted from the files someone happened to have open rather than from a grep — the same shape as J-560 §1.4, one session later, and the reason that milestone is not being sized off "two files".*** Whether all six are defects is that milestone's Phase-0 question, not this one's.

**RUNBOOK DISCIPLINE APPLIED TO CHAT'S OWN OUTPUT.** §5's file list was built **by grep and re-read against the code before hand-over**, and names `plugins/registry.ts` explicitly — *the file J-560's §5 omitted, without which the composer would never have mounted at all.* §9 requires a **positive control on every probe that gates a conclusion**. §8 is to be written **last**, and re-read rather than appended to if the work moves (N-143).

**🔑 THE THREE NOTES, ALL FROM MISSED PREDICTIONS.** **N-147 — a plugin descriptor has TWO readers**, so a new region widget's registry delta is never just its own ids: +9 = 3 composer widget ids **+ 6 plugin-list row ids**. **The J-541 lesson recurring, to the seat that recorded it** — *knowing a descriptor has two readers is not the same as remembering it while predicting a number*; arithmetic agreement afterwards (143−134=9) is a check, not a derivation. **N-148 — the registry breathes on a FIFTH axis, the ECHO COUNT** (**143 → 235 with 29 echoes → 143 EXACT**); the exact return is the evidence the store leaks nothing, and **the new quiescent baseline is 143** — a baseline quoted without its echo count is now under-specified. **N-149 — a vite module count can move by REACHABILITY, not new files:** the 7th module is **`textarea.svelte`, existing `core` code with not one new line**, pulled into the graph because **the composer is its first client-side consumer** — proven by bundle probe with positive controls, not inferred from the difference.

**⚠️ ONE LOCK UNMET, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED, FLAGGED NOT ABSORBED — AND JOE ACCEPTED THE DEVIATION.** **Lock #10 (auto-scroll on your own send) FAILS:** scrolled to top, sent, `scrollTop` stayed 0, `stuckToBottom:false`, only a pill appeared. **`message-stream` applies its no-yank rule — correct for INBOUND — to the user's OWN send**, and exposes no scroll handle (`atBottom` is internal `$state`); R5 and R6 are separate tiles, so no cross-widget DOM route exists. **User-visible:** *you scroll up to re-read, type a reply, press Enter — your message drops to a bottom you cannot see, and its send-status is on the row you cannot see.* Rare, **but exactly the moment ambiguity costs most**; the common case (composing at the bottom) works free. **Cost of fixing inside D2: a `core` change to a shipped CDP-verified component, which would make the registry delta unreadable inside a `$common` milestone (the M-RP6.1k dialog-footer lesson).** → **JOE ACCEPTED THE DEVIATION; filed as `M-RP-COMPOSER-SCROLL` — auto-scroll on the user's own send.** *An unmet lock left undecided across milestones becomes permanent by default, because nobody reopens a closed one.*

**⚠️ `send-status` GETS NO `CLIENT_PLUGINS` ROW — RECORDED AS THE REVERSIBLE DEFAULT, NOT AS A JOE DECISION.** Clair deliberately left it undecided rather than pick. Chat's recommendation, given only afterwards: **no row** — the discriminator across the registry is *does the user have something to decide*; Grid Backdrop earns a row (which backdrop), Text Processing would (its rules), **`send-status` has nothing to decide — it either tells the truth about your message or it does not, and §3's lock says it must.** Listing it invites *"can I turn this off?"* where the answer is permanently no; `registry.ts:100` already carries the widget-shaped-but-unlisted precedent (`substitutions-editor`, `entity-context-menu`). **⚠️ Joe's "both yes" was ambiguous on this item because Chat had given NO recommendation at the moment he answered** — so it is recorded as **what shipped and what is reversible**, not as a lock. *The J-559 lesson applied at the cheap end: ask before writing the record, not after.*

**FOUR RULE-6 FLAGS FROM CLAIR, TWO OF THEM AGAINST THE RUNBOOK.** ① **§5's file list is INCOMPLETE** — it omits `plugins/registry.ts`, **without which the composer never mounts at all**, and *"mount R6 in app_client"* is the generation-stale anchor N-116/J-541 already corrected once. ② **§11 item 2 is STALE** — it says *"§3 is unresolved… do not pick"* while §3's own header reads **RESOLVED BY JOE**. ***The J-499/J-548/J-553/J-556/J-558 class again: a document disagreeing with ITSELF, findable only by reading it whole — and the sixth on this arc, all Chat's.*** ③ **`core`'s `widgets?: Record<string, Component>` types every socket tenant as prop-less** — **the SAME root cause M-RP-TYPECHECK fixed in `registry.ts`, still live in `message.svelte` / `message-stream.svelte`**, and **the gate caught it on first run**. Fixed on her side (`localId` optional — honest, since `WidgetMount.props` is `Record<string, unknown>` and nothing can guarantee delivery); **the `core` fix FLAGGED, NOT FOLDED IN.** ④ the `send-status` row, above. **Lock #8's head-marker wording widened to cover own sends** (*"…including your own…"*) — required by the lock, distinct from the latch lift.

**🔑 AND A QUESTION OF JOE'S FOUND A WHOLE SUBSYSTEM WIRED TO NOTHING.** He asked whether the composer used a new component or the already-authored one with the text processor. **Answer: it reuses `$core/…/textarea.svelte` (which is why N-149's 7th module appeared) — but the PROCESSOR IS NOT WIRED TO IT.** Grounded: `composer-panel.svelte` contains **zero** mentions of `processor`/`substitutions`; `textarea.svelte` is **processor-READY by design** (*"ready, not containing"* — D-065 — forwarding `{...rest}` at `:73`); **`app_client.svelte:537` ALREADY LOADS the user's rules** via `invoke('get_substitutions')`; and `substitutions-editor.svelte` exists but is mounted **only in the sampler**. ***So the client can load your substitution rules, has no screen to edit them, and no input that applies them — a subsystem complete at both ends and connected in the middle to nothing.*** **Chat's first framing was WRONG and Joe corrected it:** Chat separated "the substitutions feature" from "the text processor" — but **`clamp.ts` is literally *text-processor KIND 3*** and **D-099 defines the text processor as ONE architecture: two engines × four rule-kinds.** Substitutions is **kind 1 of four**, not a different layer. **Chat's safety objection also collapsed on grounding:** it argued against plugin status because disabling would kill the numeric guard — **but `plugin-list.svelte:91` greys the toggle for built-ins (`disabled: !isCustom`, *"Built-in — cannot be disabled"*, W-13), so a `system` row has NO disable button and the hazard does not exist.** → **direction: ONE row, `Text Processing`, `kind: 'system'` · `surface: 'none'` · no `component` · `settingsComponent: SubstitutionsEditor`** — the first row that is **purely a settings surface** (GridPlate minus the component). **🔒 AND IT RESOLVES J-513 BY EVIDENCE:** it becomes the **SECOND `settingsComponent`**, and it is the very component cited as the precedent for component-per-plugin over the declarative `settings_schema`. *One instance is a special case; two is a pattern* — so **the processor is not a tail-end item, it is what UNBLOCKS M-RP-SETTINGS**, and doing it afterwards would mean doing that milestone twice. **[❌ RETRACTED AT J-561 — THIS SENTENCE AND THE ARGUMENT CARRYING IT ARE FALSE, AND THIS RETRACTION COMPLETES THE THREE-PLACE CORRECTION (PLAY block · ROADMAP L804 · here). M-RP-SETTINGS WAS ALREADY CLOSED when this was written — ROADMAP L931: Leg A ✅ J-535 · Leg B ✅ J-537 · Leg C CLOSED J-540, D-B → D-120 minted (DECISIONS.md:4452). J-513 was decided at J-534 and minted at J-540; it was NEVER waiting on a second `settingsComponent`. The `Text Processing` row is a second TENANT of a closed mechanism — corroboration for D-120 at best, and D-120 does not need it. The seat that wrote this did not misread the ROADMAP; IT NEVER READ IT, carrying the gate from an older memory of the arc and then RECOMMENDING JOE REORDER HIS ROUND on the strength of it. Seventh self-contradiction on the arc, all seven Chat's, and the first to change a decision rather than merely cost rework. 🔑 The lesson is NOT "check the ROADMAP": a remembered gate is not a gate, and a recommendation about SEQUENCING is where an ungrounded premise does the most damage, because it is acted on before anything downstream can catch it.]**

**🔒 THE WIRING POLICY, JOE-LOCKED, WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIELDS THAT NEED IT EXIST.** **Default OFF everywhere; plug in only where it matters.** Enforced at **TWO** gates, not one: **① the component must FORWARD `{...rest}`** — only `converter-field`, `number` and `textarea` do; **`password-field` and `textfield` do NOT, so processing them is structurally impossible** — and **② the consumer must opt in per call site.** *An XGID, a token or a password silently rewritten by a user's own substitution rule would be a real harm, and the design refuses it at the component level rather than trusting every future call site to remember.* **Measured: the ENTIRE client+common tree has TWO text-input call sites** — `composer-panel:94` (**plug in**) and `substitutions-editor:98` (**NEVER — processing the textarea where you author substitution rules is a feedback loop: typing `:)` into the rule list rewrites the rule you are writing**). **Chat's refinement to Joe's wording, accepted: COMPOSING vs CONFIGURING** — *composing is prose written in flow where the transformation is visible and correctable as it happens; configuring is a value stored and reused, where the rewrite lands silently and nobody is watching* — plus a **third, stronger category: values that must round-trip BYTE-EXACT**, which is a correctness rule and not a preference.

**🟢 NEXT: M-RP-SETTINGS, WITH THE TEXT PROCESSOR AS A LEG** (it unblocks J-513 rather than waiting on it) — the composer wiring is **one line**, the row ~12. **⚠️ OPEN BEFORE IT SCOPES: does `get_substitutions` have a WRITE path on the Rust side?** Without one an in-client editor renders and applies but **cannot persist**, and the user's edits die at reload — the difference between one milestone and two. **THEN the small filed items**, with **`core`'s `Component` typing taken early** (the last live instance of a root cause already fixed once). **DEBT NAMED, NOT DEFERRED SILENTLY:** M-RP-SKIN now also owes D2/D3's provisional appearance (send-status's three tones) · **N-144's four latent files are still one `<style>` block from breaking the gate** · M-RP-A11Y's 34 warnings · `M-RP-COMPOSER-SCROLL`. → runbook v1.1 COMPLETED · ROADMAP v5.26 · notes v1.4 · **N-147 · N-148 · N-149**. **No new D.**

## Entry J-559 — D-121 locked, and the first recommendation examined under it reversed itself: two latches, one name, and a composer that would have greyed out on the conversation you were reading

**Date:** 2026-07-19 · **Seat:** Chat (D2 re-ground + design walk + runbook authoring; D-121 authored). **NO CODE.** Runbook `tasks/M_RP6_3_LEG_D2_COMPOSER_ECHO.md` **v1.0 ACTIVE**. `tasks/M_RP6_3_COMPOSER.md` → **v2.0** (re-ground annotations). `tasks/M_RP_TYPECHECK_GATE.md` → **v1.2** (a tick corrected). **D-121 pushed at `f993c39`.**

**🔒 D-121 — EVERY QUESTION AND RECOMMENDATION LEADS WITH TWO NAMED LENSES: user-visible impact PER OPTION, then resource cost.** Architectural elegance, symmetry and implementation convenience are **tertiary** — recorded, never leading. **⚠️ ADDITIONAL LENSES, NOT A REPLACEMENT:** D-065, D6, N-091, D-110/D-111, D-067, the no-anonymity core and GDPR discipline stand **undiminished**; a collision goes to Joe **unresolved and named as a collision**, never silently traded. **"No user-facing impact" is a legal and expected answer** — *a manufactured UX rationale is worse than none, because it launders an internal preference as a user's interest.* **Joe's reason, recorded because it governs the application:** he locks architecture but **cannot independently verify most of the technical claims put to him**, so these two axes are the ones he CAN judge — stating them is what makes a recommendation **checkable rather than trusted blind**. *The lens is a trust mechanism, not a philosophy of design.* **Chat's boundary written into the decision:** resource cost is **measurable and must be measured, not estimated**; **user experience is only ever INFERRED**, since Claude never observes a user — so on many such calls **Joe is the better judge**, which is exactly why they are stated for him rather than acted on silently.

**🔑 AND THE RULE PAID FOR ITSELF INSIDE THE SAME SESSION, ON CHAT'S OWN RECOMMENDATION.** Asked where the D2 composer should get its room, Chat recommended **reading the selection bus**, on a sound architectural argument (*do not lift a deliberate component-local workaround into a shared store*). **Joe asked what it would do to the user's experience.** Grounding it then produced the finding: **`stream-panel.svelte:55` latches the ROOM** (`latchedRoomId`, stale-latch guard → `effectiveRoomId` at `:68`, which the projection filters on at `:79`), while **`rooms-panel.svelte:23` latches the SPACE** (`latchedSpaceId`). ***Two latches, near-identical shape, different subjects — and "the latch" means whichever one you happen to be reading.*** A bus-reading composer therefore **greys itself out while the user is still looking at the conversation**, on ordinary navigation (click a Space in the tree → stream keeps showing room X because it is latched → composer refuses), **with nothing on screen explaining why.** **🔒 LOCKED: the composer SHARES R5's room latch, lifted into `$common`.** *The architectural argument was not wrong — it was answering a question that ranks below the one that decides. And it aimed at the wrong latch: the objection concerned R2's SPACE latch, which the lift does not touch.* **A third option — duplicate the latch logic in the composer — was rejected: it avoids editing a shipped component at the price of two copies of a rule that must agree forever, a D-067 surface whose drift produces exactly the divergence the decision exists to prevent.**

**🔒 Q2 — THE LEG B DEV BRIDGE STAYS, AND "NO USER-FACING IMPACT" WAS THE HONEST ANSWER.** `window.__XGEN_SEND__` is guarded by `import.meta.env.DEV` (`app_client.svelte:139`) and **verified absent from a real production build** — `__XGEN_SEND__`, `sendMessage` and `send_message` in **none** of the six bundle files, while `invoke`/`Messages`/`room` are present, so **the probe was positively controlled and not blind.** No user sees it either way; **decided on the internal axis and said so.** Kept because the composer calls `sendMessage()` directly (the bridge only wraps it, so nothing is duplicated) and because **it is the only way to drive the send path WITHOUT the composer** — i.e. to tell whether a fault is in the new UI or underneath it. **Removing it in the milestone that adds the UI removes the control exactly when it becomes useful.** ⚠️ Its repo reference count is **1 — its own definition** — because its callers are CDP evals living outside the tree: ***retiring on a reference count would delete something whose users the count cannot see.*** Retires at D3 close.

**⚠️⚠️ THE FINDING NEITHER QUESTION ASKED FOR: IN A RELEASE BUILD TODAY THE CLIENT CANNOT SEND A MESSAGE AT ALL.** `sendMessage()` is called from **exactly one place — the DEV bridge** — so the whole send path tree-shakes out of production. Nothing is broken (Leg B shipped the seam deliberately), but it sharpens what D2 is: **not "add a text box to an existing capability" but the milestone that makes sending exist for real users for the first time.**

**🔒 §3 RESOLVED BY JOE — OPTION B: D3 SHIPS WITH D2; D2 DOES NOT CLOSE ALONE.** Lock #6 gives send-status three visual states and **the widget that draws them is D3**, so a D2 rendering echoes without one puts a row on screen that **looks exactly like a delivered message and may have been `rejected` — refused by the node, never arriving, ever.** ***And it never self-corrects:*** author exclusion is by identity (`fanout.rs:303`), so the message never returns from the server — §9.11.2's *the real event never arrives*. **The echo is not a placeholder awaiting confirmation; it is the only record the message ever existed, and it asserts success purely by being there.** In an ordinary client a failed message eventually goes red or never gets its tick; **here nothing ever happens** — the row is finished, and one time in four it is finished wrong. **Why B rather than accepting the gap: XGen has no users, so the exposure is not strangers** — it is that **D2 would close as an honest milestone while its most likely observed state is the lie** (`failed` fires on any outage, routine in development), and **every verification in that window would run against a UI that cannot report when a send did not land** — *an odd instrument with which to debug a send path.* **Resource cost: none** — B removes an option rather than adding work. Fallback if ever separated: a minimal honest failure signal in D2. **No build that can send may render all four outcomes identically.**

**🔒 §3.1 RESOLVED BY JOE — LOCK #7 NARROWED FOR D2, AND THE NARROWING IS RECORDED AS SUCH.** §9.11.3 lock #7 reads *"`timed_out` → retry only behind an explicit warning"*. **D2 offers no retry affordance on `timed_out` at all**: `failed` retries freely (never reached the wire, and the common outage path), `rejected` no retry as locked, `timed_out` honest copy and **no button**. **Reason — it is the ONLY status where a UI affordance can produce an irreversible, identity-bearing wire effect:** one click under uncertainty can place **a second copy of the sentence on the federated network, permanently, attributed to the user's identity**, because the node may already be holding the first. **Not building it is reversible; shipping it and letting the habit form is not** — and the decision is far better made once a user can actually SEE the three states, which is D3. **Resource cost: negative.** ⚠️ **This narrows a Joe-locked item; Joe may reinstate the full lock at any time.**

**⚠️ HOW §3.1 WAS DECIDED, RECORDED BECAUSE IT TOUCHES THE NO-ANONYMITY CORE AND BECAUSE CHAT GOT THE PROCESS WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS.** Joe's *"go as you recommend"* covered **both** open questions — §3 **and** lock #7. A later Chat turn, finding §3.1 recorded without a visible recommendation preceding it, **retracted the lock across all four records** on the reasoning that a delegation cannot cover an identity-bearing item and that Chat had put Joe's name on its own decision. **Joe corrected it: the delegation was intended for both, and it stands.** *Restored.* **The query was right to make and the answer was yes** — ***a decision Joe makes by delegating is still Joe's decision***, and D-121's "collisions go to Joe unresolved" is satisfied by Joe having already ruled, not violated by him ruling briefly. **The cost of the round trip was churn in four records; the cost of NOT asking, had the delegation not covered it, would have been a fabricated lock on the no-anonymity core.** *That asymmetry is why the question gets asked even when the answer turns out to be yes.*

**⚠️ THE FROZEN TURN, RECORDED BECAUSE THE MECHANISM IS NEW AND WILL RECUR.** The turn that produced this entry, the runbook edits, the §9.11 annotations and the v1.2 correction **wrote all six files to disk and then lost its chat output entirely** — the UI froze and the text vanished. **The next Chat turn had no memory of the work but the work was on the disk**, so it read its own uncommitted output as an intruder's and raised an alarm. ***The chat transcript and the working tree diverged, and the WORKING TREE was the truth.*** Joe supplied the missing half (*"you froze and the whole text disappeared"*). **Consequences, both directions:** a lost turn is **not** a turn that did nothing — on resume, `git status` and file mtimes come before any assumption that nothing happened; and work recovered this way is **reviewed as another seat's**, never trusted as remembered — the §9.11 annotations and the v1.2 tick correction were re-verified line by line against the source and **both were sound.** ⚠️ **But the same posture also produced the §3.1 over-correction above**: reviewing recovered work as a stranger's is right for *facts*, which can be re-measured, and **wrong for the record of what Joe SAID**, which cannot — only Joe can confirm that. *Re-verify the claims; ask about the authorisations.*

**RE-GROUND OF §9.11 (the "design already locked" claim CHECKED, not inherited — and it HOLDS).** Joe-locked, grounded the same day, prerequisites genuinely closed: **D1 CLOSED** (J-553, `53dab37`; the fix is live — `desktop.rs:363` calls `await_send_outcome(reply_rx, SEND_QUEUE_TIMEOUT)`, and `SEND_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` is **DERIVED** from `SEND_ACK_TIMEOUT + PENDING_SWEEP_INTERVAL + 5` with a test asserting it outlasts the drain's worst case) and **M-RP6.9 CLOSED** (J-556), so §9.11.6's order D1 → M-RP6.9 → **D2** → D3 is satisfied. **But FOUR references had gone stale and one section was in the wrong tense** — all annotated in place at the head of §9.11 (v2.0): `resident.rs:706`→`743–761` · `fanout.rs:305`→`303`/`1067`/`1116` · `desktop.rs:331`→`346` · `message.svelte:71`→`:56`/`:63` · and *"`bodyExtras` declared but never rendered"* **SUPERSEDED — M-RP6.9 built it.** **⚠️ §9.11.4 still read *"live at HEAD"* about a bug D1 closed** — marked ✅ CLOSED / read-in-past-tense with an explicit **"do not re-fix it"**, *because the implementer reads §9.11 as her design source and a runbook that sends her to a fixed defect costs a leg.*

**⚠️ A TICK OF CHAT'S OWN, CORRECTED (M-RP-TYPECHECK v1.2).** J-558's DoD ticked *"every §5 floor predicted then measured"* while naming only cargo, npm and vite. **§5 also lists catalogue 419 and client registry 134, and neither was measured** — they were judged unaffected because the edits were type-level, **which is a judgement, not a measurement, on a milestone that touched `region-shell.svelte` (the live grid renderer) and `mutate.ts`.** Both have since been driven and **BOTH HOLD: registry 134** (`snapshot()` keys and `ids` agree, all unique) and **catalogue 419** with `count === unique === domCount`. ***The numbers were right; the tick was not earned when it was made.*** ⚠️ And the first catalogue probe returned **`domCount: 0`** because the selector was `[data-xgen-id]` where the real attribute is **`data-debug-id`** — **the fifth clean-looking nothing of the session**, alongside `--ignore` measuring a run that never happened, `ReadAllBytes` on a relative path, `IndexOf` returning −1 into a `Substring` that printed the file head, and `Select-String` on a bundle path that did not exist. ***Only the positive control distinguishes "the bad thing is absent" from "nothing happened".***

**RUNBOOK v1.0 SELF-CHECKED BEFORE HAND-OVER, and the check caught its own defect:** all seven code references verified against the source rather than asserted (`stream-panel:55`/`:68` · `rooms-panel:23` · `app_client:139`/`:532` · `desktop.rs:363` · `message.svelte:63`), **and a numbering collision found** — a second `§7` inserted before `§4`, resolved to `§3.1` with a pointer left where `§7` used to be **so the gap does not read as lost content.** The DoD is split `IMPLEMENTER` / `[CHAT]` — **copied correctly this time, because M-RP-TYPECHECK's version got it wrong and Clair caught it (J-558).**

**CARRIED, NOT RE-DERIVED:** outage send latency is **re-anchor + `SEND_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`**, measured **19 155 ms** = **3.143 s failed re-anchor + 16.013 s bounded wait** (the bound accurate to 13 ms) — **≈19 s is NOT a bug in the bound**, and D2's lifecycle guard should normally stop the call reaching that path at all. **NOT D2's:** multi-device self-visibility (*you type on the laptop and the sentence does not exist on the phone — not "until reload", at all*), which closes at **M-RP6.4** under the binding constraint that **backfill reads the EVENT STORE and must return the requesting identity's OWN events** — *if it were ever built by replaying fan-out the hole would silently persist* · own-row ordering (`accepted` carries no authoritative timestamp).

**🟢 NEXT-ACTIVE = M-RP6.3 Leg D2 — R6 composer + echo store, implementation from runbook v1.0 (Clair), legs D2-A→E, closing WITH D3.** → `tasks/M_RP6_3_LEG_D2_COMPOSER_ECHO.md` v1.0 · `M_RP6_3_COMPOSER.md` v2.0 · `M_RP_TYPECHECK_GATE.md` v1.2 · **D-121** · ROADMAP v5.25 · **no new N**.

## Entry J-558 — M-RP-TYPECHECK CLOSED: the gate caught, on its first run, a defect that had already shipped and passed CDP — and it corrected two of its own runbook's claims on the way

**Date:** 2026-07-19 · **Seats:** Clair (implementation, Legs A–D, 7 Rule-6 flags) · Chat (independent verification, floors, records). **Runbook `tasks/M_RP_TYPECHECK_GATE.md` v1.1 → `Status: COMPLETED`.**

**🔒 THE GATE EXISTS. `npm run check` in `ui/` → `svelte-check` — 0 errors / 34 warnings / 15 files, exit 0.** N-138 **GRADUATED**. The floor is **two numbers, both quoted, always**.

**🔑 THE FINDING, AND IT IS THE WHOLE JUSTIFICATION FOR THE MILESTONE (→ N-144).** The baseline's separator family was **not** the version artifact J-557 predicted. A **literal `<style>` tag inside a `//` comment in `<script>`, in a file that ALSO has a real style block**, makes **svelte2tsx** — the type-gate's transformer, **not** the compiler — read the script as never closed. That strips the default export and **fails every importer**, which is why `menu.svelte` and `status-bar.svelte` reported *"has no default export"* and pointed at the wrong file entirely. **Both conditions are required**, which is why `sb-cell.svelte` carries the identical empty `<style></style>` and never erred — the inconsistency looked like nondeterminism and was actually a second condition nobody had spotted. **Reproducible on the pinned 5.55.5.** `svelte.compile` accepts the file under both 5.55.5 and 5.56.6, 0 warnings. It bundles. It renders. **It was CDP-verified.** ***A defect every existing floor was structurally incapable of seeing is precisely what N-138 said the project had no way to catch — and the first run of the gate built to answer N-138 caught one, in already-shipped `core`.*** Latent set swept and counted: **4 in the gate's scope** (`color-picker` · `shelf-face` · `shelf` · `region-tile`) and **3 outside it** (`ui/client/src`, which the gate does not cover). **Deliberately NOT swept** — a warning comment was left in `separator.svelte` at the point of contact instead. *A sweep protects the four files that exist; a comment protects the ones not written yet.*

**FLOORS — EVERY ONE PREDICTED BEFORE DRIVING, EVERY ONE MEASURED, ALL SEEN.** cargo **1546 / 0 / 62 across 56 terminator lines — IDENTICAL** (case-sensitive failure grep clean; *identity is the DIRECT proof zero Rust landed, not a corroboration*) · npm **132** · vite **193 CLIENT / 170 sampler** — **and that pair IS V5**, the direct evidence that the new `ui/node_modules` did not perturb the three apps' resolution, which was §2.3's named risk · **svelte-check 0 / 34 / 15**. **Warnings did not move across the entire milestone (34 before, 34 after)** — itself evidence the fixes were type-level and behaviour-neutral (→ N-146, `M-RP-A11Y` filed).

## Entry J-556 — M-RP6.9 CLOSED: the verification designed to prove a silent failure proved a loud one, and "full reload" turned out never to have meant what every baseline on this arc relied on

**Date:** 2026-07-19 · **Seat:** Clair implemented from locked runbook v1.2→v1.4; Chat verified scope + records.
**Commit `528614e`, 10 files, +482/−61.** Runbook `tasks/M_RP6_9_BODY_EXTRAS.md` **v1.4 COMPLETED**, §8 written by Clair.
**Scope proven by `git show --stat`: ZERO `.rs`, ZERO node, ZERO `layout-default.ts`.**

**GATES — ALL SEEN, apps AND dev servers stopped.** `cargo test` **1546/0/62 across 56 terminator lines, IDENTICAL** — *which is the direct proof that zero Rust moved, not a corroboration of it.* `npm test` **114 → 132** (`mounts.test.ts` = **18 exactly**) · vite CLIENT **193 exact** — *the floor Chat predicted on purpose because an unpredicted client move on a sampler-only milestone reads exactly like scope leak; it landed on the nose* · sampler catalogue **419**, with `count === unique === domCount` · client registry **134 quiescent** after a full reload, empty store, no selection. **Sampler vite 170, NOT the predicted 171 — DECOMPOSED, NOT ADJUSTED** (§8.2), per the runbook's own binding: *a difference at drive time is EXPLAINED before it is adjusted.*

**🔑 V-7 CORRECTED ITS OWN PREMISE, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE BETTER RESULT.** §1.2 predicted a duplicate `mountKey` would make the registry **shrink silently** (`Map.set` overwrites; the loser's `unregister` deletes the survivor). **Measured: it is LOUD.** The app does not mount at all, registry **419 → 0**, error captured verbatim — `each_key_duplicate — duplicate key 'k-reg' at indexes 2 and 3`. **Svelte's keyed-`{#each}` guard fires UPSTREAM of the registry entirely.** **⚠️ §1.2 is NARROWED, NOT DISPROVEN, and the distinction is the finding:** the guard is **per each-block**, so two mounts in **different blocks** minting the same final id would still land silently in the `Map`. **What is proven is the case that matters — `mountKey`'s own most likely misuse fails loudly AND NAMES THE KEY.** *A verification that changes its own premise and then states precisely which part survived is worth more than one that confirms it.* **Strong result for D-2.**

**⚠️⚠️ THE FINDING THAT REACHES BACKWARDS THROUGH THE WHOLE ARC: "FULL RELOAD" NEVER MEANT WHAT EVERY BASELINE RELIED ON IT TO MEAN.** A vite dev server **outlived repeated app restarts and kept serving a poisoned module** — **and it reached Joe**, who saw an `each_key_duplicate` overlay **twice, without touching anything**. Grounded: **one** `const cid` on disk at line 111, overlay citing **line 129**, `vite build` **clean** — a ghost from an intermediate save during S-2a, and the dev server (**PID 30520**) survived **every** `xgen-sampler` kill-and-relaunch. **⇒ N-132's "full reload" must mean THE DEV SERVER IS GONE, not merely the Tauri window — and EVERY baseline on this arc (386 · 134 · 192 · 169) was read after an app restart ONLY.** *This does not invalidate those numbers; it means their PROVENANCE was weaker than every record claimed, on the single instrument the whole arc's verification rests on.* **It also RETRACTS an earlier "unexplained"** — a CDP endpoint dying while the process lived, which the parse error now explains. *An open item closed by a finding from a different milestone is the cheapest kind of debt repayment there is.*

**🔑 A SVELTE `<style>` BLOCK IS ONE VITE MODULE — MEASURED BY PROBE, NOT REASONED:** adding one moved 170 → 171, removing it returned 170. *Directly useful to every future floor prediction on this project, and half the reason §4's 171 was unreachable once deviation ⑨ collapsed two style blocks into skin tokens.* **The other half is that the prediction was made before Joe's late requests existed.**

**⚠️ N-109 OCCURRED INSIDE THE DOCUMENT THAT CITES N-109, AND CLAIR CAUGHT IT BY RE-READING RATHER THAN APPENDING.** §8 was written after the legs; **Joe's two late requests then falsified THREE of its claims** — sampler vite (172→170), deviation ⑤ (two style blocks that no longer exist), and §8.2's *"the error name is not captured"* (it had since been captured). All three corrected, **superseded reasoning kept where it still explains why the later change mattered.** *This is not irony — it is evidence the rule is about SEQUENCE, not vigilance.* **Transferable rule, narrow and cheap: WRITE THE CLOSE LAST, and if the work moves after it, RE-READ it rather than append to it.**

**🔑 THE THIRD RESOLVER COPY — CLAIR'S FINDING, THE RUNBOOK THEN FOLLOWED (deviation ①, recorded that way round deliberately).** §1.4 v1.0/v1.1 said *"written twice"*; **the real third was `region-shell.svelte:83`, the live grid backdrop shipped at M-RP-PLATE — character-identical bar the registry variable, and its OWN COMMENT said so:** *"the `message-stream` shape exactly"*. **⚠️ CHAT ASSERTED A COUNT IT HAD NEVER GROUNDED** — from the two files it happened to open, not from a grep — **the exact rule this project applies everywhere else, pointed the other way, one hour after applying it to Ms Design.** ***And this is a DIFFERENT and worse failure class than the other three runbook catches on this arc (J-499, J-548, J-553): those were documents disagreeing with THEMSELVES, findable by re-reading. This one was internally consistent and disagreed with THE CODEBASE. No amount of re-reading finds that. Only a grep does, and Chat did not run one.*** **Migrating two of three would have shipped a shared function AND left a private copy in the grid renderer — the ILLUSION of consolidation, worse than none.** **Verified at close: `${m.widgetId}-${i}` now appears EXACTLY ONCE in the live tree — `mounts.ts:57`, the D-2 fallback, which is the one place it is supposed to live.** Four call sites: `message.details` · `message.bodyExtras` · `message-stream.background` · `region-shell.background`. **`region-node.svelte:225` correctly NOT migrated** — a fourth grep hit and a different rule (single mount, inline guard, no list/key/filter), **named in §1.4 so the next reader does not re-derive why three of four moved.**

**S-2b's SEQUENCE EARNED ITS OWN STEP AND NOTHING BLANKED.** *J-499's lesson is not "be careful with the grid" — it is that if the centre blanks you must know WHICH swap did it.* V-2b ran **both halves**: render (backdrop mounted, registry 134, `backgroundMountCount` identical) **and DROP** (unknown `widgetId` ⇒ count falls, nothing throws, reverted) — *because "still mounted" proves the socket renders, not that W-13 still works THROUGH the new function, and the filter is exactly where a subtle difference would hide.*

**TEN DEVIATIONS, ALL NAMED (§8.3).** ① third copy (above) · ② `mountKey` at S-1 not S-5 · ③ `region-shell` passes **no `idPrefix`, deliberately** · ④ V-9 driven as a four-config A/B across reloads · ⑤ superseded by ⑨ · ⑥ swept a stale `message.svelte` header claim (N-109) · **⑦ Clair's OWN N-110 repeat, discarded BEFORE it entered the record** — *a deviation caught in flight and reported anyway is worth more than one that never happened* · ⑧ emoji in fixtures (**Joe corrected Clair's first pass — he wanted them in the STRIP, not the bodies**) · **⑨ both stubs' appearance relocated into `skin.css` as named tokens (Joe), which TOUCHES `fixture-widget.svelte` — the file S-4 designated the untouched CONTROL.** *The control is now STRONGER, not compromised: the twins are identical BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by hand-synced copy, and inertness was re-measured rather than assumed.* · ⑩ DEV warn on duplicate `mountKey` **considered and NOT built**, filed with its trigger.

**FILED, NOT BUILT.** **DEV warn on duplicate `mountKey`** — *Svelte already fails loudly and names the key; a second guard on a path that CANNOT pass silently is the unfed-branch mistake this project refuses.* **Trigger recorded: Svelte names `message.svelte` but not which row/descriptor — add it the first time that costs someone real time.** **⚠️ HARNESS GAP: `-Mode console` subscribes to `Runtime.consoleAPICalled` ONLY, so an UNCAUGHT EXCEPTION IS INVISIBLE TO IT** — 265 lines, **zero matches across a crash**. Workaround used (arm a collector first, trigger by HMR not reload) **routes around the gap; it does not close it.** *An instrument that reads clean during a crash is the N-139 family again — filed as a gap, not as a solved problem.*

**APPEARANCE — §7.4 DISCHARGED.** Joe judged live at 9422 and **approved**. Block stays **PROVISIONAL**, discharger **M-RP-SKIN**. **The chip at 14px in a 28px lane is half-empty BY CONSTRUCTION** (`--fixture-chip-pad-y: 0`) — **seen, approved, and documented IN THE SKIN BLOCK ITSELF so the next person to measure it does not "fix" it**, with the tuning order recorded: **raise the chip BEFORE settling the lane, or you fit `--msg-extras-lane` to a stub about to be replaced by a taller tap target.** *A provisional number that explains its own provisionality where it lives is the difference between a placeholder and a trap.*

**FENCE HELD, VERIFIED AT CLOSE BY CHAT.** No `ReactionDescriptor`, no wire shape, no store, no asset, no URL. **`--msg-extras-lane` at `:root` ONLY. ZERO `--xgen-` in `skin.css`. NO `[data-state]`/`[data-retry]` rule — those are Leg D3's**, so the fence held **through CSS**, which was the subtle way it could have leaked. **The real client renders 0 `.msg-body-extras`: nothing feeds it, exactly as §0 requires** (N-091/D-065).

**⚠️ NEW BASELINES FOR LEG D2/D3 — catalogue 419 · client registry 134 · npm 132 · vite 193 CLIENT / 170 sampler · cargo 1546/0/62 across 56 terminators.** **Read them after the DEV SERVER is gone, not just the app.**
**🟢 NEXT-ACTIVE = M-RP6.3 Leg D2 — R6 composer + echo store (`$common`).** Its locks are already waiting: the **C-4 amendment**, the **twelve user-facing locks**, and §9.11.8's **outage send latency = re-anchor + `SEND_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` ≈ 19 s, NOT the 16 s bound alone**. **This container is now the socket Leg D3's send-status widget mounts into.** Then **Leg D3**.

## Entry J-555 — M-RP6.9 appearance returns to Chat: a design lane that never reached the disk, and a proximity ratio that was measured in another codebase

**Date:** 2026-07-19 · **Seat:** Chat Claude · **Scope:** records + runbook §7 only, NO CODE.
**Deliverable:** `tasks/M_RP6_9_BODY_EXTRAS.md` **v1.1** (§7 rewritten). Mechanics untouched — **J-554 holds in full**. Gates untouched, not re-measured, and says so.

**WHAT HAPPENED.** Ms Design returned the M-RP6.9 appearance lane as COMPLETE and Joe-ratified, naming three artifacts in `skeleton/`. **None of them exist.** `git status --porcelain` **empty**; repo-wide grep for `msg-body-extras` / `msg-extras` / `--xgen-msg-extras-lane` **zero hits**; `ui/templates/skeleton/tokens.css` mtime **8 May 2026**, unmodified. HEAD was still the Phase-0 commit with nothing after it. *N-116 exactly — a filed sketch is not a built fact — and the reason the finding surfaced at all is that the record was grounded BEFORE it was written.* **⚠️ Had J-555 been written from the handback, the canonical chain would have asserted a delivered design lane that did not exist, and Clair would have been instructed to paste a CSS file that is not there.**

## Entry J-554 — M-RP6.9 Phase-0 LOCKED: the milestone's headline question was already answered at source, and the answer was neither of the two on offer

**Date:** 2026-07-19 · **Seat:** Chat Claude · **Scope:** design + records only, NO CODE.
**Deliverable:** `tasks/M_RP6_9_BODY_EXTRAS.md` v1.0 ACTIVE (locked runbook). Gates untouched.

**⚠️ THE QUESTION THE MILESTONE WAS INSERTED TO ANSWER IS ANSWERED BY READING, NOT BY BUILDING — AND THE FRAMING WAS A FALSE DICHOTOMY.** J-552 fenced it as *"three mounts on twenty rows is sixty new registered ids — or sixty COLLISIONS, depending on how `cid()` scopes, and WHICH ONE IS NOT KNOWN."* **It is neither. As HEAD stands it is sixty ZEROS.** `cid()` (`message.svelte:79`) is called with **hardcoded string literals only** — `'avatar'`, `'name'`, `'body'` — and mounts render `<W {...d.props} />` (`:167`) with **no `id` reaching them**. `fixture-widget.svelte` states the intent in its own header: it *"deliberately does NOT register … keeping the stub registration-free keeps the registry delta per message cell predictable."* **The socket has never been asked to mint an id, so it has never had the opportunity to collide.** ⇒ **No `core` defect. Nothing brought to Joe as one.**

**🔑 BUT THE ANSWER IS ONLY TRUE UNTIL THE REAL TENANT ARRIVES, WHICH IS EXACTLY WHY THE MILESTONE STILL EARNS ITS PLACE.** A reaction is interactive and animated ⇒ it **will** want to register. So the container must hand mounts a stable id **before** a tenant needs one — otherwise `envelope.ts:39` supplies `` `${typeClass}#${++ordinal}` ``, a **module-level counter, unstable across remounts**, against which **no baseline can be taken** (N-132's whole premise). *Joe's argument survives its own answer: a socket designed against a single static led would have shipped without ever discovering this.*

**⚠️ THE FINDING THAT OUTLIVES THE MILESTONE — A REGISTRY COLLISION SHRINKS THE COUNT AND SAYS NOTHING.** `debug.ts`: `registry` is a `Map`, `register()` is `.set()` ⇒ **a duplicate id silently overwrites, no warning, no throw**; and `unregister()` is `.delete(id)` on the action's `destroy` ⇒ **when the loser of a collision unmounts it deletes the SURVIVOR's entry too.** So a collision presents as the registry **going DOWN**, which is indistinguishable from a clean unmount and sits squarely in N-132's blind spot. *Every verify leg on this arc keys off a quiescent count; the failure mode of that instrument had never been characterised.* **The runbook makes this a MEASURED fact, not a read one (V-7): two mounts are deliberately given one `mountKey`, the count is watched to FALL, then reverted.** *A failure mode you have only reasoned about is not yet known to occur.*

**🔑 THE DEFECT THAT IS REAL, AND IT IS IN THE KEY.** `key: `${m.widgetId}-${i}`` — **index-composed, in BOTH sockets** (`message.svelte:73`, `message-stream.svelte:111`). `details` has only ever been handed a **static list**, so it has never bitten. Under runtime add/remove — the reaction case, exactly — removing mount 0 of `[A,B,C]` re-keys `B` from `B-1` to `B-0`, so **Svelte destroys and recreates every mount after the removal point**: state loss and an animation restart on every *unrelated* removal. **Invisible for a `<span>` stub; disqualifying for the strong consumer.** *This is the "paid twice" cost Joe predicted, found before either tenant paid it.* Second, quieter: resolution is `$derived` over `widgets[m.widgetId]` and re-derives on the **reference**, so a consumer mutating the registry object **in place** gets nothing — **the D-119 lesson (a `$state` `Set` does not react to `.add`/`.delete`) in a second costume**, written down so it is not rediscovered a third time.

**FIVE LOCKS TAKEN, NOT ASKED — Joe restated the grant mid-session: *"mine: appearance + architectural decisions; yours: anything else."*** These are container **mechanics**: no protocol, no wire shape, no store, no federation, no identity. **D-1 — the container supplies a stable `id`; the widget may ignore it** (`<W id={…} {...d.props} />`, props spread LAST so a consumer can override). *Passing `id` is not the container learning what its contents MEAN — `id` is this codebase's universal envelope contract, the same category as `props`.* Applied to **both** sockets; **measurably inert on `details` today** because `FixtureWidget` ignores it — **and that inertness is a VERIFICATION LEG (V-2), not an assumption.** **D-2 — `WidgetMount.mountKey?: string`, optional, falling back to `` `${widgetId}-${i}` ``**: one field fixes the Svelte keying churn **and** the id stability, for both sockets, **without inventing a `ReactionDescriptor` or any wire shape**; the fallback is **byte-identical to today's key**, so every existing mount keeps its current behaviour. **D-3 — `resolveMounts()` extracted to a pure tested `core` module** (`mounts.ts`): the logic is currently **written twice with zero tests** — `core`'s `resolve.ts`/`resolve.test.ts` are **layout**, unrelated — so `npm test` moves **for an honest reason rather than an invented one** (the kickoff's fourth Phase-0 question, answered yes with evidence). **D-4 — a tombstone drops `bodyExtras`, matching `details`**: the container **cannot** distinguish an attachment (must vanish with the body) from a reaction (arguably survives) — *the fence forbids it knowing* — so one rule, conservative direction, `bodyExtrasCount` forced to 0 (the J-479 `deleted → detailsCount:0` precedent). **FILED as reversible at M-RP-REACTIONS**, where the tenant is known: *recorded rather than silently settled.* **D-5 — `types.ts:67–69` corrected HERE, not at Leg D3**: the line still lists *send-status led* under `details`, it is wrong **now**, and D3 is two legs away — **the socket's doc-comment travels with the socket's build.**

**⚠️ A FLOOR PREDICTION THAT CHANGED BETWEEN THE WALK AND THE RUNBOOK, AND SAYS SO.** The design walk derived **≈412** for the sampler catalogue; the runbook derives **419**, because the fixture set gained a **second, deliberately REGISTERING stub** (`fixture-reg-widget.svelte`) — the instrument that turns §1.1's read answer into a measured one (V-6: 4 rows × 1 registering mount ⇒ **exactly 4 new ids**, all matching `…__m-<msgid>__x-<key>`). **Both numbers are arithmetic, not measurement (N-108), and a difference at drive time is to be EXPLAINED before it is adjusted.** *A floor that changes between two documents must say it changed, or the next reader cannot tell a revision from an error.*

**⚠️ THE CLIENT VITE FLOOR MOVES ON A SAMPLER-ONLY MILESTONE, AND IT IS PREDICTED ON PURPOSE: 192 → 193.** The client renders **nothing** from this milestone, but it still **compiles** `mounts.ts` — a new `core` module is +1 to any package importing `message.svelte`. **An unpredicted client move on a sampler-only milestone reads exactly like scope leak**, so it is written down before the drive rather than explained after it. Sampler **169 → 171** (+`mounts.ts`, +the registering stub). **`cargo test` 1546/0/62 across 56 terminator lines MUST NOT MOVE — zero `.rs`; any movement at all is scope leak and stops the leg.** Client registry **134 quiescent** — the fixtures are sampler-only and **in the real client the container renders nothing until something feeds it** (N-091/D-065).

**🔑 THE VERIFICATION THE MILESTONE EXISTS FOR IS V-4, AND IT IS ONE LINE:** `bodyExtras` renders **on a GROUPED continuation row**. That position — below the body, **outside** `{#if !grouped}` — is the entire reason J-552 chose this socket over perforating grouping. **If V-4 fails, `bodyExtras` was the wrong socket and Joe hears that before anything else ships.** V-5 (drop-unknown) is **positively controlled per N-139** — the same probe must return the two KNOWN mounts, *or the absence of the third means nothing.*

**FENCE HELD, and one clause narrowed honestly:** *fixture assets locally bundled, never remote URLs* (D-111) is carried into the runbook **as an inheritance note, not a live constraint** — **this milestone ships no assets at all**, every fixture mount is a text stub. *A constraint that binds nothing should say that it binds nothing.* No `ReactionDescriptor`, no wire shape, no store, no federation, no attribution; **M-RP-REACTIONS not reopened** (Joe's deferral), named only to fix the container's purpose.

**TO MS DESIGN (§7):** the strip sits below the body and **renders where there is no header line above it**; it has **TWO future tenants** — the D3 send-status indicator (three states: sent · unresolved · not sent) and reactions (N per row, animated, well above ~16px, runtime add/remove). *Design for the second and the first is free.* Structural class `.msg-body-extras`; `.fixture-widget` styling is a stub, **not a proposal**. **Owed unchanged:** ConnStats row-swap + all Leg C/D appearance.

## Entry J-553 — M-RP6.3 Leg D1 CLOSED: the undrained send stops lying — and the leg's best two acts were an implementer refusing to build a wrong runbook and a test proven able to fail before it was trusted

**What shipped.** Commit `53dab37`, **two files, +241/−11** — `xgen-client/src/desktop.rs` and `xgen-client/src/resident.rs`, scope confirmed by `git show --stat`. **Zero `ui/**`, zero `xgen-core`, zero node, zero sampler.** Clair implemented from the locked runbook; Chat re-drove the gates independently. **`cargo test` 1546/0/62 across 56 terminator lines — the handback reproduces exactly, the third consecutive two-seat leg on this arc that does.** Runbook `tasks/M_RP6_3_LEG_D1_SEND_PATH_HONESTY.md` **v1.2, Status: COMPLETED**, §8 close written.

**The defect closed.** `send_message` never checked link state and `outbound_rx.recv()` is polled **only inside `run_session`'s `select!`**, so an outage left the queue undrained: **the promise never resolved**, and on reconnect the drain wrote the message **minutes later, unannounced** — the silent queue D6 forbids, shipped since Leg B and unreachable only because no composer existed to hit it. Now: **`await_send_outcome`** bounds the wait and returns **`failed`, never `timed_out`** (*failed = never reached the wire, which is exactly true*), and **the drain skips a request whose `reply` oneshot is closed and logs it** — without that half, bounding the wait would have created the MIRROR violation, telling the user *not sent* and then sending it.

**🔑 THE RUNBOOK WAS WRONG AND THE IMPLEMENTER CAUGHT IT BEFORE WRITING A LINE.** v1.0 §3.1 instructed `await_send_outcome(reply_rx, SEND_ACK_TIMEOUT)`. Grounded against the drain, that constant makes `timed_out` **unreachable by construction**: `pending` is stamped at **write** time (`resident.rs:446`) and the sweep resolves at *write* + `SEND_ACK_TIMEOUT` + up to one tick, while the caller's wait starts **strictly earlier than the write** — so the outer bound expires first **always, for every δ > 0**, and a send that genuinely reached the wire would have been reported *never reached the wire*. ***The mirror-lie §3.2 exists to prevent, re-introduced by §3.1's own call site.*** **Third runbook on this arc caught by the implementer reading it whole first (J-499, J-548, this), and the SECOND that was Chat's error.** *The class is stable: internally consistent section by section, contradictory ACROSS sections — §3.1 said bound the wait, §4.1 said prove `timed_out` passes through, both correct alone.* **And the warning about exactly that shape was three paragraphs above the instruction that violated it.**

**The fix: DERIVE, don't choose.** Clair proposed a named `SEND_QUEUE_TIMEOUT` at 13 s; **Joe locked it derived instead** — `PENDING_SWEEP_INTERVAL` names the bare literal at `resident.rs:334` (same value, same behaviour, and the literal is now **gone from the sweep**, not shadowed by a copy), and `SEND_QUEUE_TIMEOUT = SEND_ACK_TIMEOUT + PENDING_SWEEP_INTERVAL + 5` = **16 s**. Two reasons, both worth keeping: a hand-picked `13` **goes silently wrong the day someone tunes `SEND_ACK_TIMEOUT` up**; and **no constant is provably correct at all**, because δ — the delay before the drain pops this request — is bounded by nothing (the channel holds 64). **Only the DIRECTION of the error is decidable:** too large costs an outage seconds, **too small relabels an ambiguous send as a definite failure.**

**🔑 U4 WAS MUTATION-TESTED, NOT ASSUMED — the strongest single act in the handback.** Clair set `SEND_QUEUE_TIMEOUT = SEND_ACK_TIMEOUT` (**the v1.0 instruction**) and U4 failed with *"SEND_QUEUE_TIMEOUT (10s) must exceed the drain's worst case (11s)"*; reverted, re-confirmed green. ***A test that has never failed is not yet known to be able to.*** U4 exists precisely because v1.0's defect was **invisible to every other test in the file** — U1 proves `timed_out` passes the seam and says nothing about whether the call site can produce one — and it was **proven capable of catching that exact defect** rather than trusted to.

**⚠️ V-L MEASURED 19 155 ms, NOT ~16 s — AND WAS DECOMPOSED RATHER THAN ROUNDED.** From the client log: **t0 10:58:18.818 → re-anchor fails 10:58:21.961 (+3.143 s, connection refused) → bounded wait 16.013 s.** **So the bound is measured accurate to 13 ms**, and the control corroborates the model (its 1142 ms contains a 1.13 s *successful* re-anchor). ***A number that disagrees with the runbook and is then EXPLAINED is worth more than one that agrees.*** → filed to COMPOSER §9.11.8: **outage latency is `re-anchor + SEND_QUEUE_TIMEOUT`**, carried into Leg D2 so nobody later reads ~19 s as a bug in the bound.

**§3.2 proven end-to-end, against a positive control.** `resident: dropping abandoned outbound (caller timed out)` at 11:02:44, then the node's **persisted store**: control present (1), abandoned absent (0), resident READY for minutes after. **The same grep returned 1 for the control — which is what makes the 0 mean anything.** Correct instrument, too: proving absence from the store rather than from `bob`'s client, since a second identity would have proven **fan-out**, not **non-writing**.

**⚠️ → N-139 — THE v1.0 PROBE WOULD HAVE RECORDED A FALSE "NOT RUN" ON A WORKING PATH.** `window.__TAURI__` → `"undefined"` (no `withGlobalTauri` in this build); `__TAURI_INTERNALS__.invoke` → `"function"`. **The failure mode was honest-looking:** the runbook named a leg that could silently not-run, told the driver to check first, and told them to record the absence rather than fake it — and a driver following it exactly would have produced *"V-L NOT RUN"*, **accurate, checkable, and completely misleading**, skipping the leg's most important verification **with a paper trail explaining why that was correct.** Same family as the hidden-element confident zero (J-548) and the empty `data-debug-id` array (N-110). **Rule: a probe that gates a verification must itself be positively controlled** — *an instrument that has only ever returned false has not been shown to work*, which is the U4 argument wearing different clothes.

**⚠️ CHAT'S FIRST GATE RUN WAS INCONCLUSIVE, NOT A PASS — N-117 LIVE.** `cargo test` returned **exit 101, ZERO terminator lines, `0/0/0`** (*failed to remove `…debug\xgen-client.exe`, Access is denied*). **Recorded because `0/0/0` reads exactly like a clean run to anything that parses totals** — quoted as a result it would have been a floor of zero. **And the holder was NOT Clair's leftovers:** `xgen-client` PID 40432 / `xgen-node` PID 19580, both started **14:02**, ~3 h AFTER her 11:02 drive. Stopped, re-run, clean.

**Deviations (Rule 6), all accepted:** §3.2's predicate test is a **PROXY and named as one** (N-092a) — it proves the signal the drain branches on, not the drain's `continue`, so **V-L step 5 is that half's only end-to-end evidence** · **U1 widened** to loop `Accepted`/`TimedOut`/`Rejected` because **`Rejected` carries a `code` the others do not and "verbatim" is a claim about all four fields** — the runbook under-specified it · absence proven from the node's store, per above.

**Also corrected: THREE stale comments, not one** (`desktop.rs:59`, `desktop.rs:347`, `resident.rs:691`). The third claimed the reply is *"always resolved exactly once"* — **§3.2 makes that NEWLY false**, not merely stale, which is exactly when a comment must travel in the same commit as the code.

**🟢 NEXT-ACTIVE = M-RP6.9 — `bodyExtras`: the per-row message container (`core`, fixture-driven)**, then **Leg D2 — R6 composer + echo store (`$common`)**, then **Leg D3 — send-status widget**. **NEW FLOORS: `cargo test` 1546/0/62 across 56 terminator lines · `npm test` 114 · vite 192 client / 169 sampler · sampler catalogue 386 · client registry 134 quiescent.** **Sampler 386 was NOT re-measured and is grounded BY SCOPE** (zero `ui/**` in the diff, J-497 precedent) — named rather than quoted. **No new D. No new `core`.** **OWED unchanged:** ConnStats row-swap + all Leg C/D appearance → Ms Design. **Test env left changed:** `LegBSpace`/`general` gained one control message (`D1-CONTROL-nodeup`); both apps stopped; CDP probe globals cleared by reload (N-123). Records: runbook **v1.2 COMPLETED** · `tasks/M_RP6_3_COMPOSER.md` **v1.9** · `ui/docs/xgen-ui-notes.md` **v1.1** (N-139) · ROADMAP **v5.19**.

## Entry J-552 — M-RP6.3 Leg D Phase-0 LOCKED: the first Phase-0 on this arc that did NOT come back shell-only — a silent queue is already shipped, C-4 needs amending, and a user question about emoji retired the recommendation I had just made

**What happened.** Design + records only, **no code, nothing built.** Leg D's grounding questions were driven against HEAD before any runbook. **Unlike C2's Phase-0, the answers did not come back shell-only:** Leg D touches `.rs` AND `core`, and one milestone is inserted ahead of it at Joe's call. Deliverable: `tasks/M_RP6_3_COMPOSER.md` **v1.8 §9.11** (five locked decisions D-1–D-5, twelve user-facing locks, one amendment-in-place to C-4, three new filings). Gates untouched. **Joe pushes.**

**🔑 TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE SESSION BRIEF, BOTH MATERIAL.** The four-way `SendOutcome` is `accepted` · **`rejected`** · `timed_out` · `failed` (`resident.rs:706`) — the brief listed *in-flight* as the fourth. **In-flight is not an outcome; it is the state before one exists**, and `rejected` is a real one carrying a wire `code`: a message that will never arrive however long the user waits, which is a different thing to tell them than *timed out*. And **`event_id` arrives WITH the outcome, not before it** — `send_message` awaits the correlated reply and resolves once, so at the moment the user presses Enter the frontend does not know the id. **The brief's "pending-sends store keyed by `event_id`" is not constructible.** Keyed by a client-minted local id instead, with the real id stitched on at outcome.

**🔑 C-4 IS AMENDED, AND THE BRIEF'S PROPOSED ESCAPE DOES NOT EXIST.** The node excludes the author from fan-out **by IDENTITY, not by connection** (`fanout.rs:305`, `EV-D2`, in terms). With C-4 projecting only `ingest` on read, a send round-trips, returns `accepted`, and **the stream does not change** — the user's own words render nowhere. The brief proposed an echo *"dropped when the real event arrives — a mirror with a defined death."* **The real event never arrives.** There is no server-sent fact to reconcile a user's own messages against, ever. **LOCKED: C-4 governs inbound unchanged; outbound is a NAMED exception** — a session-mortal, never-federated echo store in `$common`. *The awkwardness becomes a documented property instead of a leak.*

**⚠️ THE SILENT QUEUE D6 FORBIDS IS ALREADY SHIPPED, AND ONLY A COMPOSER MAKES IT REACHABLE.** `send_message` never checks link state — it `try_send`s onto the outbound channel and awaits the reply; and `io.outbound_rx.recv()` is polled **only inside `run_session`'s `select!`**. Between sessions **nothing drains that queue.** So a send during an outage: the promise **never resolves**, the message sits queued, and when the link returns the drain writes it **minutes later, unannounced.** `SEND_ACK_TIMEOUT` (10 s) does not save it — that sweep ages only sends already WRITTEN; a queued-but-never-written send **has no timer at all.** ***Nobody was careless: Leg B is scrupulous about D6 everywhere it writes (`"Never written → say so"`), and this is the seam between two correct pieces.*** **LOCKED (D1): bound the wait, and on expiry return `failed`, NOT `timed_out`** — `failed` means *never reached the wire*, which is exactly true; `timed_out` would claim the node may hold it, **the D6 lie inverted**. A frontend lifecycle guard blocks the common case, *but the guard is the nicety and the timeout is the guarantee* (§0 G-4). **Rejected: failing the whole queue on teardown** — tidier, but it destroys a message the user may still want offered under D6's explicit *"send when reconnected"*. **Consequence: C2's zero-Rust shape does NOT repeat.**

**🔑 A USER QUESTION ABOUT EMOJI RETIRED THE RECOMMENDATION I HAD JUST MADE — AND THIS IS THE ENTRY'S BEST MOMENT.** `details` is live (not reserved-unfed): `message.svelte:71` resolves mounts against a consumer registry and drops unknown ids, so a status widget needs **zero `core`** to mount. **But grouped continuation rows suppress the whole header line — name AND `details`.** Three sends in a row ⇒ rows 2 and 3 cannot show send-status, so **a `failed` third message looks exactly like the delivered first one** — D6's mirror broken by a `core` render rule, in the most common send pattern there is. *Locks #6 and #9 were in direct tension and neither I nor the brief had noticed.* I recommended **perforating grouping so `details` survives**. Then Joe asked: *what if I want to add an emoji to one of the grouped messages?* **Grounding that answered the send-status question instead.** `bodyExtras` sits BELOW the body, **outside** the `{#if !grouped}` block — **grouping-immune by position** — and `types.ts:69` has named it for *attachments / reactions* all along. So a reaction on a continuation row was never a problem; **and my recommendation was wrong.** Suppression is **correct**: repeating the author's name and time on every row of a run is precisely what grouping exists to remove. ***Punching a hole in a right rule to admit one tenant is the wrong repair — the tenant was in the wrong socket.*** **LOCKED: send-status moves to `bodyExtras`, and the socket gets BUILT** (declared but never rendered, so it is a `core` change — but *building a socket that was always designed*, not perforating a rule that was always right). `types.ts:67–69` is corrected with it: *send-status led* leaves the `details` list, because that line was written before a composer existed, **when nobody had asked whether send-status is header chrome or per-row state.** It is per-row state — the same category as a reaction, not the same category as an author name.

**⚠️ NO PROVISIONAL-TIMESTAMP FIELD, and the reason is not cost.** Marking `timestamp` provisional is a `core` change — but **`SendOutcome` carries no timestamp**, so even on `accepted` there is nothing to correct the time TO. *A provisional marker that can never resolve is worse than none.* Provenance rides the status widget. **Filed:** a user's own rows keep a client-minted time for the session and **may order differently for them than for everyone else in the room** — real, permanent within a session, not Leg D's to fix.

**🔑 JOE INSERTS A MILESTONE, AND THE ARGUMENT IS HIS.** Rather than build `bodyExtras` around a single static led, build it **fixture-driven first** — the R5 precedent exactly (M-RP5.6 built the stream on fixtures; Leg C wrapped it live four milestones later). ***A socket designed against a single static led will hold a single static led.*** Reactions are the far richer consumer — N mounts per row, runtime add/remove, interactive, on continuation rows — so **design against the strong consumer and send-status is trivially a second tenant.** And this is the cheap moment: one message component, one stream, one registry. **What the build teaches that a walk cannot:** `cid()` behaviour under **N mounts × M rows**. The client registry has sat at **134 quiescent** through C2 and every verify leg keys off it; three mounts on twenty rows is sixty new ids **or sixty collisions**, and which is not known. *Answer it on a fixture bench, not during a composer drive where it would look like the composer's fault.* → **M-RP6.9 — `bodyExtras`: the per-row message container.**

**⚠️ THE FENCE ON M-RP6.9, BINDING.** The container renders `WidgetMount[]` and **never learns what a tag or a reaction IS** — sampler passes fixture mounts, a future arc passes real ones, and **the component does not change between those two events.** *That is what makes it a container to complete rather than a stub to replace.* **Fixtures live in the SAMPLER only; in the real client the container renders NOTHING until something feeds it** — a client rendering invented tags is fake data on screen (N-091 / D-065). Fixture assets are **locally bundled, never remote URLs**, so not even a fixture establishes the precedent **D-111** forbids. **No `ReactionDescriptor`, no wire shape, no protocol, no attribution:** *a data shape invented before the protocol exists is a shape the protocol then has to satisfy* — and **who reacted is identity data, on the no-anonymity core, Joe's.**

**⚠️ #11b — MULTI-DEVICE, NAMED AND NOT SOLVED.** Author exclusion is by identity while fan-out delivers to **every connection** of each recipient — so other people's messages reach all of their devices **and the user's own reach none of theirs.** Type on the laptop and **the sentence does not exist on the phone**; not *until reload* — at all. **Joe: *"this awaits us from day one, and I keep it in mind the whole time."*** **The encouraging half: the node DID persist the event.** Fan-out is a live-delivery optimisation, **not the record** — so the hole closes at **M-RP6.4**, not Leg D. **Binding constraint written now while it is free: backfill reads the EVENT STORE and must return the requesting identity's OWN events.** *If backfill were ever built by replaying fan-out, the hole would silently persist.*

**🟢 NEXT-ACTIVE = M-RP6.3 Leg D1 — send-path honesty (Rust).** First because it is a **live D6 violation** and depends on nothing else here. Then **M-RP6.9 — `bodyExtras` container (`core`, fixture-driven)** · **Leg D2 — R6 composer + echo store (`$common`)** · **Leg D3 — send-status widget (`$common`)**. **Floors: `cargo test` 1541/0/62** (**D1 moves it by design**) **· `npm test` 114 · vite 192 client / 169 sampler · sampler catalogue 386 · client registry 134 quiescent.** **Filed:** M-RP-REACTIONS (blob-backed custom reactions — custom sets, animated, above 16px, not unicode; **discussion deliberately deferred to the real interface**, no design record) · no authoritative timestamp on `accepted` · the M-RP6.4 event-store constraint. **No new D, no new N.** **OWED unchanged:** ConnStats row-swap + **all Leg C/D appearance** → Ms Design, who should know `bodyExtras` is a socket two future arcs will also mount into. Records: `tasks/M_RP6_3_COMPOSER.md` **v1.8** · ROADMAP **v5.18**.
