## Entry J-551 — the filed one-field wire fix lands — and it was three readers, not one, because the "harmless" fallback stopped type-checking; which surfaced that NO frontend gate on this project can see a type error at all

**What happened.** The `IngestEvent.event_type` → `type` fix filed at J-550 §8.5 and carried in COMPOSER §9.9 was driven as a **Chat micro-change** ahead of Leg D Phase-0 (Joe's call on the seat; the seat division reserves code to Clair, and this was taken as the named exception, recorded here so it is visible rather than silent). **Three files, code + comments only. Zero `.rs`, zero `core`.** Floors held exactly: `npm test` **114** · client `vite build` **192** · sampler **169**. `cargo test` was **not** re-run and this entry says so — the change is confined to `ui/common/**`, and the DIRECT evidence for "no Rust changed" is the diff, not a test count.

**🔑 THE KICKOFF'S "NOTHING BREAKS" WAS WRONG, AND THE GREP IS WHY IT WAS CAUGHT.** The brief said `wireType()` reads `type` first with an `event_type` fallback, *"so nothing breaks; the fallback simply stops being load-bearing."* `grep -r "event_type" ui/` returned **three files, seven hits** — and the second reader was `return (e as IngestEvent & { type?: string }).type ?? e.event_type;`. After the rename, `e.event_type` is a property **that no longer exists on `IngestEvent`**. It does not stop being load-bearing; **it stops type-checking.** *A one-field fix that was scoped from a description rather than from the code would have been committed broken — and, per the finding below, would have passed every gate.* Fixed by re-casting once: `const w = e as { type?: string; event_type?: string }; return w.type ?? w.event_type;`

**⚠️ AND THE FINDING THAT OUTLIVES THE FIX — → N-138. NO `ui/**` PACKAGE RUNS A TYPECHECK.** `client` and `node` expose `dev` / `build` / `preview`; `sampler` adds `test`. **No `svelte-check`, no `tsc`, nowhere.** vite strips types through esbuild without checking them and vitest does the same, so **`npm test` 114 and `vite build` 192 / 169 cannot fail on a type error.** The three floors this arc quotes in every handback are honest about runtime and the module graph and **silent about exactly the class of defect a rename produces.** *Citing them as evidence that a typed change is correct is the N-108 error in a new costume — an underived claim riding on a number that really was measured.* For this change the direct evidence is the grep plus the read of each reader; the floors only corroborate. → filed **M-RP-TYPECHECK — admit a typecheck to the frontend gate set**, unscoped, Joe's. **Not smuggled in here:** first run will almost certainly surface a backlog, and finding that mid-leg is the wrong moment.

**Why this cannot have changed runtime behaviour, stated rather than assumed.** TypeScript types erase at build; the single executable line has identical semantics before and after (`.type ?? .event_type` either way). So **no live re-drive was performed, and none is claimed** — the argument is erasure plus the diff, not a CDP run I did not do. The gates were still run, because "cannot break" and "did not break" are two statements and only one of them is free.

**`wireType()` and its fallback are KEPT** — one thing at a time, per the brief. Two further reasons the brief did not name: the fallback's unit test is part of the **114** floor, so deleting it would move a gate inside a fix that is supposed to move nothing; and its test title (*"falls back … if a future interface fix renames it"*) had become a statement about a future that has now happened — retitled to name it as a **legacy** read. Two comment blocks describing the drift as live were rewritten for the same reason: **a comment asserting a defect that has been fixed is a false record** (D-065), and the next reader has no way to tell it is stale.

**The declaration now carries a do-not-revert note.** `wire.rs:476` is `#[serde(rename = "type")] pub event_type: EventType` — the Rust field is `event_type` **only because `type` is a Rust keyword**. Without that note the next person to compare the two files will "correct" the frontend straight back. **This fix is frontend-only by construction; the Rust name cannot change.**

**⚠️ A TRAP NO GREP CAN REACH, CARRIED INTO LEG D:** synthetic `ingest.push` payloads live in **CDP eval strings**, not in the repo. Every future drive must push `type`. The fallback covers a stale `event_type` push, which is a second reason it stays — *but a drive that passes only through the fallback is testing the wrong path*, and should be read as a defect in the drive.

**Records:** `ui/docs/xgen-ui-notes.md` **v1.0** (N-138) · `tasks/M_RP6_3_COMPOSER.md` **v1.7** (§9.9 row closed + M-RP-TYPECHECK filed). **ROADMAP not touched and deliberately so:** no milestone changed state — a filed one-field fix discharging is not a navigation event, and bumping the map for it would make the map noisier, not truer.

**🟢 NEXT-ACTIVE unchanged = M-RP6.3 Leg D — R6 composer + send path**, now at **Phase-0 grounding**, three questions against HEAD before any runbook: (1) your own sends render nowhere today — the node excludes the author from fan-out and `stream-panel` projects only `ingest`, so a local echo is required and **C-4 may need amending**; (2) what R6 actually wraps, and whether Leg D can be zero-`core`; (3) what of Leg B's four-way `SendOutcome` — `timed_out` especially — actually crosses the Tauri boundary today. **Floors for Leg D unchanged: `cargo test` 1541/0/62 · `npm test` 114 · vite 192 client / 169 sampler · sampler catalogue 386 · client registry 134 quiescent.**

## Entry J-550 — M-RP6.3 Leg C2 CLOSED: R5 is live in the real client — and the re-drive upgraded a synthetic leg to a measured one, corrected a floor, and disproved a filed observation

**What happened.** Leg C2 (`stream-panel` widget + live projection, shell) built by Clair from the locked runbook and **re-driven end-to-end by Chat (Rule 5) — all thirteen legs, on its own instance, against real client 9222 and a live node.** Feat `38ee185`, code-only, **6 files**, +558/−0. **Scope proven by `git show --stat`: zero `.rs`, zero `core`, zero `ui/sampler/**`, zero `skin.css`, zero `layout-default.ts`.** *Chat did NOT re-run `cargo test`, and says so: for the claim “no Rust changed” the `--stat` read is the DIRECT evidence and an identical test count would only corroborate it — stated that way round rather than quoting a gate Chat never measured.* **R5 is now a real region widget, fed live.**

**🔑 THE HANDBACK'S HEADLINE FINDING IS REAL, AND CHAT CONFIRMED IT TWICE OVER.** `wire.rs` carries `#[serde(rename = "type")] pub event_type: EventType` — the **Rust field** is `event_type`, the **wire name** is `type`, and Leg B's `IngestEvent` declares **the Rust name**. Leg B only ever read counts, so the drift was latent — **C2 is the first reader of that field**, and keying the allowlist on `event_type` would have matched nothing, producing an empty stream that reads as a dead projection. ***The phantom-defect family a third time on this arc.*** She read the grounded name via `wireType()` (with a fallback so a later correction cannot break it) and did **not** edit the shared store, which was out of §1 scope. **Filed: fix `IngestEvent.event_type` → `type` at the source.**

**🔑 THE RE-DRIVE UPGRADED V7 FROM SYNTHETIC TO MEASURED — AND THAT IS THE ENTIRE POINT OF THE SEAT.** The handback's leg table showed V7 (C-3) as satisfied; its own deviation list then said V7/V8/V13 used **synthetic `ingest.push`**. Both true, but only together — **the summary line outranked the deviation line**, and C-3 was the one binding the runbook called out in capitals. Chat drove the real thing: a second room was created, `bob` **left and rejoined the ROOM** → live `membership.leave` + `join` with **`room_id` length 83**, rendered as centred notices; then `bob` **left and rejoined the SPACE** → `received: 4`, two carrying **`room_id === ""`** and two carrying a real id, with **`projectedCount: 2`** and the rendered rows unchanged. **The Space-level pair is correctly excluded by the room filter — measured on the live wire, not reasoned from `state_key.rs`.** ***Zero was correct at J-546 and J-547; here it is correct for a reason that was SEEN.*** The verb was confirmed from `join --help` (`--room` omitted ⇒ joins the Space itself), never fabricated — the runbook asked, and the answer is on the record.

**V11 — THE REAL OUTAGE, DRIVEN THROUGH THE PRODUCTION PATH.** The node was killed abruptly (the detectable class; a *freeze* produces no transition at all, §0 G-4 amended). The episode published through the shell `$effect` → `gaps.apply` seam — **not** an injected setter — and ran `dialling` → `counting-down` → `resolved`, `resolvedAfterMs: 71183`, `statusRowCount: 1`, **one DOM node throughout**. **Proven by ELEMENT IDENTITY on Chat's own independently-stamped probe:** `probeSurvived: true` across every transition, `nodeCount: 1`, no duplicate left behind. *A rendered-text check passes either way, which is exactly why the runbook forbade it.* Clair measured `resolvedAfterMs: 103218` and Chat 71183 — **different numbers and both correct**: each measures its own outage. *A number that SHOULD differ between seats is not a failure to reproduce, and conflating those two is its own error.*

**⚠️ ONE GATE DID NOT REPRODUCE, AND IT MATTERS FORWARD.** The handback said client `vite build` **191**; Chat measured **192**, twice. HEAD differs from the feat commit only by a **CSS-rules-only** skin commit (11 insertions, no `@import`, no `url()`), which cannot move a module graph — *so the feat commit also builds 192, and that last step is REASONED from the diff, not separately measured* (N-108). **C2 added +8 modules to the 184 floor, not +7. The floor for Leg D is 192.** A floor quoted one low reads as a phantom regression at the next leg — the cheapest possible bug to prevent and the most annoying to chase. `npm test` **114** and sampler **169** reproduced exactly.

**⚠️ AND ONE FILED OBSERVATION DOES NOT SURVIVE BEING DRIVEN.** The handback filed that *fold→unfold resets the room latch to “select a room”*. **Chat folded and unfolded the tile and the latch SURVIVED** — `latchedRoomId` unchanged, `projectedCount` still 2. **Why:** the latch `$effect` re-runs on mount and reads `selection.current`, which still holds the room, so it re-latches immediately; the reset happens only if the bus no longer holds a room at remount time. **The issue is real but strictly narrower than filed** — and the correction earns its keep, because the broad version would have justified work that is not needed. **A useful invariant fell out of disproving it:** the latch effect writes only when `kind === 'room'`, so **the latch cannot change unless the BUS changed.**

**What else reproduced.** **V1 134** twice, each after a full reload with the quiescent state stated (N-112/N-132) · **V2** tile titled **“Messages”**, `placeholderIds: []`, `plugin-list` row present — **one descriptor, three readers, zero register lines** (F-1) · **V3** — **the leg C1 could not drive** — fill against a **region leaf** at two tile sizes with a real splitter moved between reads: body 419→403 and 298→282, **`fillDelta` constant 16**, `docScrollable:false` both; *the CONSTANT is the proof, not either absolute* · **V4** no-room `streamCount:1`, empty-room `streamCount:2` — **the measurement trap confirmed live: `core`'s `count` reads 2 on an empty room** · **V5** a real send painted, `isOwn:false`, initials-only author (C-8), head marker `kind:'system'` with `author:null` · **V6** filtered-not-dropped **and** the switch-half · **V8** copy flipped with `probeSurvived:true` on Chat's own stamp — the marker **mutated in place**, `__head__` never changed · **V9** one **synchronous** expression, before/mid/after all **0** — *synchronous by construction, so it cannot have straddled `GRACE_MS`* · **V10** 0 inside grace → exactly 1 after · **V12** the widget genuinely unmounted (`panelMounted:false`, out of the registry) and **the episode survived with its id and `resolvedAfterMs` intact** — the single cleanest justification for C-10 moving the store out of the widget · **V13** driven against a **control**: `groupedCount 1` → **0** with an episode timestamped between two real same-author messages. *A 0 means something only because the 1 was established first.*

Per the invariant above, **whatever moved the latch moved the SELECTION BUS** — which narrows the search to a bus writer rather than the widget. → **M-RP6.8 — view-latch persistence across remount + the unattributed bus move.**

## Entry J-549 — M-RP6.3 Leg C2 Phase-0 LOCKED: three questions grounded before the runbook, all three came back shell-only — and the one that would have cost a `core` change was answered by a type that shipped five milestones ago

**What happened.** Design + records only, **no code, nothing built.** The three C2 grounding questions were driven against HEAD before the runbook was authored, because a `core`-shaped answer to any of them changes the milestone's shape — and **finding that out after the runbook is written is the expensive order** (the M-RP6.2 / N-116 lesson, paid twice on this arc). **All three came back shell-only. There is no C1b.** Deliverables: `tasks/M_RP6_3_LEG_C2_STREAM_PANEL.md` **v1.0 ACTIVE** (the locked runbook for Clair) + `tasks/M_RP6_3_COMPOSER.md` **v1.5 §9.10** (three new locks C-9/C-10/C-11 + two amendments-in-place + one correction). Gates untouched — `cargo test` 1541/0/62 · vite 184 client / 169 sampler · npm 93 · sampler catalogue 386. Records ready; **Joe pushes.**

**🔑 Q1 — THE HEAD MARKER NEEDED NO NEW ROW KIND, AND THE ANSWER WAS ALREADY IN THE TYPE.** C-6's marker is neither a message nor a divider, and *“the view begins at session start”* is not one of C1's four status phases — so the obvious reading was a fifth phase or a fourth `StreamRow` kind, **both `core`, both forbidden to C2**. Grounded instead against `data-dependent/types.ts`: `MessageKind = 'text' | 'system'`, and `system` is an **authorless centred notice** with optional `author`, optional `body` and a free `id`. §9.3 **already** routes `membership.*` through that render. So the marker is a synthetic `MessageDescriptor{kind:'system'}` the widget prepends — **zero `core`, on a path that shipped at M-RP5.5 and has been verified since.** *The cheapest answer to a `core`-shaped question was a type nobody had re-read.*

**⚠️ AND IT BREAKS `core`'s EMPTY STATE — FOUND BY READING THE BRANCH, NOT BY RUNNING IT.** `showEmpty = count === 0 && !backgroundDeclared`. A **permanently present** marker makes `count ≥ 1` forever, so *“No messages yet”* **can never fire again from this widget**. Left undiscovered, a quiet room would have shown the marker alone — ambiguous, and reading like something still loading. **C-5 amended in place: both empty states are now widget-composed**, one level up from where C1 put them; the truths and the distinct-copy requirement (N-091) are unchanged, only who renders them moved. **A second consequence is a measurement trap and is written into the runbook as binding:** G's `count` is no longer the message count — a latched empty room reads **`count: 2`**, not `0`. *The J-548 hidden-element family in a new costume: not a confident zero this time, but a number that is right about the wrong quantity.*

**🔑 Q2 — EPISODE IDENTITY HAS NO SOURCE, CONFIRMED BY GREP RATHER THAN BY THE SHAPE OF THE STORE.** `ResidentStatus` is exactly `{attempt, max_attempts, next_attempt_in_ms, terminal, connect_timeout_ms, ping_interval_ms}` — **no episode id, no gap start time, no outage duration**, and the lifecycle state arrives on a *separate* channel. C1's V6 depends on an `id` stable across a phase transition and `resolvedAfterMs` is retrospective, so **C2 mints both client-side** (C-10).

**⚠️ THE STORE-VS-WIDGET CALL, AND WHY IT AMENDS A LOCK RATHER THAN QUIETLY DEVIATING FROM ONE.** C-7 put the grace timer *in the widget*. A widget-local tracker **loses every outage row when the tile is folded, the layout changes, or the plugin is toggled** — and **restarts the grace timer on remount**, so a still-live outage blinks out and returns two seconds later. A second mount (M-RP-SETTINGS' `surface:'window'` arc) would give two views of one connection **two disagreeing stories**. Moved to a `$common` store; **C-7's binding half — not `core`, not Rust, nothing added to `resident.rs` — is untouched.** Taken to Joe as an amendment, not absorbed as a mechanism call, because it edits a locked decision. ***Hiding a panel must never delete a fact.*** **The single-writer rule is carried forward from J-548 explicitly:** ONE function ingests an observation, the reactive effect calls it and the DEV hook exposes **that same function** — no setter that injects a finished episode, because *a verify seam that skips the mechanism verifies the wrong thing*.

**🔑 Q3 — F-6 WAS WRONG ABOUT HEAD, AND THE CORRECTION MADE THE LEG SAFER.** J-547 recorded that *“R5's shipped `onSelect` moves the bus to a MESSAGE”*. **It does not.** `message-stream.svelte` sets its own `$bindable selected` and calls `onSelect?.(mid)` — an explicitly **reserved** hook that never writes the selection bus; the consumer decides. So C2 simply **does not wire it**, and the N-136 self-invalidating read-modify-write is **not merely avoided — it is unreachable**, since nothing this widget does moves the bus off a room. **A stronger finding fell out of the same read: a message selection is not expressible on the bus at all** — `EntityDescriptor.kind` is `'identity' | 'space' | 'room'`, there is no message kind. Wiring R5 to the bus is a `core` union change, **filed, not built**. *A grounding pass that corrects a finding from the previous grounding pass is the D-071 discipline working, not a defect in it.*

**C-11 — A USER QUESTION BECAME A LOCK, ONE LEG OVER FROM WHERE IT WAS ASKED.** Joe asked whether affected rows should carry a *“not delivered yet”* note. Grounded: **C2 has no outbound rows** — every projected row is inbound and therefore delivered by definition, and the node **excludes the author from fan-out** (`fanout.rs:301`), so your own sends never ingest. The indicator has a home already: `MessageDescriptor.details` is the reserved socket whose own comment names *send-status led*, and Leg B ships the four-way `SendOutcome` behind it. **Filed to Leg D, not smuggled into C2.** But inverted from outbound to inbound the question lands on something real and cheap: **messages other people sent DURING a gap are gone, and nothing will fill the hole.** So a resolved row meaning only *connection restored · 8s* is **true and incomplete**. **LOCKED: the resolved row asserts “the record is discontinuous here”, not “we're fine now”** — the head marker's own D6 rule (*the stream may never look complete when it isn't*) applied to the middle of the stream instead of the top, at zero cost since `resolvedAfterMs` already ships. Wording and appearance remain Ms Design's.

**Written into the C2 runbook as legs that can silently not-run** — the J-548 discipline applied forward, before the leg is driven: **V11** (a real outage maturing in place) passes trivially on rendered text, so it must be proven by **element identity**; **V9** (the grace discard) passes trivially if the two writer calls sit in **separate** evals, because the PowerShell round-trip may exceed `GRACE_MS` and prove a timeout instead of a discard — **it must be one synchronous expression**; **V3** (region fill) passes trivially against a fixed-size tile, so the splitter must move between reads; and **V5** is not proven by your own send. **The C-3 binding is restated at the top of the verify section: drive a ROOM-level `membership.join`, and confirm the verb from `--help` rather than fabricating a command line.**

**No new D, no new `core`, no new N.** Three new C-locks, two amendments-in-place (C-5, C-7), one corrected finding (F-6). **OWED unchanged:** the M-RP6.6 ConnStats row-swap and **all Leg C/D appearance** → Ms Design.

**What happened.** Design + records only, **no code**, nothing built. Joe granted **full autonomy on this leg except visual appearance (Ms Design) and fundamental architecture**; every decision below is Chat's under that grant. Gates untouched — `cargo test` 1541/0/62 · vite 184 · npm 77 · sampler 328. Code + records ready; **Joe pushes.**

**🔑 THE FINDING THAT CHANGED A DECISION — AND IT WAS ABOUT TO BE A PHANTOM DEFECT.** The projection design called for a room-scoped filter on `ingest`, and the obvious allowlist put `membership.join` in the stream as a system row. Rather than reason from the shape of the wire type, the two-level question was **grounded**: `state_key.rs:252–253` builds a **Space** join with `room_id = ""` and a **Room** join with a real `room_id`; `derive.rs:1026–1030` emits the pair. **So a Space-level join is correctly EXCLUDED by a room filter** — and **Clair's very first live ingest at Leg B was a `membership.join`**. The event class most likely to be driven first at verify is the one the filter legitimately drops. Left ungrounded, C2's verify would have driven a Space join, seen an empty stream, and written *"the projection is dead"* into a record. ***This is the J-546 fan-out-excludes-the-author trap in a second costume: zero was correct there too.*** Written into §9.3 as a binding instruction to whoever verifies C2 — **drive a ROOM-level join.**

**The six findings (§9.1).** **F-1** there is no R5 widget and **the register path has moved** — `stream → RegionPlaceholder`; the current mechanism is a `CLIENT_PLUGINS` descriptor that `layout-default` **derives** the registry from, and no `app_client` register line exists any more. **F-2** `message-stream` is **boxed at `max-height: 340px`** in its own scoped `<style>` — a fixture-bench constraint; a region leaf must fill and self-scroll (J-499 D5). **F-3** `const now = new Date()` is captured **once at mount**, so divider labels freeze for the life of the process — invisible on a fixture mounted for thirty seconds, wrong on a resident that runs for days. **F-4** `StreamRow` is a **closed union**; the live mutable item is a third kind. **F-5** the ingest store is **flat and unscoped** — `INGEST_CAP = 500` global across every room with a global `dropped`, so a busy Room B evicts Room A. **F-6** R5 inherits **R2's latch problem one level deeper**: `rooms-panel` latches the last *space* because its own click moves the bus to a room; R5's shipped `onSelect` moves the bus to a *message*, so R5 needs a **room latch** on the identical D3 shape — nothing else holds “the active room”.

**⚠️ WHY THE LEG SPLIT — F-2, F-3 and F-4 ARE ALL `core`.** Three `core` edits inside a shell milestone is exactly what made the M-RP6.1k registry delta unreadable (the `dialog` footer, correctly filed-not-built). So **C1** = `core` region fitness + the row *shape*, verified in the **sampler** where catalogue 328 is the readable signal; **C2** = the widget + projection + live feed, touching **zero** `core`, verified in the real client. ***A registry delta that mixes a `core` change with a shell change cannot be attributed to either.*** **C2's runbook is deliberately NOT authored yet** — its anchors are whatever C1 ships, and this arc has already paid twice for a runbook written against a generation-stale anchor (M-RP6.2, N-116).

**🔑 C-6 — THERE IS NO BACKFILL, AND REFUSING TO HIDE THAT IS THE DESIGN.** Switching rooms shows only what arrived over the resident **this session**; there is no history load anywhere in the client. **An empty room and a not-yet-loaded room render identically** — a message-loss illusion in the D6 family (*a stream may never look complete when it is not*). ## Entry J-546 — M-RP6.3 Leg B CLOSED: the message plane ships, verified two-seat — and Clair found a Leg-A defect that Leg A's own verification was structurally incapable of catching

**What happened.** Leg B (outbound multiplexer + ack correlation + live ingest) closed. Chat built it single-seat and ran V1–V3; **the arc returned to the Chat–Clair split for verification**, and Clair ran V4–V6 against the pushed code-only feat. She passed all three — and, in the course of it, measured a defect in **Leg A**, already closed and pushed at J-545. That defect is fixed here. **Gates: `cargo test` 1541/0/62** (Leg-B floor 1539 + the 2 new regression tests) · vite **184** · npm **77** · sampler **328**. Code + records ready; **Joe pushes.**

### The defect — and why it is the more important half of this entry

**`attempt` is documented “0 while live” and was not.** `run_resident` reset the published counter only via `outcome.reached_ready()`, which runs **after a healthy session ENDS**. Nothing zeroed it when READY was *reached*, so a resident that reconnected on attempt 8 published **`8/10` for the entire healthy session that followed**. Clair measured `attempt:8` stable with `state:READY` and traffic flowing.

**⚠️ The real finding is not the bug — it is that Leg A's verification COULD NOT have found it.** J-545's V1 read `attempt:0` on a **freshly connected** client. A fresh connect reads `0` whether or not the reset rule exists: it cannot distinguish *“correctly zeroed on ready”* from *“never incremented yet”*. **The discriminator is RECONNECT-then-READY, and Leg A never drove it.** Chat tested the trivial case and recorded the contract as proven.

***This is the N-099 family a third time, and — sharper — it is the SAME shape as the bug M-RP6.6 shipped (N-137): there, a unit test asserted the mapping and never the emission; here, a live check asserted a value and never the transition that value is a claim about.*** A field is not verified by reading it in the state where every implementation agrees.

**Fix:** the reset rule is extracted as a named, unit-testable `ResidentStatus::on_lifecycle(&state)` — reaching `Ready` zeroes `attempt` and clears the countdown — and `run_resident` wraps the sink so **every** lifecycle transition passes through it. Extraction is the point: the rule existed only as an implicit consequence of loop placement, which is why nothing could test it. `run_session` is untouched (the spine stays UI-agnostic); `terminal` is deliberately NOT touched (it is owned by the cap/park path, and clearing it here would silently un-park a resident that never resumed — asserted by its own test).

**Two regression tests, both driving the case Leg A missed:** `reaching_ready_zeroes_the_counter_mid_session` sets `attempt:8` + an armed countdown, walks `Reconnecting`/`Connecting`/`Authenticating` (counter must HOLD — a retry in progress still counts), then `Ready` (counter and countdown must clear); `ready_does_not_disturb_the_terminal_flag`.

**Live-verified on the exact broken case (Chat, real client 9222 + real node):** fresh connect `attempt:0` (recorded as **non-discriminating**, which is the whole lesson) → node killed → `attempt:4`, `CONNECTING` → node returned → **`READY` with `attempt:0`, `next_attempt_in_ms:null`, traffic flowing**, stable across a 12 s re-read. Before the fix this read `4`.

### Leg B — what shipped

**Rust (`resident.rs`, `desktop.rs`, `service.rs`; ZERO `xgen-core`).** The drain is the single reader **and** the writer: `Connection` cannot be split (`ws` is private; an accessor would edit GPL core, M-RP6.6 D3), so instead of a writer task the `select!` gained an outbound arm. Send enqueues and returns; the drain builds → signs → writes and correlates `event_id → oneshot` without stalling inbound (D3). Correlation reuses `TransportMessage::event_id()` and the shipped `EventConfirm` rather than minting a parallel outcome type (D-067). A 1 s sweep resolves entries past `SEND_ACK_TIMEOUT` (10 s) as `timed_out`; session teardown resolves every survivor to `failed` **with a stated reason** — dropping the map would surface as a bare `RecvError` and an in-flight message must resolve to a *reason*, not to silence.

**`SendOutcome` is a four-way status, never a boolean:** `accepted` · `rejected` (+ wire `code`) · `timed_out` · `failed`. **Collapsing `timed_out` into either success or failure is exactly the lie D6 forbids** — the node may be holding the event.

**🔑 B-5 — the finding that reshaped the leg (Joe-locked option 2).** A message needs `prev_events`, and every `ops::*` write verb gets them from `batch::get_dag_tips` — which **owns the drain**, so it is D2-forbidden on the resident socket. There was therefore **no way to construct a sendable event over the resident socket at all**. Resolution: **`TipTracker`**, a resident-held DAG frontier updated from live ingest *and* from our own sends. *`get_dag_tips` exists because a short-lived control-mode connection has no memory — a resident does.* Anchors are invalidated at **every session start** (a reconnect is exactly when a frontier silently goes stale, so the invalidation is automatic rather than remembered by a caller) and re-seeded **once per session per Space** from a control-plane `get_dag_tips` on its **own short-lived connection** — D2-legal, never per message. *Honest limit, recorded not hidden: across a gap the tips are stale; a stale anchor is not corruption, it yields an event that reads as concurrent, which resolution already settles, and `ops::send` has always tolerated an imperfect anchor via its root fallback.*

**Live ingest closes the M-RP6.6 deferral:** every inbound `Event` → `app.emit("xgen-event")` → the new `$common` `ingest.svelte.ts` store, carried **verbatim** (no projection — turning an Event into a `MessageDescriptor` is R5's job at Leg C, and doing it here would put the projection in a second place before the first exists). Capped at `INGEST_CAP` with a reported `dropped`, so the UI can never imply it is showing everything when it is not.

### ⚠️ The Leg-B finding that nearly entered the record as a defect

`ingest.received` sat at **0** through every send Chat made — including from a separate CLI connection. The obvious read was *“the seam is dead.”* Grounding `xgen-node/src/fanout.rs:301` showed the opposite: **`if rid == author_id`** skips the sender, and the node's own test is named `message_fans_out_to_other_members_and_excludes_author`. **Zero was CORRECT behaviour** — the resident authored every message and was never an eligible recipient. It took a second registered member to feed it. *The seam looked dead and was fine; the answer came from the node's source, not from a plausible story.*

### Verification — attribution stated per leg (this matters, see below)

| leg | claim | seat |
|---|---|---|
| **V1** accepted round-trip | real Space/Room → `accepted`, real `event_id`, conn stays READY | **two-seat** — Chat, then Clair on her own inputs (every V5b/V6 send) |
| **V2** frontier anchoring | control-plane `get_dag_tips` → `tip_count=1` **= msg1's event_id**; msg2 chained onto it | **Chat, single-seat** |
| **V3** live ingest | node fan-out → drain → `xgen-event` → store, verbatim | **two-seat, independently re-driven** — Chat *“hello from Bob”* @ received=3; Clair *“sanity from bob”* @ 0→1, sustained to **44**, `dropped:0` |
| **V4** in-flight failure on drop | ✅ PASS | **Clair** |
| **V5** drain non-stall under load | ✅ PASS | **Clair** |
| **V6** re-anchor connection hygiene | ✅ PASS | **Clair** |

**🔑 V2 IS DELIBERATELY NOT MARKED TWO-SEAT, AND THE REASON IS A STANDING RULE.** Clair's V6 first-sends all re-anchored and all came back `accepted` — which re-confirms the re-anchor **path fires and produces a sendable anchor**, but **NOT** that the anchor was **the frontier**. A root-anchored event is equally valid and equally `accepted`; the node takes both. **An `accepted` outcome proves the anchor was VALID, never that it was OPTIMAL — chaining is observable only in the tips, never in the send result.** Recorded so nobody later reads a wall of green accepts as proof the frontier is being tracked. *(Clair raised this herself rather than letting the tick blur — the flag is hers.)*

**Clair's V4 method (accepted as designed, and better than the obvious one).** Loopback acks in ~1 ms, so kill-during-a-burst almost never catches a send genuinely in `pending`; she **refused to approximate**. Instead: `NtSuspendProcess` (self-tested on a throwaway counter *before* being depended on) freezes the node — its kernel socket keeps accepting small writes, so sends land in `pending` with no ack possible, for as long as chosen. **Arm A (positive control):** suspend → fire 2 → `{a1:null,a2:null,READY}` → resume → both `accepted`, window **1854 ms** (inside the 10 s sweep ⇒ real acks). **Arm B:** suspend → fire 3 → all outstanding → kill from frozen → all three `failed`, reason **“connection ended before the node confirmed”** (the **teardown drain**, not the write-fail arm), every reason non-null, none `accepted`/`timed_out`; first-send→kill **1542 ms ≪ 10 000** so the sweep is excluded; not-wedged proven by a **live `attempt` climbing 1→2→3** rather than a status read that could succeed against a stalled drain. ***An arm that proves the window is real before the other arm claims a failure is the leg J-501 was missing.***

**Clair's V5 disambiguation — the part worth keeping.** A first 40-send burst showed an apparent inbound plateau; she did **not** accept it at face value. The burst's own acks flowed (0→21→40) *while writes were outstanding* — a drain blocked on writes cannot read acks — and the acks were themselves delayed, so the bottleneck was the **node**, not the drain. Cause: a burst on an un-anchored Space fires up to 40 concurrent re-anchor connections, saturating the debug node. Clean re-run (anchored, sustained trickle): `received` climbs **26→34** throughout while the resident fires every tick, 19/19 accepted. **Recorded plainly: V5 passed under a sustained trickle, NOT under the 40-send burst** — that burst was confounded, and once the herd is bounded a genuinely heavy load test would be cleaner. *Better the record says that than implies we proved something we did not.*

**V6:** counting **Established** only (TIME_WAIT accumulation is normal teardown, and she said which state she counted). 20 concurrent first-sends → EST max 4 **during**, settled 1; **4 reconnect cycles** (the condition that actually re-exercises the path, since anchors invalidate per session) → settled EST=1 every time. No growth with send count or across sessions. D2 confirmed **against the code**: `get_dag_tips` runs only on `reanchor_space`'s own connection; the drain uses only `send_event`/`recv`.

### Rule-6 findings — flagged, and one of them corrects a LOCKED note

1. **⚠️ §0 G-4 IS IMPRECISE — corrected by measurement, not argument.** G-4 reads as though `PING_INTERVAL` bounds dead-peer detection generally. **It does not.** There is **no pong timeout** (`resident.rs` sets `pending_ping` and never acts on a missing pong), so against a peer whose kernel still ACKs TCP (a suspended process — or a frozen/paused host) the ping **write keeps succeeding** and the resident stays **READY indefinitely**. Clair measured **27 s across 2+ ping intervals**, with `bytes_out` growing at the ~10 s and ~20 s marks — the pings were written and succeeded. **Detection fires only where the WRITE fails or `recv()` errors** (an abrupt kill/RST). Phase-0 §0 G-4 amended in place with the measurement attached.
2. **Latent: the concurrent-first-send re-anchor herd.** N concurrent `send_message` on an un-anchored Space → up to N concurrent control connections (the V5 saturation). All close (V6 — no leak), but it is a thundering herd. **Not fixed:** Leg D's composer sends one at a time, so it is not hit in practice. Filed.
3. **Chat's own gate hygiene:** `cargo test` returned **`0/0/0`** twice — once on the N-117 exe lock (a leftover `cargo-tauri` from Clair's session), once as a genuine compile error. *A gate that did not execute is not a gate that passed*; both discarded, re-run clean.

### ✅ In-place corrections to ALREADY-PUSHED records (J-545)

J-545 and its PLAY block state *“V5 the re-arm — resume → `true` → real auth → READY, `attempt` 0”* and describe `attempt` as *“0 while live”*. **The observation was real; the claim it supported was not tested.** Both records are corrected in place to say the reading was taken on a path that could not discriminate, and to point here for the fix. *A record that was true-as-measured but stronger-than-earned gets corrected, not quietly left standing.*

**§6 DoD — Leg B boxes discharged:** non-blocking drain under load ✅ · ack correlation live ✅ · live ingest wired (the M-RP6.6 deferral closes) ✅ · D2 invariant verified against the code ✅ · `cargo` off the floor ✅ · CDP-verified on real client 9222 + live node ✅. **No message ever rendered as delivered when it was not.**

**No new D** (D1–D6 realisations; B-5 is a D2-compliant mechanism, Joe-locked by-recomm). **No new `core`.** **OWED, unchanged:** M-RP6.6 ConnStats row-swap (Ms Design) · all Leg C/D appearance (Ms Design). **🟢 NEXT-ACTIVE = M-RP6.3 Leg C — R5 stream wrap + the live mutable item class** (it reads `ingest` and the Leg-A status surface; **the terminal item must NOT be drawn as permanent** — any `focus` resumes a parked resident, J-545). → `tasks/M_RP6_3_COMPOSER.md` v1.2 · ROADMAP v5.13.

## Entry J-545 — M-RP6.3 Leg A (resident status publication) CLOSED: the retry is bounded, the counter and countdown are published, the terminal state parks and re-arms — and one live state change could not be attributed, so the verb now names its caller

**What happened.** Leg A of M-RP6.3 built, live-verified on real client 9222 against a real node. Single-seat (Chat technical lane, under the J-544 autonomy grant). The three facts the resident already knew but kept private — **how many attempts have been spent, when the next dial happens, and whether it has given up** — now leave `run_resident` on a published surface. **Gates: `cargo test` 1530/0/62** (floor 1524 + exactly the 6 new Leg-A tests — the honest signal Rust landed) · `vite build` **183** · `npm test` **77** · sampler catalogue **328** untouched. Code + records ready; **Joe pushes.**

**D-071 re-ground first (N-116).** The Phase-0 was written at `aa3cc3e`; HEAD was `92dcb2c` (J-544, doc-only). `resident.rs` re-read in full against HEAD: **all six §0 findings hold, nothing had moved** — no cap, `Backoff{attempt}` private and getter-less, `next_delay()` computed and slept inside the loop, the sink still a bare enum, `PING_INTERVAL`/`CONNECT_TIMEOUT` both 10 s. *The record was checked against the code before anything was built on it, which is the only reason that sentence is worth anything.*

### Shipped

**Rust (`resident.rs` + `desktop.rs`).** `RECONNECT_MAX_ATTEMPTS = 10` — grounded, not picked: the real schedule `1·2·4·8·16·30·30·30·30·30` = **181 s of sleeping**, plus up to 10 × `CONNECT_TIMEOUT` ⇒ ≈6 min worst case. Long enough to ride out a node restart, short enough that a closed-lid laptop parks instead of dialling all night — and it is what makes `(2/10)` expressible, since **before this constant there was no denominator**. `Backoff` gains `attempt()` + `exhausted(max)` (pure, clock-free, unit-tested). `ResidentStatus` = shared Arc'd atomics, **the `TrafficCounters` shape deliberately re-used rather than a mechanism invented** (D-067); `get_resident_status` mirrors `get_conn_stats` and rides the **same 2 s poll** — no second push channel. The resume channel is a `watch::Sender<u64>` generation counter, **the sibling of the shipped `PipeShutdown`**, so the parked resident `select!`s on it exactly as it already does on shutdown — one loop, one owner of `Reconnecting`, no second task.

**Frontend.** `selfState.resident` carries the snapshot **verbatim snake_case, no mapping layer** (the `ConnTraffic` precedent). The `[Reconnect]` verb ships as command `resident.reconnect`; auto-resume triggers are `focus` + `online` **in the webview, deliberately** — Rust-side link detection would mean a new dependency and a per-platform surface where the WebView gives both events for free.

### Two design points that are load-bearing, not stylistic

**① `next_attempt_in_ms` is REMAINING time, not an absolute deadline.** `Instant` is not serialisable and a Rust↔JS epoch bridge buys clock skew for nothing. Internally it *is* stored as an absolute deadline, so a slow or missed poll can never publish a stale remainder; the UI interpolates locally between polls, which is legitimate because the value is a deadline — it cannot change without a state change the next poll catches.

**② The countdown is CLEARED the moment the sleep ends.** §0 G-4 says each dial can take up to `CONNECT_TIMEOUT`; a countdown left armed through that window would sit at zero and read as **frozen**. `None` is precisely what tells Leg C to hand off to `connecting…` — and the handoff was **caught live**: a read at T+6 s returned `next_attempt_in_ms: 113` with the lifecycle already at `CONNECTING`.

### ⚠️ A defect caught in Chat's own edit, before it ever ran

`ResidentStatus` was first written with `#[derive(Default)]`. That seeds `next_attempt_at_ms` to **`0` — a real epoch-ms value in 1970** — so `snapshot()` would have computed `saturating_sub` → **`Some(0)` and published a PHANTOM COUNTDOWN from the moment the app booted**, on a connected client with no retry in progress. Replaced with a hand-written `Default` seeding the sentinel, and a test (`resident_status_defaults_to_no_countdown_not_zero`) exists specifically to fail if anyone re-derives it. *This is the absent-not-zero rule (D4/N-060) biting in a new place: `TrafficCounters` needed a hand-written `Default` for `RTT_NONE` for the identical reason, and the second occurrence of a rule is the one that proves it is a rule.* **"The countdown reads zero" and "there is no countdown" are different facts and must never collapse into the same `0`.**

### Live verification (real client 9222 + real node, Rule 5 — every leg re-driven by Chat)

- **V1 baseline, quiescent + connected:** `attempt:0 · max_attempts:10 · next_attempt_in_ms:null · terminal:false · connect_timeout_ms:10000 · ping_interval_ms:10000`, lifecycle READY. The sentinel holds (the ① defect would have shown here as `Some(0)`), and the three constants arrive **as data** — D5 proven on the wire, not asserted.
- **V2 the guard:** `resume_resident` on a LIVE resident returned **`false`**. A focus storm cannot reset a live backoff — proven against the real Rust guard.
- **V3 the numbers, live:** node killed → T+6 s `attempt 2/10`, countdown **113 ms**, state `CONNECTING` (**the G-4 handoff caught mid-act**); T+16 s `attempt 4/10`, countdown **6238 ms** — consistent with the 8 s step 1.8 s in. *Both of these were literally inexpressible before this leg (§0 G-1/G-2).*
- **V4 the cap:** `attempt 10/10 · terminal:true · next_attempt_in_ms:null`, lifecycle DISCONNECTED. **And the stronger proof: the node was brought BACK while parked and the client did NOT reconnect** — so the cap genuinely stops the resident rather than merely flagging it. *That is exactly why D4 requires both halves; a cap without auto-resume would be a dead app.*
- **V5 the re-arm:** resume → **`true`** (terminal this time), schedule reset, real auth handshake, **READY**; `attempt` back to `0`, `terminal:false`, countdown absent, traffic counters live (`bytes_in 555 / bytes_out 513`, `rtt_ms:null` — absent-not-zero, no pong yet). **⚠️ CORRECTED IN PLACE (J-546): the `attempt` reading here was taken on a path that CANNOT DISCRIMINATE.** This resume followed a *terminal park*, whose exit resets the counter explicitly — so `0` appeared whether or not reaching READY resets it. The struct's *“0 while live”* contract was therefore NOT verified by this leg, and it was in fact BROKEN: after an ordinary reconnect the counter held its pre-reconnect value for the whole healthy session (Clair measured `attempt:8` at READY). Fixed at **J-546** (`ResidentStatus::on_lifecycle`) with a regression test that drives reconnect-then-READY. *The observation above was true as measured; the claim it was taken to support was not earned.*

### 🔑 THE FINDING — A STATE CHANGE THAT COULD NOT BE ATTRIBUTED, AND WHAT WAS DONE ABOUT IT

During the first park, the resident **left the terminal state on its own** — a later read showed `attempt:1, terminal:false`. The log confirmed exactly one cap-reach and exactly one resume, ~2 min apart, coinciding with CDP polling. The obvious story was *"the harness focused the window"* — and **that story is false**: counting listeners installed via CDP recorded **`focus:0, online:0`** across two further attach cycles. So the harness was not the trigger, and **the cause remains unknown.**

The available move was to write a plausible cause into the record. **That is exactly the N-118 / N-124 shape this arc has already been burned by twice** — a diagnosis written down as "measured" when it was inferred. Instead the hole itself was closed: `resume_resident` now takes a **`source`** and logs it, and the three callers pass `focus` / `online` / `command` (plus `dev-bridge`). Re-driven end-to-end, the log now reads **`resident: resume accepted source=dev-bridge`**. *The original event stays unexplained and is recorded as unexplained — but it can never recur unexplained.* **An unattributable user-visible state change is a debugging hole, and the fix for not knowing is instrumentation, not a guess.**

**⚠️ A consequence Joe should see, stated plainly:** because any `focus` resumes a parked resident, a user who has the window in front of them will effectively retry indefinitely. That is arguably correct — someone looking at the app *should* get retries — but it means **`terminal` is durable only while the app is ignored**, which is the sleeping-laptop case D4 was written for and not a general "stop trying" guarantee. Recorded, not silently accepted.

- **N-117 fired:** the first post-change `cargo test` returned `0/0/0` — the dev client held the exe, so cargo never ran. Re-run with the apps stopped: **1530/0/62**. *A gate that did not execute is not a gate that passed;* the 0/0/0 was discarded, not reported.

The **verb** is live and real (`resident.reconnect`), awaiting its element in Leg C: the `layout.revert` precedent. *A built verb with no element yet is ABSENT, which is honest; what this project refuses is a painted element that does nothing (J-500 / 6.1j).*
- `run_session` is untouched, so `service.rs` (the headless `--service` caller of the same spine) needed **zero** changes — checked against the call sites, not assumed.
- The owed **`tasks/M_RP6_6_RESIDENT.md` v1.2** correction rides this commit as agreed at J-544 (§2 D3 "resident-level wrapper" → the stream-layer `CountingStream`; the "auth handshake excluded" caveat deleted — it is now false, the wrap happens before authenticate).

**No new D** (D4/D5 realisations, arc-local). **No new `core` component.** **OWED, unchanged:** the M-RP6.6 ConnStats row-swap (Ms Design) · all Leg C/D appearance (Ms Design). **🟢 NEXT-ACTIVE = M-RP6.3 Leg B — outbound multiplexer + `event_id → oneshot` ack correlation in the drain**, where live ingest (the M-RP6.6 deferral) wires in and the drain becomes the single reader. → `tasks/M_RP6_3_COMPOSER.md` (Leg A DoD boxes) · ROADMAP v5.12.

## Entry J-544 — M-RP6.3 (live messaging: R6 composer + narrow-B send path) OPENED: send path locked NARROW B, the three-plane invariant minted, and four security gaps surfaced by the unified socket filed as named successor arcs

**What happened.** M-RP6.3 opened (M-RP6.6 closed J-543). A design-only session in the Chat lane: the A-vs-B send-path question was walked from the **user's** point of view, B was chosen on that basis, then grounded against `main` — and grounding **narrowed** it. Four security/plane gaps surfaced in the same walk and are filed as arcs rather than absorbed. Doc-only; no code. Phase-0 `tasks/M_RP6_3_COMPOSER.md` (v1.0 ACTIVE). Six arc-local decisions D1–D6; no DECISIONS.md change.

**Autonomy grant (Joe, this session).** *"After we assert and agreed the form of socket, you have autonomy — except visual appearance."* Chat set its own boundary on top of that and recorded it: **visual appearance excluded** (Ms Design), **the auth-tier question excluded** (it sits on the no-anonymity core — Joe locks it), **wire-spec changes excluded**, **pushes excluded**. Arc creation, leg splits, milestone sequencing and invariant naming are Chat's under the grant. D1–D6 and the §4 sequence are **by-recomm under that grant**, not individually Joe-locked.

### The decision that was made before the grounding, and survived it

The send path was chosen **B (unify — outbound multiplexes over the resident's one socket)** on a user-experience argument, with the **non-blocking drain** as the constraint that makes B *strictly better* rather than a trade (it captures A's one real edge: inbound stays crisp under a jammed uplink). Chat's own additions to that case: under A, **most of M-RP6.6 would be decorative** — a client that only opens a socket to send has no sustained thing to be in a *state* about, so the led, the lifecycle, RECONNECTING and the traffic rows would all describe a fiction (a D-065 argument, not a performance one); plus **ordering** (one socket = one ordered stream; concurrent short-lived connections can race, and out-of-order chat reads as brokenness) and **offline send** (B + 6.6's backoff makes type-while-disconnected-flush-on-recovery *possible*). The honest half, recorded: **the user never experiences architecture until it fails** — B introduces a *silent* failure mode A did not have (a stuck queue or lost ack degrades everything at once, invisibly), which is why D6's *a message may never LOOK sent when it is not* is a binding rule and not a nicety.

### Grounding verdict (verified `main` @ `aa3cc3e`) — six findings; three shrank the milestone, one changed it

(1) **No retry cap exists** — `run_resident` loops forever; `Backoff{attempt}` is private, getter-less, saturating. A `(2/10)` counter is **not expressible today**. (2) **Next-attempt-time is not published** — the delay is computed and slept inside `run_resident`; a countdown is **not expressible today**. (3) **The lifecycle sink cannot carry either** — `FnMut(ClientLifecycleState)` is a bare enum, no payload; a second published surface is required, mirroring the shipped `TrafficCounters`/`get_conn_stats` shape (one pattern, not a new mechanism, D-067). (4) **The detection window is ~10 s twice over** — `PING_INTERVAL = 10s` (a silently-dead peer goes unnoticed that long) and `CONNECT_TIMEOUT = 10s` (each retry dial can take that long), so **the countdown must hand off to `connecting…`** or reaching zero followed by ten seconds of silence reads as frozen. (5) **⚠️ `send_event_confirmed` owns the connection and eats the drain** (`connection.rs:186`, discard at `:243` — `_ => continue`): under a unified socket, fan-out events are **swallowed while a send awaits its ack** — directly incompatible with live ingest. It is a **family**, not a method (`upload_blob:256`, `fetch_blob:323`, `batch.rs::get_dag_tips`), and the client-crate call-site sweep is **~114 hits**. → *"Move correlation into the drain" as a general rule is a crate-wide refactor, far past this milestone.* (6) **No auth tiers and no session lifetime** — `auth.rs` is nonce → Ed25519 → verify; `CHALLENGE_EXPIRY_SECS = 30` bounds the **challenge**, not the session. No expiry, no re-auth, no scopes, no roles anywhere in the transport auth layer; authentication is binary and permanent for the life of the socket. `ws://` only, no TLS.

### The narrowing — and the three questions that forced it

Joe raised three aspects of the unified socket **after** B was decided: streaming, bulk transfers, and security/auth tiers. **Each independently argued for narrowing B**, and together they settled it. **Streaming:** WebSocket has **no multiplexing** (unlike HTTP/2 or QUIC) — head-of-line blocking is *inherent* to one socket, not a bug to design away; `BLOB_CHUNK_BYTES` chunking is the mitigation, but only if the drain is fair, which loads the non-blocking-drain constraint with more work than it was originally given. **Bulk:** `upload_blob`/`fetch_blob` chunk **base64** (+33%) over the same WS *and* own the connection and drain — so on the resident socket a large upload would leave the client **blind to inbound fan-out for the entire transfer** (minutes), with no cancel, resume or progress. **Security:** B does not create the auth weakness but **extends its duration by orders of magnitude** — under A each short connection re-proves key possession and a stolen socket is worth seconds; under B one authentication holds for as long as the app runs. Plus: MLS protects message *content*, not metadata (who, when, how often, how much — and M-RP6.6's Leg C now literally counts those bytes), and M6's node-admin verbs on a shared socket would inherit **byte-identical** authentication to sending a chat message.

→ **D1 NARROW B (Joe-confirmed explicitly, the one call not taken under the autonomy grant): the resident socket is the control/message plane ONLY.** The `ops::*` verbs keep their own short-lived connections — already correct under **D-056** (control-mode, not resident). *B was decided for the user's messaging experience; that is the composer, not `create_space`.* Same user-facing win, and the blast radius stays off the ~114 call sites.

### Locked (D1–D6, arc-local)

- **D1 — NARROW B.** Message plane only; `ops::*` unchanged.
- **D2 — THREE PLANES, as a standing invariant.** control/message → the resident socket · bulk data → own connection per transfer · real-time media → out of scope, separate transport. **BINDING: the own-connection-and-drain family (`send_event_confirmed`, `upload_blob`, `fetch_blob`, `get_dag_tips`) may NEVER run on the resident socket.**
- **D3 — NON-BLOCKING DRAIN is a constraint, not a style.** Send queues and returns; the drain writes and correlates without stalling inbound. `ops::send` stays as a **software** fallback (multiplexer bug), **never a network** fallback.
- **D4 — BOUNDED RETRY + TERMINAL STATE + AUTO-RESUME.** Capped attempts (so the counter and a terminal state are expressible at all), terminal `disconnected — [Reconnect]` as a **real action, not a greyed spinner**, plus auto-resume on window-focus/network-return so the sleeping-laptop case still recovers. *Both halves are required: uncapped kills the counter, capped-without-resume kills the laptop case.*
- **D5 — SHAPE SETTABLE, DO NOT WIRE SETTABLE.** Named constants in one place; values travel to the UI as **published data**, never hardcoded a second time in Svelte; no behaviour keys on a specific number. **Explicit non-goal: no config-plumbing layer**, migration waits on **J-513**. *A named constant migrates in one line; a premature config layer charges now for a decision not yet made.* (Joe's framing: *"prediction in the code, that it has to count this possibility"* — shape it, don't wire it.)
- **D6 — FAIL-FAST DEFAULT, with an explicit queue offer.** **Block send, never block typing** (killing the textarea mid-thought is the worst response to a blip); a long outage **offers** "send when reconnected" as a user choice, never a silent queue. **BINDING: a message may never LOOK sent when it is not.** *Honest limit:* a half-open socket means the first send after a drop can fail **even with the guard in place** — blocking sends is a nicety, never a guarantee; per-message failure state is still required.

### Leg split

**A** resident status publication (Rust — cap, attempt count, next-attempt-time, terminal state, `[Reconnect]`, auto-resume) · **B** outbound multiplexer + `event_id → oneshot` ack correlation in the drain (Rust; **live ingest — the M-RP6.6 deferral — wires here**, since the drain becomes the single reader) · **C** R5 stream wrap + the **live mutable item class** R5 does not have today (a gap item that counts `reconnecting (2/10) · retrying in 6…`, hands off to `connecting…` across the dial window, and **collapses in place** to `connection restored · 8s` — *the live widget IS the historical marker, matured*; ~2 s grace so a recovered blip is never shown — *silence is the correct UI for a blip*) · **D** R6 composer (**a BUILD, not a wrap** — R6 does not exist).

**Two numbers were merged in discussion and separated in design:** *"restored · 8s"* is **retrospective** (how long the outage lasted, final on resolve) and *"8…7…6…"* is **prospective** (time to the next retry). Both ship, and the second is the better feature — it converts dead waiting into a visible schedule and makes the backoff legible — but it **requires the scheduler to publish `next_attempt_at`**, which it does not today (grounding finding 2).

### The gaps the unified socket surfaced — filed as arcs, not absorbed (Joe: *"we need to close gaps … certainly!"*)

**None blocks M-RP6.3 shipping.** The resident dials a local node today; what these block is **the resident talking to anything beyond loopback** — the gate is on **deployment, not on the milestone**, so the UI arc proceeds. Filed as §3 accepted risks with named successors: **R-1** no TLS (`ws://` only) · **R-2** no session lifetime (B extends the hijack window from seconds to days) · **R-3** no auth scopes/tiers (admin/user separation under D1 is mitigated **by convention, not by mechanism** — recorded honestly) · **R-4** metadata exposure (MLS covers content, not who/when/how-much) · **R-5** bulk transfers have no cancel/resume/progress and pay +33% base64.

**GATE: `wss://` is a hard prerequisite before the resident dials anything non-loopback** — stated as a gate, not a preference.

**Sequence (§4):** M-RP6.3 → **M-SEC-TLS** (`wss://` + certificate handling) → **M-SEC-AUTHSESS** (session lifetime, re-auth, auth scopes) → **M-BLOB-PLANE** (bulk transfer connections: cancel, resume, progress, binary framing). *TLS first because it is cheapest and unblocks the most; auth-session before the blob plane so the blob plane inherits a settled session model rather than being retrofitted twice.*

**⚠️ M-SEC-AUTHSESS is NOT a technical scoping call.** *"What is an identity authorized to do, and for how long"* sits directly on the **no-anonymity core** — it is **Joe's to lock**, may need spec/doc work before any code, and is flagged as possibly large enough to deserve its own grounding session before it is even scoped. Chat explicitly declined to lock it under the autonomy grant.

### Records + next

- **Canonical (D-074, one atomic commit):** this JOURNAL J-544 · `tasks/M_RP6_3_COMPOSER.md` (NEW, v1.0 ACTIVE) · CLAUDE.md PLAY head · `docs/ROADMAP.md` v5.10→v5.11 (M-RP6.3 🟡→🟢 + three new 🟡 arcs). No new D (D1–D6 arc-local), no `core`, no sampler, no Rust.
- **Owed / still open:** the M-RP6.6 **ConnStats row-swap** (Ms Design, unchanged) · `tasks/M_RP6_6_RESIDENT.md` **v1.2** (the §2 D3 text still says *"resident-level wrapper"*; the shipped code is the stream-layer `CountingStream`, and the *"auth handshake excluded"* caveat is now wrong — the wrap happens **before** authenticate, so auth bytes ARE counted; J-543 already recorded the revision, the task doc has not been amended) · **all appearance in Legs C and D → Ms Design** (§5 specifies *what states exist, what they mean, when they appear* — no colour, type, spacing, glyph or animation).
- **Next-active = M-RP6.3 Leg A.** **Entry (Rule 0): CLAUDE.md PLAY → JOURNAL J-544 → `tasks/M_RP6_3_COMPOSER.md`.** Not pushed — Joe pushes.

## Entry J-543 — M-RP6.6 — the client resident: live connection state + traffic accounting — CLOSED: the discard-the-stream scaffold becomes a real long-lived resident (live lifecycle · reconnect/backoff · byte+RTT accounting), all three legs live-verified on the real client 9222 + node

**Single-seat, technical lane (Joe, this session: "all technical stuff is yours; mine is visual").** Chat authored the build runbook, ruled the one open decision, wrote all the Rust + the frontend store facet, and drove every live verification on the real client (9222) against a real node — Legs A/B/C in one session. The one visual piece (the ConnStats row-swap) is left standing as a small **Ms Design** leg (§7); the milestone closes **code-complete with the two `connection-stats.svelte` rows still literally `'N/A'`** (Joe's call — a swap done outside the visual lane is how a provisional appearance decision gets made by accident). Code + records ready; **Joe pushes.**

**The gap this closed.** Since M1 the desktop shell's own doc-comment claimed the resident was *"wired in 2b/M3"* — **it never was.** `run_startup` did **one** 2 s `connect_async`, **threw the stream away**, `sleep(150ms)`, emitted `Ready`, and never touched the socket again. So the client's connection state was **relaunch-scoped**: stopping the node while the app ran changed nothing on screen. This is the live half of gate finding **F-1** (M-RP6.0), and the ROADMAP's *"stop the node → the led flips"* proof was **un-runnable** until now.

### §0 open decision — ruled Path A by Chat (technical-autonomy grant)

Phase-0 §1(3) had recorded the byte seam as *"outbound choke `send_bytes`; inbound `recv()`."* Re-grounded against `main` (N-116, cutting the other way): **neither is usable under D3 (GPL core `Connection` untouched)** — `send_bytes` is **private**, and `recv()` returns a **parsed `Inbound` enum**, so the frame length dies inside core; the resident cannot observe bytes at all without editing GPL core. Ruled **Path A**: a client-crate `CountingStream` interposed **below the WS handshake** (a stream-layer counter), which keeps GPL core untouched *and* delivers real bytes. D3's note revised: *"resident-level counters at the **stream** layer; core untouched; honest scope = all socket bytes this resident session, auth handshake included."*

### Shipped (7 files, all client crate + frontend — GPL core untouched, proven by diff)

- **Spine (D1) — new `xgen-client/src/resident.rs`:** `run_session` (connect → authenticate → drain) with a `SessionEnd` outcome and an injected `FnMut(ClientLifecycleState)` **lifecycle sink** — so the SAME spine drives the Tauri UI (sink = `emit_state`) and stays headless in `--service` (sink = `tracing`), not two forks (D-056). `service::run_ws_loop` was refactored onto it (the watch channel hoisted so the resident shares it) as the **regression-lock**: the extraction compiling clean with headless behaviour unchanged is the proof it's a pure move.
- **Leg A — real lifecycle:** the scaffold in `desktop.rs::run_startup` replaced by the resident. Node via `resolve_node` (hardcoded `ws://127.0.0.1:8080/xgen` gone), real `client_authenticate` (the `sleep(150ms)` gone), lifecycle from **actual** socket outcomes. `Degraded_*` left inert (no real source — N-091). Best-effort `goodbye` on the shutdown arm (races `app.exit`).
- **Leg B — reconnect + backoff:** `run_resident` wraps `run_session` in a retry loop; a pure, unit-tested `Backoff` (`1,2,4,8,16` s → 30 s cap; reset after a session that reached READY). `run_resident` is the **only** emitter of `Reconnecting`; the terminal `Disconnected` (Leg A) is superseded by retry.
- **Leg C — accounting (§0 Path A):** `CountingStream<S>` (a byte-tallying `AsyncRead`/`AsyncWrite` wrapper) + `connect_counted` (hand-dials TCP → wraps → `client_async` → `Connection::new`, ws:// Phase 1; wss:// a documented future concern) + resident-timed RTT (`ping()` on a 10 s interval, matched to `Inbound::Pong`, `want_ping`-flag pattern so ping never races the `recv()` borrow). `TrafficStats(TrafficCounters)` managed state + `get_conn_stats` command (mirrors `get_pacing_state`) → the frontend `selfState.traffic` slot (`ConnTraffic {bytes_in, bytes_out, rtt_ms}`, snake_case verbatim, absent-not-zero: `rtt_ms: null` before the first pong) + a 2 s poll in `app_client.svelte`. `connection-stats.svelte` **not touched** — the row-swap is Ms Design's (§7).

### The finding — a real bug caught only by driving the real app (→ N-137)

The first live drive (node up → READY → kill node) proved DETECTION worked (`recv error (os 10054)` → `session ended outcome=Disconnected` in the log) **but the UI stayed pinned at READY.** `run_session`'s drain-drop arms *returned* `Disconnected` without ever *emitting* `sink(Disconnected)`, while the connect/auth-fail arms did — a silent divergence. The unit test (`reached_ready`) asserted the outcome mapping, not the emission, so only the live drive surfaced it (N-099 family). Fixed by making the **caller** own the terminal state (Leg A emits `Disconnected`, Leg B emits `Reconnecting`) — one owner, no divergence, and the exact shape Leg B needed. **→ N-137** (*a return value is not a notification; returning and emitting are two acts*).

### Verify — real client 9222 + real node, Chat re-drove every leg (Rule 5, real-node session)

- **Leg A** — fresh session log: `CONNECTING → AUTHENTICATING → resident: authenticated (real XGID, connected_node=ws://127.0.0.1:8080/xgen) → READY` (real challenge-response timing, no 150 ms sleep). Clean single run: READY → node kill → `recv error (os 10054)` → `lifecycle_state="DISCONNECTED"` → CDP live state `DISCONNECTED`. Detection→emission ~1 ms once the RST arrived.
- **Leg B** — the reconnect loop's `RECONNECTING → CONNECTING` gaps walked the exact schedule against wall-clock (`1,2,4,8,16,30`-cap, measured); then **the same running process** (same log file, no restart) auto-reconnected the moment the node returned: `CONNECTING → AUTHENTICATING → authenticated → READY`. CDP live state `READY`.
- **Leg C** — `__XGEN_SELF__.traffic` = `{bytes_in:587, bytes_out:609, rtt_ms:0}` at READY, and **grew** across a ping interval to `{595, 633, 0}` (live-cumulative, not a snapshot). `rtt_ms:0` is a genuine sub-ms loopback measurement (not the `null` sentinel — the unit test proves `None` before the first pong). The client reached READY **through the counted stream** (`connect_counted` + auth succeeded live), so the interposer is proven end-to-end.

### Gates (measured, not predicted — N-105)

- `cargo test` **1524 / 0 / 62** — the floor **1519 + the 5 new resident unit tests** (`reached_ready`, 3× backoff, `counting_stream`), **exactly**; `ignored` unchanged at 62, `0 failed`, 56 result lines all `0 failed`, final line present (no N-117 truncation). This is the honest Rust-primary signal — `cargo check` clean is not (the count moving off 1519 is what goes in the record).
- `npm test` **77** (unchanged — no frontend/sampler tests added; the store facet is CDP-verified, the project's pattern). `vite build` clean (941 ms). Sampler catalogue **328 unchanged** (no `core`/sampler touched).

### Confirmed against the actual diff (Joe's close conditions)

- **D3 — GPL core `Connection` untouched:** the change set is **7 files, ZERO `xgen-core`** (`git status` clean of `xgen-core/`). `CountingStream`/`connect_counted` live in the client crate (`resident.rs`); the counter sits on the stream. Proven, not asserted.
- **D2 — live ingest stayed out:** the drain still discards inbound (`// Deferred: dispatch to R5 fan-out (own milestone)`); no fanout/dispatch wiring. R5 real-time ingest remains its own milestone (gated on R5 + M-RP6.3).

No new D (D1–D5 arc-local; the §0 ruling is Chat's technical call under the session grant, recorded as a D3 note revision). No new `core`, no sampler change.

### What shipped (D-B → D-120, B2)

New `$common/lib/stores/backdrop.svelte.ts` (one boolean `pattern`, default true) + new `$common/…/widgets/grid-plate-settings.svelte` (a `core` `Toggle` writing the store, id `grid-plate-settings__toggle`). `grid-plate` reads the store and **paints `data-pattern`** (B2 — no longer fully inert), G `{backgroundLive, pattern}`; `registry.ts` grid-plate row gains `settingsComponent`; `skin.css` `.grid-plate[data-pattern]`=raster / plain otherwise. `settings-dialog.svelte` **drill-in generalised** `detailId → drill={id, mode:'info'|'settings'}` (the J-539 reuse), `settings` **intercepted locally**, generic `{@const C}<C/>` mount — `app_client.handlePluginAction` and `plugin-list` **untouched**. `uistate.svelte.ts` gains a `backdrop` session key + `setSessionBackdrop` (N-107 per-key merge, zero Rust); `app_client` binds `backgroundLive={backdrop.pattern}`, seeds before `loadLayout`, persists via an **`untrack`ed** effect.

### The defect Clair shipped in `5f4a6fe` and caught in live verify → N-136

The backdrop persist `$effect` called `setSessionBackdrop()`, whose read-modify-write **read `_store.session` inside the effect** → it became a dependency → the write self-invalidated it → `effect_update_depth_exceeded` → Svelte halts the render scheduler: `$state` keeps mutating (getters advance, toggle animates natively) but the **DOM freezes**. Symptom = a *dead-button UI*, **not a crash** → it passed every static gate; **only a live drive surfaced it** (Joe caught it on screen). Fix (`8b7ca1a`) = `untrack` the write. **The other persist axes (`installed`/`disabled`/`locked`/`layout`) were safe because they persist from EVENT HANDLERS, not effects** — backdrop was the first persist wired through an effect. → **N-136** (Rule-5 / N-099 family: a failure only a live drive can see). *This is why the leg was not closed on the static gates alone.*

### Measured — Chat re-drove EVERY leg (live 9222, full reload first, N-132; zero errors)

| leg | result |
|---|---|

| persisted value at first frame | `region-shell` G `backgroundLive:true` + `grid-plate` G `pattern:true` + **painted `data-pattern="true"`** — the persisted choice paints on reload |
| mechanism (D-B) | gear → Settings `:modal true` @ Plugins; `[settings]` **ENABLED for grid-plate ONLY** (self-panel/inspector-panel/plugin-list `aria-disabled`) — descriptor-derived; click → drill `detail:{id:'grid-plate',mode:'settings'}`, header **“Grid Backdrop”**, Back present, `toggle#grid-plate-settings__toggle` registers, **99→76** (list unmounts, settings component swaps in) |
| B2 flip (the REAL toggle, N-097) | true→false: store + `grid-plate` G `pattern` + `region-shell` G `backgroundLive` + **painted `data-pattern` REMOVED** (raster→plain) + input unchecked + `session:false` persisted; false→true restores **`data-pattern="true"`**. **Two-way on the painted DOM** |
| untrack fix | reads return cleanly through the flip — no `effect_update_depth_exceeded`, DOM responsive (the N-136 fix proven) |

- **D-B — J-513 → B (component-per-plugin).** The J-513 gate (*how a plugin's settings get drawn*) was binding-deferred until the grid works. The grid works. **Resolved: B** — a plugin that has settings ships its own settings component; the modal hosts it (the shipped widget-tier pattern; `substitutions-editor` was its first instance). The declarative `settings_schema` auto-render (Ch6 §6.8.2/§6.8.5, **zero lines exist**) is not built and is superseded as a path (*"it does not need to be yet another widget system"*, Joe). A technical/mechanism choice; the look stays Joe's. *A formal `D`-number is Joe's to bless when Leg C builds it.*

Sections = app-level categories + a **Plugins** category (the `plugin-list` rows + the action row) + per-plugin settings in the content pane. The `gear` (`widget.manager`) opens Settings **on the Plugins section**; **File ▸ Settings** (new `settings.open` command + a new File item **above Restart** — grounded: File is `Restart · —— · Exit` today) opens it on the **default** section. `plugins-dialog.svelte` is **absorbed**. ## Entry J-531 — D-118 LOCKED: the plugin package (one zip + root manifest, universal for node + client); plus the node frame/grid postponed and the client's next exemplar set

**Architecture + naming convention. No code.** A design conversation this session settled how plugins are distributed and installed, and re-pointed the near-term work.

### D-118 — the package

Every out-of-tree plugin — either app, any delivery kind — ships as ONE `.zip` with a manifest at its root. `host` / `delivery` / `surface` / `kind` (D-112) become manifest FIELDS, not separate on-disk shapes — one uniform unit the plugin manager enumerates, trust-badges, installs, removes. The manifest is readable **without executing or unpacking-to-live** (enumerate + trust-badge + route-by-host from the manifest alone). **D-085 unchanged:** a zip is transport, never a load path — `service` spawns out-of-process, `packaged` runs in the no-key sandbox (gated on S-1…S-6, D-113/S-7), nothing is `dlopen`ed into the node; `compiled` stays baked in, so every zip in `plugins\` is `kind: custom` by construction. Two-tier location (`[app_root]` bundled read-only · `[userdata]` user-writable — the app-vs-user lock). Discovery ≠ loading: the manager can list `plugins\` before the sandbox floor exists.

**Naming:** `pg{c|n}_<plugin-id>_r<YYMMDD>.zip` — `pgc` client / `pgn` node (the host axis + routing hint); `r` = single-letter release channel (room for `d`/`b`); date a human label. **No ui-vs-system token** (Joe): system plugins are `compiled` + non-removable and never appear as loose packages, so the namespace is custom-only, and the host badge is already `pgc`/`pgn`. A filename is a label + routing hint, never a trust descriptor — everything trust-relevant lives in the manifest. D-117 stays reserved for the fold axis; this takes D-118.

### Direction re-point (records catching up to the conversation)

- **M-RP7.7 (node inherits the frame + grid) → POSTPONED** until the client UI is complete (Joe). Port a FINISHED frame+grid to the node in ONE pass, not twice — the client still has appearance (M-RP-SKIN), real region content, and Settings ahead of it. The node is “working enough to simulate traffic,” which is what makes the client's connection widget real later. **D1 (a)** + **D2** (File menu = Restart / Shut Down; **hide-to-tray IS the native window X**, no new menu item — the shipped `CloseRequested`→`hide()` intercept becomes reachable the moment D3 flips `decorations:true`) recorded as 7.7 design intent; **D3** (native resizable window, twin-config, N-088 fix, **no status-bar grip** — native frame resizes) and **D4** (retire `app_node.svelte` legacy chrome → placeholder centre) are node-UI, deferred with 7.7.
- **Client next = the two custom-widget exemplars, plate first**, then connection-stats, then the plugin manager (`M-RP-SETTINGS`). Order is architectural: a custom widget is the HARDER, more general case than any system widget (system = always-present, easy; custom = install → registry → layout-inject → uninstall → remove-without-blanking) — prove the lifecycle on one instance before scaling. **`M-RP-PLATE`** (grid-background, `surface:'none'`, inert, no data source) is the most self-contained exemplar and closes the containment/mount question; **connection-stats** (`surface:'region'`, `kind:'custom'`, the first traffic consumer, a natural node widget too) closes install→dock→uninstall. System widgets fill in as live data matures; sub-element widgets (temperature etc.) ride INSIDE their host regions (D-061, §6.2), never as standalone panels — which is why “build all system widgets” is not a clean unit.
- **The open ground the exemplars close:** the plugin ARCHITECTURE is locked (D-112 taxonomy, D-103 region model, D-113/S-7 sandbox sequencing), but the install/uninstall LIFECYCLE and the compiled-LOADING mechanism are explicitly open (D-112) — the registry today is a static TS array (`CLIENT_PLUGINS`) with no runtime install path. That gap is what the exemplars exist to close.
- **`plugins\{client,node}` folder split** agreed (matches the host axis; the node's is the stricter — out-of-process / no-key sandbox only, never its address space).

### Records

DECISIONS **D-118** · CLAUDE.md PLAY (NEXT-ACTIVE re-pointed to M-RP-PLATE; 7.7 postponed; D-118 filed) · ROADMAP (7.7 ⏸, plate promoted, D-118 ref). No code; nothing pushed by Chat (Joe pushes).

## Entry J-530 — M-RP-SHELF-FRAME CLOSED: fixed-height shelves — the empty strip holds its frame, and the grid stops reflowing

**Skin-only, 1 file (`ui/assets/skin.css`). Zero Rust · zero component · zero registry change · no schema change.** PROVISIONAL skin (Joe HMR-tunes). Chat authored + drove the CDP verify on the live client 9222 (Rule 5) — a skin edit under the running `tauri dev` session, HMR-applied and measured in place.

### The one sentence

A lock that only collapses an EMPTY shelf is not a frame — neutralising `.shelf[data-empty]` (was `min-height/padding/border → 0`) makes BOTH shelves hold the base `min-height: var(--ctl-h)` + the position hairline whether empty or full, so an empty favourites strip (or pinning into it) never shifts the centre grid.

### What shipped (Joe-locked)

Joe: both shelves fixed height, not collapsible, even when empty — a calmer grid frame. The base `.shelf` rule already gives a fixed frame (`min-height: var(--ctl-h)` + `padding: 0 var(--sp-2)` + a position hairline; top `border-bottom`, bottom `border-top`), and BOTH shelves already share it — so the “button shelf height” Joe asked to measure is not a special number, it is `--ctl-h` + hairline, and “match the button shelf” reduces to “stop collapsing the empty one.” One block removed; `data-empty` stays EMITTED (a skin hook, no JS reader — grepped) but no longer zeroes the box.

### Measured — live 9222, Chat drove (Rule 5)

| leg | before | after (HMR) |
|---|---|---|
| bottom (button) shelf | 28.8px, `data-empty:false` | 28.8px — unchanged |
| top (favourites) shelf | **0px** (collapsed, `data-empty:true`) | **28px**, `data-empty:true` (attr retained), `min-height:28px`, hairline 0.8px |

The collapse is gone: the top strip went 0 → 28px, so the grid no longer reflows between an empty and a populated favourites shelf.

### The sub-pixel finding (accepted, recorded so it is not “fixed” later)

Top 28 vs bottom 28.8 = **0.8px** (one device pixel). Cause: `.shelf` is `box-sizing:border-box` with `min-height: var(--ctl-h)` — the POPULATED bottom shelf's faces push its border-box 0.8px past the 28 min, while the EMPTY top sits exactly at min-height. It is not a collapse (both are fixed); it is a content-vs-min artifact of the border-box. Joe accepted it (the optical bar, N-128 — optically correct is satisfied); it is sub-pixel and DPR-safe (a pinned `28.8px` would freeze this display's scaling). The exact-equality alternative — `.shelf { height: var(--ctl-h) }` → both 28px, faces clamp harmlessly — is filed-not-taken. → N-130.

### Ripples

The node inherits it free at M-RP7.7 (shared skin → both apps get the identical fixed frame). No registry / catalogue / schema impact. No new D. Deviations: none.

### Records

The skin.css shelf docblock is corrected in place (the “`data-empty` collapses the strip … the 6.1j pre-pinning look” note → the fixed-frame note). ui-notes N-130 · ROADMAP · CLAUDE.md PLAY · task file COMPLETED. Feat: skin-only, 1 file — **not pushed (Joe pushes).**
